summary: The article discusses the increasing concentration in the Spanish banking sector, driven significantly by the 2008 financial crisis and the current economic impact of the coronavirus. It highlights how the number of banks and savings banks has drastically reduced through mergers, acquisitions, and absorptions, leading to a few large entities dominating the market. Experts suggest this trend will continue, with implications for employment, branch closures, and customer services, though opinions vary on the impact on competition.

title: Morgan Stanley Hires $265-Mln Asset Merrill Team in Florida
summary: Morgan Stanley has hired a four-person team from Merrill Lynch in Ponte Vedra Beach, Florida, managing $265 million in client assets. This move is part of Morgan Stanley's aggressive hiring efforts, contrasting with Merrill Lynch's continued freeze on experienced advisor recruitment. The article highlights the ongoing shift of advisors between major wealth management firms.

title: PNC opens first retail branch in Greater Boston
summary: PNC Bank has opened its first retail branch in Greater Boston, located at 55 Boylston St. in Chestnut Hill. This is the first of five planned locations for the Pittsburgh-based banking giant in the region for 2020, signaling an expansion into the Boston market.

title: Truist, BofA among banks with largest Orlando market share
summary: The article discusses how Truist and Bank of America hold the largest banking market shares in metro Orlando. The merger of BB&T and SunTrust was a key factor in establishing Truist as one of the largest banks in the market. The content highlights the competitive landscape of the banking sector in the Orlando area.

title: IRSA buscará reestructurar su deuda en dólares
summary: IRSA will present a proposal to its creditors to restructure its debt of US$181 million, which matures on November 15, adhering to BCRA regulations. This comes as the BCRA has called on companies with foreign currency debt exceeding US$1 million monthly to present restructuring plans. The proposal must include a maximum 40% access to the exchange market and a two-year extension for the remaining payments.

title: Goldman Sachs to go ahead with "modest" job cuts after coronavirus pause
summary: Goldman Sachs Group Inc plans to proceed with a "modest number of layoffs" after pausing job cuts due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The bank is reportedly looking to cut about 400 jobs, or roughly 1% of its workforce, primarily targeting back-office roles as part of an earlier reorganisation aimed at improving efficiency. This comes as the U.S. Federal Reserve curbed big bank capital distributions through the end of the year, affecting share buybacks and dividends for major banks.

title: Lithia Announces Pricing of Public Offering of Common Stock
summary: Lithia Motors, Inc. announced the pricing of its public offering of 3,181,819 shares of Class A common stock at $220.00 per share, with an option for underwriters to purchase additional shares. Concurrently, Lithia announced a private offering of $550 million aggregate principal amount of 4.375% senior notes due 2031, an increase from the previously announced size. The offering is expected to close on October 5, 2020.

title: Bank of America Stands by Pledge of No Layoffs This Year
summary: Bank of America plans to uphold its promise of no staff layoffs in 2020, as stated by CEO Brian Moynihan. This commitment stands in contrast to several other major banks, including Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase, which have resumed job cuts amidst the pandemic. The bank will continue to manage its headcount through attrition alone.

title: As Goldman, JPMorgan resume cuts, Bank of America reiterates no-layoff vow
summary: As Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase resume job cuts, Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan reiterated the bank's commitment to no layoffs for the year. This comes as other major banks like Citi and Wells Fargo have also restarted workforce reductions, with the industry on pace to cut over 80,000 positions in 2020. Moynihan highlighted Bank of America's strategy of relying on attrition and its progress in diversity initiatives.

title: KKR-backed Academy Sports and Outdoors raises $203 million in IPO - source
summary: Academy Sports and Outdoors, backed by KKR, raised $203 million in its IPO by selling shares at $13 each, below its target range of $15-$17. The IPO valued the company at $1.1 billion, despite a surge in demand for at-home leisure activities during the coronavirus pandemic which significantly boosted its e-commerce sales. Shares are expected to begin trading on Nasdaq under the symbol "ASO".

title: USAA sues PNC over alleged infringement of mobile deposit tech
summary: USAA has sued PNC in federal court, alleging that PNC infringed on two patents related to mobile check deposit technology. This lawsuit follows USAA's prior nine-figure judgments against Wells Fargo for similar patent infringements. USAA seeks reasonable compensation for the use of its remote deposit capture patents, which are also used by over 6,500 financial institutions that utilize Mitek Systems' technology.

title: Lightsource bp Secures Financing on Bighorn Solar Project in Colorado
summary: Lightsource bp has secured $285 million in financing for its Bighorn Solar project in Pueblo, Colorado. The project, located on the Evraz Rocky Mountain Steel mill property, will supply power to the steel mill via a long-term contract with Xcel Energy, helping to preserve 1,000 local jobs and support Colorado's renewable energy goals. Construction has begun and is expected to create 300 direct jobs, with commercial operation slated for late 2021.

title: Bank of America, Wells Fargo and Truist remain deposit leaders in Sarasota-Manatee
summary: Bank of America maintained its lead as the largest bank by customer deposits in the Sarasota-Manatee region, marking its tenth consecutive year at the top. Despite its merger, Truist Bank narrowly missed unseating Wells Fargo for the second position, with only a $90.3 million difference in deposits. The region saw an overall increase of $3.1 billion in deposits, partly attributed to investors seeking the security of insured bank deposits.

title: Bank of America wades into digital financial planning space
summary: Bank of America is launching "Life Plan," a new digital financial planning tool to compete with fintech companies. This tool allows customers to set financial goals and receive personalized recommendations by leveraging existing client data, making financial planning accessible beyond high-net worth individuals. The initiative aims to provide a fuller financial picture to customers and potentially increase engagement with the bank's services.

title: Today In Digital-First Banking: BoA Launches Life Plan; United Airlines, Chase Roll Out United Gateway Card
summary: Bank of America has introduced its Life Plan program for digital financial planning. Concurrently, United Airlines and Chase Card Services have launched a new no-annual-fee United Gateway credit card, offering travel miles for various purchases. Additionally, NCR Corp. has upgraded its ATM operating software with the "Activate Enterprise NextGen ATM infrastructure," aiming to integrate ATMs further into the digital age.

title: What's next for TD after completing Ameritrade sale to Charles Schwab
summary: TD Bank has completed the sale of Ameritrade to Charles Schwab, resulting in TD holding a 13.5% stake in Charles Schwab. After an eight-month holding period, analysts believe TD may sell this stake to fund the acquisition of another U.S. bank. This move could significantly alter TD's strategic presence in the American banking market.

title: Morgan Stanley’s Eaton Vance Acquisition Could Mean More Asset Management Mergers Are Coming
summary: Morgan Stanley is acquiring asset management firm Eaton Vance for $7 billion, increasing its assets under management to $1.2 trillion and solidifying a trend of consolidation in the asset management industry. Analysts believe more mergers are likely as firms seek to fill product gaps and benefit from historically low valuations. This acquisition follows Morgan Stanley's earlier purchase of E-Trade, indicating a strategic shift towards expanding its investment management business.

title: Bank of America enters the small-dollar loan fray
summary: Bank of America announced it will begin offering "Balance Assist" loans of up to $500 for a flat $5 fee. This initiative, rolling out in January and expanding nationwide in early 2021, aims to provide an alternative to high-interest payday loans, aligning with recent regulatory encouragement for banks to enter the small-dollar lending space. The loans can be repaid in three equal installments over 90 days and consumers can only take out one loan at a time.

title: Bank of America's plan in Columbus: Keep going
summary: Bank of America is continuing its expansion in Central Ohio, having opened its first Columbus branch on Morse Road in July 2019. The bank's market leader discussed plans for further growth in the region, focusing on a technology-centered design to attract customers.

title: Symcor helps to accelerate digital transformation in the COVID-19 era and beyond
summary: Symcor, a joint venture of Canada's top financial institutions, played a crucial role in helping the Canadian financial services sector respond to the COVID-19 pandemic by quickly deploying fraud detection solutions and digitizing operations. The company specializes in payment processing, customer communications, and fraud detection, assisting large organizations across various sectors. Symcor anticipates a continued acceleration of digital transformation and aims to be a key player in the future of open banking in Canada, ensuring data security and accessibility.

title: Actualización: Cemex recauda fondos en emisión internacional para pagar deuda
summary: Cemex, a Mexican cement company, issued $1 billion in senior guaranteed notes in the international market at a 5.200% rate with a 10-year term to pay down debt and for general corporate purposes. This private placement, which closed on September 17, involved several legal advisors for Cemex and the initial purchasers. The company plans to list these notes on the Irish Stock Exchange for trading on Euronext Dublin, following a similar bond issue in June.

title: China’s Ping An-Backed Lufax Files for $3 Billion U.S. IPO
summary: Lufax Holding Ltd., a Chinese online wealth management platform backed by Ping An Insurance Group, has filed for a U.S. IPO aiming to raise about $3 billion. This move comes as the company shifts away from its P2P lending origins and follows another Ping An-backed fintech listing (OneConnect Financial Technology), amidst a backdrop of rising U.S.-China tensions. The company reported a net profit of 7.27 billion yuan for the first half of 2020.

title: Eastern Bank Prepares for $1.8B IPO
summary: Eastern Bank, the oldest mutual bank in the US, is set to go public on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on October 14, with shares launching at $10 each, valuing the company at nearly $1.8 billion. The capital raised from the IPO will be used for technology investments, new services, and acquisitions in banking and insurance. Additionally, former CEO Ken LaRoe announced plans to launch Climate First Bank in Florida, focusing on an impact-based "triple bottom line" approach.

title: Credit Suisse Hires Veteran Meissner to Lead New Unit Serving Wealthy Clients
summary: Credit Suisse has hired Christian Meissner, a former veteran of Bank of America and Goldman Sachs, to lead a new unit aimed at connecting its wealthiest clients with its investment bank. Meissner will serve as co-head of international wealth-management investment banking advisory and vice chairman of investment banking. This strategic move is intended to enhance revenue from affluent clients by offering them exclusive access to deals and business opportunities through Credit Suisse's investment banking services, amidst increasing competition in banking the ultra-rich.

title: Americold acquires Agro Merchants Group in $1.74 billion deal
summary: Americold Realty Trust has announced its acquisition of Agro Merchants Group, the world's fourth-largest temperature-controlled operator, for $1.74 billion. This deal significantly expands Americold's global footprint, particularly in Europe, and is expected to be modestly accretive to earnings in 2021. The acquisition will be financed through a combination of Americold stock, cash, debt repayment, and capital lease assumption, with management from Oaktree and Agro retaining a substantial equity position in Americold.

title: Credit Suisse Set to Hire Ex-BofA Investment Banker Meissner
summary: Credit Suisse Group AG is preparing to hire Christian Meissner, former head of Bank of America's investment bank. He will co-head a new unit designed to connect the bank's wealthiest clients with services and deals from its investment banking division. Meissner will relocate to Europe and report to the heads of both the investment bank and the international wealth management business.

title: Americold Acquires Agro Merchants Group In $1.74 Billion Deal
summary: Americold Realty Trust (NYSE: COLD) has announced the acquisition of Agro Merchants Group, the world's fourth-largest temperature-controlled operator, for $1.74 billion. This strategic move aims to expand Americold's global network, particularly facilitating its entry into Europe and strengthening its presence in the U.S., South America, and Australia. The deal, expected to close late 2020 or early 2021, will result in Americold's portfolio comprising 229 owned and managed facilities globally.

title: Bank of America registers 16% fall in profit in Q3 | Daily Sabah
summary: Bank of America Corp. reported a 15.6% fall in profit for the third quarter, dropping to $4.88 billion from $5.78 billion a year ago. The bank's earnings of 51 cents per share missed Wall Street expectations, and its revenue of $21.69 billion (net of interest expense $20.34 billion) also fell short of forecasts. Bank of America shares have declined significantly since the beginning of the year and over the past 12 months.

title: Bank of America weathers profit drop in ongoing Covid-19 environment
summary: Bank of America reported a net income of $4.9 billion, or 51 cents per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2020. This indicates a profit drop in the continuing COVID-19 pandemic environment. The article highlights how the Charlotte-based bank is navigating these financial challenges.

title: Wells Fargo earnings fall short of estimates as low rates hit interest income
summary: Wells Fargo reported disappointing third-quarter earnings, missing analyst estimates with 42 cents per share against a Refinitiv forecast of 45 cents. The bank's net interest income declined by 19% due to historically low interest rates, though revenue of $18.86 billion surpassed expectations. Despite the challenges, Wells Fargo showed some positive signs with lower credit loss provisions and increased noninterest income, but its stock remained down significantly year-to-date.

title: Credit Suisse Taps Ex-BofA Rainmaker to Target Richest Clients
summary: Credit Suisse has hired Christian Meissner, a former top rainmaker at Bank of America Corp., to help cater to its wealthiest clients. Meissner will co-run a new group designed to connect entrepreneurial clients of its international wealth management unit with investment banking services. This move is part of Credit Suisse's strategy to deepen relationships with its richest customers and compete with rivals like UBS Group AG.

title: Goldman's trading business returns to former glory during pandemic stress
summary: Goldman Sachs reported its best quarterly performance in a decade, largely driven by a 29% jump in trading revenue during the pandemic. The bank's limited exposure to consumer lending, unlike its rivals, proved to be an advantage. Analysts consider its current business mix, with strong capital markets leverage and a small, high-quality loan portfolio, to be well-suited for the current economic climate.

title: Bank of America Profit Falls 16%
summary: Bank of America's third-quarter profit declined by 16% to $4.88 billion compared to the previous year, although the bank stated it is prepared to handle the coronavirus recession. This comes after earning $3.53 billion in the prior quarter. The Charlotte, N.C., lender announced these figures from July to September.

title: Goldman’s Pandemic Hot Streak Continues in Third Quarter
summary: Goldman Sachs reported a near-doubling of its third-quarter profit, reaching $3.62 billion on revenue of $10.78 billion, significantly exceeding analyst forecasts despite the ongoing pandemic and recession. This strong performance, driven by trading revenue increases, highlights Wall Street's continued profitability amidst broader economic challenges. While banks' "Main Street" arms also show resilience, concerns about a potential double-dip recession and prolonged high unemployment remain.

title: Bank of America Profit Falls 16%
summary: Bank of America's profit fell 16% in the third quarter to $4.88 billion, down from $5.78 billion a year ago. Despite the drop, the bank stated it is well-prepared to handle the coronavirus recession. This earnings report was part of a series of bank reports highlighting financial performance during the pandemic.

title: Wells Fargo cuts 'sizable group' of advisers after profits slump
summary: Wells Fargo is laying off a "sizable group" of financial advisers, particularly those in the Financial Relationship Advisors group, as part of a cost-cutting effort due to slumping profits and the COVID-19 pandemic. The bank reported a year-over-year decline of 815 advisers, a 5.9% drop, bringing its total to 12,908 advisers. This move is significant given the rarity of adviser layoffs in the wealth management industry where they are crucial for revenue generation.

title: Truist posts $1.1B profit, continues merger-related job cuts and branch closures
summary: Truist reported a $1.1 billion profit for the third quarter of 2020, a significant increase from the previous year. The Charlotte-based bank is continuing to implement merger-related cost-cutting measures, including closing 104 branches and eliminating 769 jobs during the quarter, with plans for further consolidation in 2021. Despite the pandemic, the company is on track to achieve $1.6 billion in cost savings by 2022.

title: Peloton Has Soared 350% In 2020. Here’s Why The Stock Will Keep Rising This Year, According To Experts
summary: Peloton shares reached an all-time high despite a recall and patent infringement suit, with analysts predicting further growth. Experts suggest that a permanent shift towards at-home fitness due to the pandemic will continue to drive Peloton's success, with several analysts raising their price targets. The company's stock has quadrupled since May, driven by strong quarterly earnings reports and increased investor optimism.

title: Fidelity on pace to dominate HSA business
summary: Fidelity Investments is rapidly expanding its market share in the health savings account (HSA) business, with its assets increasing by 39% through June this year. The company has seen its market share more than double since 2016, making it a leading player alongside Optum, HealthEquity, and HSA Bank. Fidelity's HSA is also highly rated for both spending and investing, offering a competitive all-in investment fee.

title: Miniso Raises $608 Million in U.S. IPO, MNSO Stock Jumped in Debut
summary: Miniso Group Holding Limited, co-founded by Chinese entrepreneur Ye Guofu and Japanese designer Miyake Junya, successfully raised $608 million in its U.S. IPO, with its shares (MNSO) debuting at $24.40 and closing up 4.4%. The company, backed by Tencent and Hillhouse Capital, stated its intent to use technology to stay ahead in the competitive retail market against giants like Amazon and Walmart. Ye Guofu, who owns an 80% stake, is set to become a dollar billionaire as a result of the listing.

title: 'FinCEN Files' leaker harmed US anti-laundering regime and should be prosecuted, say bankers
summary: Bank compliance officers are calling for the prosecution of the individual responsible for leaking over 2,000 highly confidential suspicious activity reports (SARs) that led to the "FinCEN Files" news articles. They argue that the leak undermines trust in the SARs system, which is crucial for the U.S. fight against illicit financial transactions, and necessitates re-evaluation of how banks file these sensitive documents to maintain partnerships with law enforcement. Authorities are investigating the source of the leak, which has raised concerns about the efficacy and future of the anti-money laundering regime.

title: Who is Truist CEO Kelly King? He’s not the banker you think he is
summary: This article profiles Truist CEO Kelly King, detailing his journey from poverty in rural North Carolina to leading the sixth-largest bank in the U.S. It highlights his pivotal role in the $66 billion merger of BB&T and SunTrust, emphasizing how his challenging upbringing shaped his leadership style and resilience in the banking industry. The story explores his personal transformation after a behavioral psychology retreat and his commitment to overcoming challenges, drawing parallels between his past struggles and his current leadership role.

title: Pandemic presents a ‘terrific opportunity’ for BMO executive’s plans to digitize
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic has prompted Bank of Montreal (BMO) chief strategy and operations officer Cameron Fowler to accelerate the bank's digitization efforts. Despite initial surges in digital adoption easing, Fowler aims to embed new digital tools across all BMO divisions and redefine workspace needs and branch functions. This strategic shift is expected to save hundreds of millions of dollars and modernize the bank's operations.

title: Is Charles Schwab Still Active in the Company?
summary: Charles Schwab Corporation is a significant entity in financial services, founded by Charles Robert Schwab in 1971. The article explains Charles Schwab's personal history, how his company revolutionized investing through discount brokerage services, and its current offerings including banking and asset management. Charles Schwab himself remains active as the company's chairman and largest shareholder, with an estimated net worth of $7.4 billion.

title: UBS Profit Doubles on Trading Surge
summary: UBS Group AG announced that its net profit nearly doubled in the third quarter due to a surge in client trading and deal-making, enabling the company to free up cash for dividends and share buybacks amidst the pandemic. This strong performance, particularly in its investment bank and wealth-management units, highlights the growing divergence between European banks during the health crisis. The results were achieved as CEO Sergio Ermotti approaches the end of his term.

title: Essent increases credit facility
summary: Essent Group Ltd has increased its credit facility from $500 million to $625 million, which includes an increase in its revolving credit facility and an additional non-amortising term loan. This move enhances the Bermudian-based mortgage re/insurer's capital and liquidity position, with borrowings available for working capital and general corporate purposes. The amended terms and extended maturity to October 2023 reflect Essent's strong financial profile and provide added financial flexibility.

title: After Helping Shepherd Pandemic Loans, Banks Now Brace for Regulatory Risks
summary: Banks that participated in the U.S. government's Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) are facing increasing regulatory scrutiny and legal risks despite their initial role in distributing $525 billion in pandemic loans. Concerns include potential violations of application rules, inadequate documentation, and "know your customer" compliance, as the government begins to forgive loans and fraud inquiries mount. Major lenders like JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, and Bank of America have warned investors about these impending challenges.

title: GDS Holdings hosts Hong Kong IPO in bid to raise $1.8bn
summary: GDS Holdings, a Chinese data center company, is launching an IPO on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange to raise $1.8 billion. The company plans to sell 160 million Class A ordinary shares at approximately $11 each, with a portion offered to Hong Kong investors and the rest internationally. Proceeds from the IPO will primarily fund data center expansion and R&D efforts.

title: Wells Fargo to Eliminate 401(k) Match for High-Paid Employees–Sources
summary: Wells Fargo & Co. is eliminating the 401(k) retirement account match for employees earning $250,000 or higher, as part of its expense reduction efforts. The bank aims to emphasize support for lower-paid employees and will introduce new efforts to seed retirement plans for those making less than $75,000 annually. Despite not anticipating significant savings from this change, it represents a broader measure taken by the bank to address financial pressures and past scandals.

title: Does Capital One Offer Student Loans?
summary: Capital One does not offer student loans, prompting individuals to seek alternatives for private student loans or refinancing. The article suggests exploring options from other banks, credit unions, online lenders like Ascent, College Ave, and Earnest, and state-based agencies. It also emphasizes exhausting federal financial aid opportunities before considering private loans due to their unique benefits.

title: Shinhan closing in on HSBC to be top foreign bank in Vietnam
summary: Shinhan Bank Vietnam is on track to become the leading foreign bank in Vietnam, driven by strong performance, advanced digital services, and an aggressive localization strategy. The bank's net profit saw significant growth despite the global pandemic, placing it in fierce competition with HSBC Vietnam. Shinhan's focus on retail banking services, expansion of its network, and support for Korean SMEs in Vietnam have been key factors in its success.

title: Dave & Buster’s Announces Closing of $550 Million Senior Secured Notes Offering by its Subsidiary Dave & Buster’s, Inc.
summary: Dave & Buster's Entertainment, Inc. announced the closing of a $550 million senior secured notes offering by its subsidiary, Dave & Buster's, Inc. The proceeds from the 7.625% senior secured notes due 2025 will be used to repay outstanding amounts under its Term Loan Facility and drawings under its Revolving Credit Facility. J.P. Morgan acted as lead book running manager for the private offering.

title: Texas Capital Bancshares names JPMorgan executive Rob Holmes as its new CEO
summary: Texas Capital Bancshares has appointed Rob C. Holmes, a JPMorgan Chase & Co. executive, as its new Chief Executive Officer, effective January 2021. Holmes will replace Larry L. Helm, who took on the role after a proposed $5.5 billion merger with Independent Bank fell apart earlier in the year. The Dallas-based bank struggled earlier in 2020 but saw a turnaround in the third quarter after Helm took over.

title: Carver Selected for Bank of America Investment
summary: Bank of America has made equity investments in ten minority depository institutions as part of its $1 billion commitment to racial equality and economic opportunity. Carver Financial Corporation, holding company for Carver State Bank of Savannah, is among the institutions to receive an investment. These investments, totaling approximately 4.9% of the common equity in each organization, aim to scale critical projects and enable positive change within communities served by these MDIs and CDFIs.

title: This Bank Wants to Use Animal Crossing to Sell You on Financial Services
summary: Ally, a financial services company, hosted a sponsored island in Animal Crossing to market its banking and investment services to millennials. The campaign aimed to connect with a demographic less engaged with traditional banking by showcasing financial products within the game's context, emphasizing wealth management and investing as easy and accessible. The article critiques this marketing approach as a manifestation of the financialization of games and the gamification of finance, aiming to define how millennial consumers "should" act in a capitalistic system.

title: Citigroup issues largest-ever private sector social bond
summary: Citigroup has issued the largest-ever private-sector social bond, a $2.5 billion issuance aimed at affordable housing as part of a broader $1 billion initiative to combat racial inequality. This transaction contributes to a surge in social bond issuances during the coronavirus pandemic, with proceeds channeled to socially beneficial projects, mirroring similar efforts by banks like Bank of America. The move reinforces Citi's commitment to increasing homeownership among racial minorities and reflects growing interest in ethical investments.

title: American Express pledges $1B toward racial, gender equality
summary: American Express has committed $1 billion to advance racial and gender equality, with a significant portion dedicated to doubling spending with diverse and minority-owned suppliers to $750 million annually by 2024. The company also announced it achieved 100% gender pay equity worldwide and aims to support Black-owned businesses, female entrepreneurs, and non-profit organizations led by underrepresented groups. This pledge follows similar commitments from other financial institutions in response to recent social justice movements.

title: Dayton area business people hired, promoted
summary: This article details recent hirings and promotions among business professionals in the Dayton area. Key appointments include Tony Boddie at Merchants Bank of Indiana, new volunteer officials at Day Air Credit Union, and Tara Marlow as CEO of the Boys & Girls Club of Dayton. Additionally, Dr. Isaac Koh joined Soin Family Practice Center, and Jocelyn Spencer Rhynard was reappointed to the Ohio School Boards Association’s Federal Relations Network.

title: Wells Fargo taps Capital One executive to lead diversity efforts
summary: Wells Fargo has hired Kleber Santos, a former Capital One executive, to lead its newly formed diversity and inclusion group. Santos will report directly to CEO Charlie Scharf and will be responsible for creating a more diverse workplace and developing products and services for diverse customer segments. This move is part of Scharf's objective to increase minority representation in leadership roles, following previous criticism he received for comments about the availability of Black talent.

title: Biden Basket Vs Trump Trade — Potential Stock and Sector Winners and Losers
summary: This article explores potential stock and sector winners and losers under a Biden administration versus a second Trump term, based on analyses from financial institutions. It identifies "Biden basket" stocks in alternative energy, infrastructure, and those benefiting from fiscal stimulus and reduced tariff tensions, while "Trump basket" stocks include banks, fossil fuel companies, big tech, defense, and pharma/biotech due to differing regulatory and policy approaches.

title: Eight big banks must face U.S. cities' allegations of municipal bond collusion
summary: A federal judge has ruled that Philadelphia and Baltimore can proceed with a lawsuit against eight major banks, alleging they conspired to inflate interest rates on municipal bonds. The cities claim this collusion forced state and local governments to pay higher rates on variable-rate demand obligations (VRDOs) between 2008 and 2016, hindering funding for essential public services. The judge permitted antitrust and breach of contract claims to move forward, while dismissing unjust enrichment claims.

title: Capital One, JPMorgan Chase top J.D. Power’s small-business satisfaction survey
summary: A J.D. Power survey revealed that small businesses' satisfaction with their banks increased in 2020, particularly for larger businesses and those approved for the Paycheck Protection Program (PPP). Capital One and JPMorgan Chase emerged as top performers in various regions, though overall satisfaction varied significantly between business sizes and PPP outcomes. The survey highlights that banks successfully delivered for many during the pandemic but need to refine approaches for smaller businesses.

title: What executives at Pioneer Bank, Bank of Greene County made in 2020
summary: This article discusses the compensation of executives at Pioneer Bank and Bank of Greene County for the year 2020. It notes that strong bank performances in 2020 led to increased total compensation for almost every named executive at Albany-area banks with fiscal years ending in June 2020.

title: San Francisco skyscraper part-owned by Trump is on the market, but not selling
summary: A San Francisco skyscraper at 555 California St., partly owned by Donald Trump, has been on the market since June but has not yet sold and may go for less than its $1 billion valuation. Vornado Realty Trust, which owns 70% of the building, stated that while there is active investor interest, they might not achieve their original pricing objective due to investor caution. Trump's 30% stake in the building originated from a passive real estate investment in 2007.

title: San Francisco skyscraper part-owned by Trump is on the market, but not selling
summary: A San Francisco skyscraper, 555 California St., part-owned by Donald Trump, has been on the market since June but remains unsold and may fetch less than its original $1 billion valuation. Vornado Realty Trust owns 70% and Trump holds a 30% limited partnership. The lagging sale is attributed to investor caution, according to Vornado Realty Trust CEO Steven Roth, who also referenced another Trump-linked Manhattan property facing similar challenges.

title: Sallie Mae lays off 100+ in Delaware in restructuring
summary: Sallie Mae laid off 105 employees in Delaware as part of a company-wide restructuring to cut costs and boost operating efficiencies amid a disrupted higher education market. The layoffs represent 6% of the company's total workforce and incurred $24 million in restructuring expenses, primarily for severance and benefits. Despite the cuts, Sallie Mae is actively hiring in Delaware and its CEO stated the restructuring is to align the business with strategic imperatives and strengthen the company for 2021.

title: Wells Fargo now requires 'affirmative request' from customers before providing COVID forbearance
summary: Wells Fargo has changed its policy to require an affirmative request from customers before providing or extending COVID-related forbearance, following a class-action lawsuit and complaints about negative credit impacts. The bank had previously placed some customers into forbearance without explicit consent, a practice that drew scrutiny from Senator Elizabeth Warren and resulted in over 1,600 complaints. Wells Fargo stated that this policy change was implemented "several months ago."

title: Private Prison Stocks Drop as the Reality of Biden’s Win Sinks In
summary: Following President-elect Joe Biden's victory, stocks for the two largest private prison companies, GEO Group and CoreCivic, significantly dropped as Biden campaigned on ending the federal government's use of private prisons. These companies heavily rely on federal contracts for over 50% of their revenue. While ending Bureau of Prisons contracts might be straightforward, dismantling immigration detention in private facilities, which accounts for about 70% of ICE detainees, presents a more complex challenge due to its deep entrenchment within federal operations.

title: Zoom and other ‘stay-at-home’ stocks got crushed on the positive vaccine news
summary: Shares of "stay-at-home" stocks like Zoom, Amazon, and Netflix dropped significantly after positive news regarding a COVID-19 vaccine from Pfizer and BioNTech. Investors rotated out of these pandemic-benefiting companies and into those expected to gain from an economic reopening, such as banks and cruise lines.

title: Wirehouse Wars: Merrill Loses Young NYC Star to Morgan Stanley
summary: James P Taylor, a young and highly-regarded Merrill Lynch advisor who built a significant book of business, moved his 13-person team to Morgan Stanley. This move highlights an ongoing trend of Merrill losing seasoned and next-gen advisors, despite the firm's efforts to retain talent through new career-development programs amid its recruiting freeze. Taylor's team, specializing in corporate executive stock portfolios, represents a significant gain for Morgan Stanley, which has actively recruited teams in this niche.

title: Bradesco Cartões lança promoção “Transforme sua Casa” assinada pela One Digital
summary: Bradesco Cartões launched the "Transforme sua Casa" promotion, distributing R$ 2 million in prizes to help Brazilians make their homes more comfortable. Participants can register on the campaign's hotsite, and every purchase of R$ 30 or more by credit or debit card accrues a lucky number for drawings held every fifteen days, with a grand prize of R$ 500,000 in January 2021. The campaign, which also includes social media pieces created by One Digital, aims to capitalize on the increased time people are spending at home.

title: American Airlines Proposes The Sale Of 38.5 Million Shares
summary: American Airlines has announced a proposed public offering of 38.5 million shares of its common stock at $13 each to boost liquidity and cover general corporate purposes. This is the second share issue this year, aimed at mitigating losses caused by the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic and declining ticket sales. The airline has also implemented significant cost-cutting measures, including a reduction in its workforce, deferred aircraft deliveries, and the retirement of its Airbus A330 fleet.

title: Arbor Realty Names Affordable Housing Managing Director
summary: Arbor Realty Trust Inc. has appointed Arthanais Williams as managing director of affordable housing, where he will oversee the agency's multifamily affordable financing platform and structured product lines. Williams brings over 20 years of experience from previous roles at Freddie Mac and Bank of America Merrill Lynch, specializing in valuation, acquisition, rehabilitation, and financial structuring for various real estate assets.

title: HDFC Bank aims to grow merchant payments base to 20 million in 3 years
summary: HDFC Bank plans to expand its merchant network from 2 million to 20 million within the next three years. This expansion is supported by the upgraded Smart Hub platform, which offers various digital tools like a digital ledger, billing software, and inventory management. The bank intends to cross-sell loans and credit cards, including 'buy now, pay later' options, to further drive growth and deepen digital payment penetration across India.

title: 2021 COMP: RBC Restores Small-Account Penalty
summary: RBC Wealth Management-U.S. has reinstated its zero-payout policy for customer accounts under $100,000, which had been suspended in March 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic. This penalty is part of its 2021 compensation plan, which is largely consistent with 2020, and aims to focus brokers on wealthier clients, a common practice among large firms like Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch. Additionally, RBC is restoring a benefit that allows qualifying brokers to be reimbursed for business development account expenses through pre-tax deductions.

title: Xpeng (NYSE: XPEV) Stock Is Currently Severely Overvalued Relative To Its Larger Peer NIO (NYSE: NIO)
summary: This article argues that Xpeng (XPEV) stock is severely overvalued compared to its larger Chinese EV peer, NIO (NIO). While Xpeng has seen significant stock appreciation since its August 2020 IPO, its production levels are much lower than NIO's, and its Price-to-Sales ratio is nearly double. The author suggests that despite a recent bullish outlook from Bank of America for Xpeng, investors might find better returns by waiting for a dip due to its current lofty valuation.

title: Irsa y Cresud: contundente apoyo al canje de sus ON
summary: IRSA and Cresud successfully concluded their debt exchange offers, receiving strong support from investors. IRSA achieved a 98.31% acceptance rate for its bonds totaling US$178 million, while Cresud saw an 88.41% acceptance for US$65 million. The exchange involved the issuance of new series of negotiable obligations with varying maturity dates, enabling the companies to navigate restrictions imposed by the BCRA on foreign currency debt payments.

title: What Stocks Did Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Buy in the 3rd Quarter? We Will Soon Find Out.
summary: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway was active in the stock market during the third quarter, with movements in major holdings. The company bought stock in Bank of America, sold shares of Wells Fargo, and seemingly reduced its significant stake in Apple. More details on these transactions are expected to be revealed soon.

title: Richard Gagliano, Black Knight (US)
summary: This article profiles Richard Gagliano, President of Black Knight's origination technologies division. It details his 25 years of experience in financial services, including nine years at Black Knight, and his previous roles at Aurora Bank, Bank of America, Nexstar Financial Corporation, Citi, and Mercantile Bank. Gagliano's responsibilities include directing the organization's loan origination system and leveraging his expertise from his educational background in business administration and finance.

title: LPL Affiliate Gladstone Hires $2-Billion Morgan Stanley Team
summary: Gladstone Wealth Management, an LPL Financial affiliate, has recruited a team of advisors, John W. Gallagher and Mark T. Levin, from Morgan Stanley Wealth Management, bringing with them $2 billion in assets and $5 million in annual revenue. This move represents Gladstone's largest recruitment to date and allows the advisors to operate with greater independence and a higher payout level. They plan to expand their business by leveraging Gladstone's partnership model and LPL's open architecture platform.

title: PNC Bank Buying BBVA USA Bancshares for $11.6 Billion
summary: PNC Financial Services Group is acquiring BBVA USA Bancshares for $11.6 billion, a deal expected to close in mid-2021. This acquisition will create one of the largest banks in the U.S., with a significant presence across 29 of the 30 largest markets and an estimated $560 billion in assets, ranking it as the seventh-largest American bank. The transaction will see existing BBVA USA branches converted to the PNC Bank name and its customers transitioned to the PNC platform.

title: Banco Santander Is Reportedly Planning to Shut Down Up to 1,000 Branches, May Cut 4,000 Jobs
summary: Banco Santander is reportedly planning significant cost-cutting measures in Spain, including the closure of up to 1,000 branches and the elimination of 4,000 jobs. These actions are a response to economic challenges from the COVID-19 pandemic, low interest rates in the euro zone, and a growing consumer shift to digital banking. The bank, along with other European lenders, is struggling to adapt to these market changes and maintain operational efficiency.

title: BBVA sells U.S. subsidiary to PNC for $11.6 billion
summary: BBVA has agreed to sell its U.S. subsidiary to PNC for $11.6 billion in cash, a transaction that will significantly enhance BBVA's financial position and provide flexibility for capital deployment and shareholder distributions. The deal, valued at 19.7 times the unit's 2019 earnings, excludes BBVA's broker dealer and New York branch, allowing BBVA to continue serving corporate and institutional clients in the U.S. PNC will become the fifth-largest bank in the U.S. by assets after the transaction closes, which is expected in mid-2021.

title: Tom York on Business: Cleantech Startup Nuvve Goes Public in Unusual Merger
summary: San Diego-based cleantech startup Nuvve Corp., a company developing vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology, is going public through a merger with Newborn Acquisition Corp., a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC). The deal is expected to bring over $70 million to Nuvve, and the combined entity, Nuvve Holding Corp., will be listed on Nasdaq under the ticker "NVVE." CEO Gregory Poilasne projects the global V2G market to exceed $17 billion by 2027, with Nuvve positioned at the forefront.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | PNC Financial Services to Buy U.S. Arm of Spain’s BBVA for $11.6 Billion
summary: PNC Financial Services Group Inc. has agreed to acquire the U.S. operations of Spain's BBVA for $11.6 billion. This deal marks one of the largest bank mergers since the financial crisis, poised to establish the fifth-largest U.S. retail bank with over $550 billion in assets.

title: PNC buys Houston-based BBVA USA for $11.6 billion
summary: PNC Financial Services Group has agreed to acquire BBVA's Houston-based U.S. banking operations for $11.6 billion, positioning it to become the country's largest regional bank. This acquisition allows PNC to expand into Texas and California, using funds from its BlackRock Inc. stake sale, while providing BBVA with capital for potential acquisitions and an exit from a business that has weighed on its earnings. The deal, expected to close by June, will boost PNC's earnings and significantly expand its presence across the southern and southwestern U.S.

title: Spain's BBVA Sells US Arm To PNC In $11.6 Billion Deal
summary: PNC Financial Services Group, which previously divested its stake in BlackRock, has agreed to acquire the US arm of Spain's BBVA for $11.6 billion. This acquisition will expand PNC's presence across 29 of the 30 largest markets in the US, adding substantial deposits and loans. The deal, expected to close in mid-2021, aims to be significantly accretive to PNC's earnings and generate over $900 million in cost savings.

title: Think Private Prison Companies Are Going Away Under Biden? They Have Other Plans
summary: Despite the election of Joe Biden, who pledged to curb private prisons, major companies like CoreCivic and GEO Group are well-positioned to continue profiting. They have been aggressively diversifying their business models, shifting away from traditional prisons towards other government contracts such as commercial real estate, electronic monitoring, and halfway houses, and capitalizing on growing needs for immigration detention and re-entry services. This strategic pivot ensures their financial stability even as the political climate changes regarding mass incarceration.

title: Saudi Aramco gets $8 billion with jumbo five-part bond deal
summary: Saudi Aramco successfully raised $8 billion through a five-part bond deal, receiving $48.1 billion in order; this marks a significant move by the world's largest oil producer to secure cash amid low oil prices and to fund its substantial dividend payments and the acquisition of a 70% stake in Saudi Basic Industries (SABIC). The bond placement is part of a broader trend of Gulf issuers tapping international debt markets to address pandemic- and oil price-related financial pressures. The sale included tranches ranging from three to 50 years, with the 50-year bond being the longest-dated international debt issued by Saudi Arabia to date.

title: Hawaiian Airlines, Barclays, CPI Card Group, Collaborate on Recovered Ocean-Bound Plastic Credit Cards
summary: Hawaiian Airlines and Barclays US Consumer Bank have partnered with CPI Card Group to introduce Second Wave™ credit cards made with recovered ocean-bound plastic for its Hawaiian Airlines World Elite Mastercard® members. This initiative aims to address plastic waste in oceans, with CPI estimating that over one ton of plastic will be diverted for every one million cards produced. To further support coastal stewardship, Hawaiian Airlines and Barclays are contributing $50,000 to Sustainable Coastlines Hawai‘i.

title: Desglobalización bancaria
summary: BBVA's strategic move to sell its US operations and propose a merger with Banco Sabadell signifies a shift towards "desglobalización" and a "back to basics" approach, focusing on its traditional Spanish market. This strategy aims to improve solvency and achieve synergies to counter low banking profitability in Spain and Europe, despite increasing market concentration. The article also notes that while national market share will rise, competition in sub-markets and from non-bank digital entities will mitigate potential negative effects.

title: European Customer Experience Index, 2020: How Banks And Insurers Can Connect CX With Business Impact
summary: This article discusses the findings from Forrester's European Customer Experience Index, 2020, focusing on how banking and insurance companies can link customer experience (CX) to business impact. It highlights that CX leaders achieve faster revenue growth and cost reductions, but many financial services firms struggle to quantify this value. The research, based on a survey across several European countries, reveals that direct banks outperform incumbents in CX, while most insurers offer mediocre and undifferentiated experiences, underscoring the need for these firms to prioritize CX improvements to drive financial performance.

title: HSBC to Let HK Staff Work at Home Four Days a Week and More Asia Real Estate Headlines
summary: HSBC is allowing some Hong Kong staff to work from home up to four days a week, promoting flexible working arrangements. Other major real estate headlines include CapitaLand securing green loans for Indian tech parks, Roxy-Pacific buying a Singapore residential site, and SL Green's joint venture landing a $1.3 billion construction loan in New York. Chinese firms are also dominating industrial land investments in Vietnam.

title: Banker Jorge Brito killed in Salta helicopter crash
summary: Argentine banker, businessman, and entrepreneur Jorge Brito, 68, was killed in a helicopter crash in Salta, Argentina, along with his pilot. The accident is believed to have occurred when the helicopter, flown by Brito, collided with a zip line owned by a local tourist company. Brito was known for founding Banco Macro and his extensive business interests, and was among Argentina's wealthiest individuals.

title: NISN - NiSun International Enterprise Development Group Co Ltd Stock Price and Quote
summary: This article provides a stock price quote and financial data for NiSun International Enterprise Development Group Co Ltd (NISN), including market capitalization, insider ownership, and performance metrics. It also lists recent news releases and operational updates detailing the company's expansion into various sectors like edible oil trading, corn supply, and gold business.

title: How Charlotte's largest banks are stepping up their ESG initiatives — and why it's more important than ever
summary: Charlotte's largest banks are escalating their environmental, social, and governance (ESG) initiatives, a trend amplified by the impact of Covid-19. This push toward ESG is becoming increasingly crucial across various industries, with banks like Bank of America and Truist demonstrating their commitment through sustainability bonds and community impact programs. The article highlights the growing importance of these initiatives for corporations.

title: Fifth Third Bank plots next branch in Charlotte amid fast-paced retail expansion
summary: Fifth Third Bancorp is planning to open another retail branch in Charlotte, continuing its rapid expansion in the region. This news comes as the bank has been actively growing its presence in the Charlotte market, a strategy that has been highlighted by its CEO. The ongoing expansion indicates a significant focus on retail banking growth in the area.

title: UPDATE: Bank of America Says Access to Merrill Accounts Has Been Restored
summary: Bank of America's Merrill Lynch wealth management platform experienced widespread technology outages for about four hours on Tuesday, preventing advisors from wiring client funds and confirming stock executions, and blocking self-directed Merrill Edge customers from accessing their accounts. While a bank spokesman confirmed services were restored, the incident led to significant customer frustration and financial losses for some, highlighting persistent issues with brokerage platforms during active trading periods. This outage follows several similar incidents for Merrill and other firms, prompting clients to consider switching brokers.

title: RXIL's First Trade Credit Insurance Transaction in Sandbox with Tata AIG, ICICI Bank and YES Bank
summary: Receivables Exchange of India (RXIL) has successfully initiated the first Trade Credit Insurance (TCI) backed transaction in a Sandbox environment with Tata AIG as insurer and ICICI Bank and YES Bank as financiers. This pioneering transaction aims to enhance financiers' ability to assign credit limits to corporates and improve liquidity for MSMEs by enabling discounting of invoices from lower-rated corporate buyers. The adoption of TCI on TReDS is expected to digitize credit insurance and significantly boost the platform's throughput.

title: Bank of Butterfield appoints Sonia Baxendale to its board
summary: The Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son has appointed Sonia Baxendale to its board as an independent director. Baxendale brings extensive experience from her role as president and CEO of the Global Risk Institute and previous senior leadership positions in retail banking and wealth management at CIBC. Her appointment coincides with Leslie Godridge's departure and is expected to provide invaluable insight into emerging risk factors affecting the global financial services industry.

title: Chinese education technology group 17 Education & Technology Group sets terms for $288 million US IPO
summary: 17 Education & Technology Group, a Chinese online K-12 tutoring service provider, announced terms for its US IPO, aiming to raise $288 million by offering 27.4 million ADSs at $9.50 to $11.50 per share. New investor China Pinnacle Equity Management plans to purchase $80 million worth of ADSs. The company, which provides data-driven teaching solutions to over 70,000 K-12 schools in China, expects a fully diluted market value of $2.2 billion at the midpoint of its proposed range.

title: How Charlotte's largest banks are navigating the surge in Covid-19 cases
summary: Charlotte's largest banks, including Bank of America and Wells Fargo, are maintaining modified branch operations as COVID-19 cases increase. Bank of America has implemented over 33,000 clear barriers and social distancing markers in its branches to adapt to the pandemic. The article was updated on December 1, 2020, at 12:09 PM EST.

title: PNC Makes Pittsburgh into a Banking Powerhouse
summary: PNC Bank has become the fifth-largest bank in the U.S. and the largest regional bank after acquiring the U.S. operations of Spanish bank BBVA for $11.6 billion. This acquisition expands PNC's footprint across the West Coast and Sun Belt, increasing its assets to $564 billion and giving it a presence in 29 of the 30 largest metro markets. This strategic move solidifies Pittsburgh's position as a national player in financial services.

title: First Republic Bank stock rises Tuesday, outperforms market
summary: First Republic Bank (FRC) stock rose 1.43% on Tuesday, closing at $131.41, and outperformed the broader market which also saw gains. This gain snapped a three-day losing streak for the company. Despite the rise, the stock underperformed some competitors like Bank of America Corp., SVB Financial Group, and East West Bancorp Inc.

title: Equifax Announces New President of Canadian Business
summary: Equifax has appointed Sue Hutchison as the new Canada Region President, effective November 30. John Hartman, President of Equifax International, highlighted her strong expertise in lending, digital payments, and financial services as crucial for accelerating growth. Hutchison previously held senior leadership roles at Mastercard, Payments Canada, D+H Corporate, HSBC, and Bank of America, bringing extensive industry experience to Equifax.

title: CIBC Announces Appointment of Katharine Stevenson as Chair of the Board
summary: CIBC announced the appointment of Katharine B. Stevenson as Chair of the Board, effective April 8, 2021, subject to her election as a director. Ms. Stevenson has been an independent director since 2011 and will succeed The Honourable John P. Manley, who is retiring. She brings extensive corporate governance experience and a background in financial executive roles in telecommunications and banking.

title: HDFC Bank's digital outages: 7 key takeaways from RBI action
summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has taken supervisory action against HDFC Bank due to frequent digital banking outages, instructing the bank to halt new digital launches and credit card customer sourcing. This unprecedented move by the RBI highlights concerns about the reliability of digital channels and the pressure banks face to rapidly introduce new digital products without adequate testing. The article outlines seven key points, including the first-time nature of RBI's action, the recurrence of such issues in HDFC Bank and other financial institutions, and the significant challenge this poses for HDFC Bank's new management in restoring customer confidence.

title: High-Producing Boston Broker Joins Kestra After Morgan Stanley Departure
summary: Jonathan Lonske, a former high-producing broker from Morgan Stanley Wealth Management in Boston, has joined Kestra Investment Services after being dismissed from Morgan Stanley for allegedly using unapproved client-prospecting software. Lonske, along with two other advisors from his former team, Tara Schutz and Mary Flanigan, will set up an independent practice with Kestra. Kestra, which works with around 1,700 independent brokers, has been actively recruiting advisors from employee-model firms, noting an acceleration of wealth managers leaving such models recently.

title: Maryland Bankers Association taps Bank of America lobbyist as CEO
summary: The Maryland Bankers Association has appointed Ramon Looby, a former Bank of America lobbyist, as its new CEO. Looby takes over from Kathleen Murphy, who departed in August to lead the Massachusetts Bankers Association. This transition marks a new chapter for the association as it brings in leadership with significant banking and lobbying experience.

title: M&T Bank Corp. stock rises Friday, outperforms market
summary: M&T Bank Corp. (MTB) stock rose 2.56% on Friday, closing at $128.02, outperforming the broader market as the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average also saw gains. This marked the fourth consecutive day of increases for M&T Bank, though it remained $45.98 short of its 52-week high. The company's stock also outperformed key competitors like Bank of America Corp., Wells Fargo & Co., and PNC Financial Services Group Inc.

title: Richard Etter Obituary (1938 - 2020) - Las Vegas, NV - Las Vegas Review-Journal
summary: Richard Albert Etter, a prominent figure in Nevada banking and a community leader, passed away on December 5, 2020, at the age of 82. Etter was instrumental in the growth of Valley Bank of Nevada, orchestrating its merger with Bank of America and pioneering banking innovations like ATMs. He was also deeply involved in the Las Vegas community, bringing national events to Southern Nevada and supporting educational institutions like Bishop Gorman High School and UNLV.

title: Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Bank of America diverge on bonuses
summary: Major banks in the U.S. are taking different approaches to employee bonuses, reflecting a divergence in compensation strategies. Morgan Stanley is issuing a one-time $1,000 bonus to about half its employees, primarily those earning less than $150,000. JPMorgan Chase is considering increasing variable compensation for traders by 15% to 20%, while Bank of America's senior executives suggested maintaining bonus pools for sales and trading at previous year levels despite revenue growth.

title: C3.ai Announces Pricing of Initial Public Offering
summary: C3.ai, a leading enterprise AI software provider, announced the pricing of its initial public offering of 15,500,000 shares of Class A common stock at $42.00 per share, aiming to raise $651 million. The shares were expected to begin trading on the New York Stock Exchange on December 9, 2020, under the ticker symbol "AI" and the offering was slated to close on December 11, 2020. Morgan Stanley, J.P. Morgan, and BofA Securities are lead book-running managers.

title: Banks look at ‘explainable’ AI systems to boost consumer trust
summary: Financial institutions are investing in "explainable" artificial intelligence (AI) to address concerns about algorithmic bias and lack of transparency in automated decision-making. This technology aims to make AI decisions more traceable and understandable for auditors, regulators, and consumers, helping to build trust and mitigate issues like discrimination in loan denials. While explainable AI offers solutions to the "black box" problem, experts caution that poorly structured data can still lead to skewed outcomes, emphasizing the need for continuous fine-tuning and good governance.

title: Penumbra Responds to False Allegations from Short Sellers Seeking to Manipulate Company Stock and Remove Life-saving Medical Devices from the Market
summary: Penumbra, Inc. issued a statement responding to what it calls "false allegations" from short sellers. The company addressed claims regarding scientific research by its co-founder, Dr. Arani Bose, clarifying that papers attributed to "A. Bose" are indeed his work. Penumbra also defended its JET 7 Reperfusion Catheter, stating that claims of patient deaths are baseless when the device is used as instructed.

title: Seer Announces Closing of Initial Public Offering and Full
summary: Seer, Inc. announced the closing of its initial public offering, raising approximately $201.3 million gross proceeds. The offering included the full exercise of underwriters' option to purchase additional shares, totaling 10,592,106 shares of Class A common stock at $19.00 per share. Seer's Class A common stock began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "SEER" on December 4, 2020.

title: BBVA México formaliza crédito sustentable por 51 millones de dólares con el Grupo Hotelero Valentin
summary: BBVA México has formalized a $51 million sustainable credit with Grupo Hotelero Valentin, marking the first KPI-linked loan of its kind for the Mexican hotel sector. This financing aims to promote a more sustainable economy by reducing energy and PET consumption, managing water properly, and protecting marine turtles. The initiative aligns with several UN Sustainable Development Goals, including affordable and clean energy, climate action, and life below water.

title: You can have it all — just not all at once, says first woman to head major Wall Street bank
summary: Jane Fraser, the first woman CEO of a major Wall Street bank (Citigroup), advises that career success and personal life balance are achievable, but not necessarily all at the same time. She emphasizes that young people should not rush their careers, which are measured in decades, and that collecting diverse experiences is more valuable than solely focusing on upward promotions. Fraser also highlighted the importance of putting employees first, a philosophy she aims to continue at Citigroup.

title: Fifth Third commits $2.8 billion to help lift underserved communities
summary: Fifth Third Bancorp has announced a $2.8 billion commitment to programs aimed at advancing racial equity in the U.S. This three-year initiative will provide long-term investments to at least five underserved communities, increase mortgage and small-business lending in minority areas, and establish new branches in low- and moderate-income neighborhoods. This pledge is part of a broader trend among financial institutions responding to civil unrest and the disproportionate impact of the coronavirus pandemic on minority communities, with many other banks also committing substantial funds to similar efforts.

title: Deal of the Year: American Express buys Kabbage
summary: American Express acquired Kabbage's team, fintech products, data platform, and internet protocol for small businesses in a deal estimated between $750 million and $1 billion. This acquisition highlights both companies' strategies to expand beyond their traditional services, with Kabbage moving beyond lending into checking accounts and AmEx aiming to strengthen its small-business offerings and become more essential to its customers. The move by American Express follows similar acquisitions by Visa and Mastercard, demonstrating a broader trend in the payments industry to integrate data aggregation and expand services.

title: Moody’s revisa ratings de bancos como Bradesco, BB, Santander, Itaú e Caixa
summary: Moody's announced on December 11, 2020, that it revised the ratings of 28 Brazilian banks including Bradesco, Santander, Itaú Unibanco, BNDES, Caixa, and Banco do Brasil. The decision was primarily motivated by changes in the methodology for foreign and local currency ceilings, resulting in elevated long-term foreign currency deposit ratings for most banks. An exception was ING Bank N.V. (São Paulo), which saw its local currency classification downgraded.

title: Kevin Greenard: Ensure you have the maximum deposit insurance
summary: This article explains the different types of banking institutions in Canada, including Schedule I, II, and III banks, and credit unions, along with their respective deposit insurance protections provided by the Canadian Deposit Insurance Corporation (CDIC) and the Credit Union Deposit Insurance Corporation (CUDIC). It highlights the critical differences in coverage limits, especially for GICs, and advises investors, particularly those with credit union accounts, to be aware of how transitions to federal regulation can impact their insurance coverage. The author emphasizes the importance of structuring investments to maximize deposit insurance and avoid unnecessary risk exposure.

title: Huntington and TCF Financial to merge in $22 billion deal
summary: Huntington Bancshares and TCF Financial Corp. are merging in an all-stock deal valued at $22 billion, creating a regional bank expected to rank in the top 10 nationally. The Huntington brand will survive, and the combined company will maintain dual headquarters in Columbus, Ohio, and Detroit, with a significant commitment to Michigan including jobs and community investments. The merger is expected to close in the second quarter and result in approximately $490 million in cost savings.

title: Singapore’s Lim family, BP sued for US$313 million on oil deals
summary: Bank of China has sued BP Plc and the Lim family of collapsed trader Hin Leong for US$313 million over alleged fabricated oil deals. The bank claims BP withdrew US$125.7 million based on fictitious gasoil sales to Hin Leong and is also demanding US$187.2 million from Hin Leong's founder Lim Oon Kuin and his children for these and other overdue payments. BP refutes the allegations, while investigations reveal Hin Leong allegedly used forged documents and phantom cargoes to secure financing.

title: ‘Keep it simple’: Aditya Puri on HDFC Bank’s path to market leadership
summary: This interview with former HDFC Bank CEO Aditya Puri discusses how the bank achieved market leadership through customer-focused innovation and disciplined risk management. Puri emphasizes the importance of simplicity, a strong customer focus, and technology-led innovation while maintaining a "first among equals" culture. He shares insights into risk management strategies, adapting to the digital era, and empowering employees, highlighting the bank's consistent strong performance and future outlook for India.

title: BNY Mellon Wealth Management Announces Laura Kaplan as Market President in Miami, FL
summary: BNY Mellon Wealth Management has appointed Laura Kaplan as Market President in Miami, FL, to lead the region's wealth management practice. Kaplan, with extensive experience from Bank of America Private Bank, Deutsche Bank, and Citi Private Bank, will oversee client strategists, wealth managers, and support staff, reporting to Southeast President Kent Moegerle. This appointment aims to strengthen BNY Mellon's offerings for ultra-high-net-worth individuals and families in the Southeast market.

title: The IXUS ETF Puts the Whole World in Your Hands
summary: The article highlights the iShares Core MSCI Total International Stock ETF (IXUS) as a way to gain international exposure, especially with major banks forecasting a global economic rebound. IXUS tracks non-U.S. equities, offering low-cost access to developed and emerging markets for portfolio diversification. Financial institutions like Bank of America and Citigroup predict global GDP growth, emphasizing the role of fiscal stimulus and vaccines in recovery, despite an uneven timeline.

title: IHG faces junk rating as banks agree covenant waiver on $1.35bn of debt
summary: InterContinental Hotels Group (IHG) has secured its second loan covenant waiver and relaxation in 2020 on $1.35bn of debt, as its increasing leverage risks pushing its credit rating into junk status. The article indicates that full content access is restricted to subscribers.

title: 4D Molecular Therapeutics Announces Closing of Initial Public Offering and Full Exercise of Underwriters’ Option to Purchase Additional Shares
summary: 4D Molecular Therapeutics, Inc. announced the closing of its initial public offering, raising approximately $222 million, including the full exercise of the underwriters' option to purchase additional shares. The shares began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol “FDMT.” The company, a clinical-stage gene therapy firm, is focused on developing product candidates using targeted and evolved AAV vectors in ophthalmology, cardiology, and pulmonology.

title: Memo: Bank of America extends child-care benefits through the first quarter
summary: Bank of America is prolonging its child care benefits for employees until March 31, as revealed in an internal memo obtained by the Charlotte Business Journal. This extension affects the approximately 15,000 Bank of America employees located in the Charlotte region. The article highlights the bank's continued support for its workforce during challenging times.

title: Bancos fecham agências no Brasil no maior ritmo em três anos
summary: Os bancos brasileiros estão fechando agências no ritmo mais rápido em três anos, impulsionados pela pandemia de Covid-19 que acelerou o uso de canais digitais e intensificou a competição com fintechs. No período de 12 meses até novembro, foram fechadas 1.444 agências, representando um aumento de 78% em comparação com o ano anterior, o maior corte desde 2017. Essa adaptação tecnológica também resultou na eliminação de mais de 72.500 empregos bancários desde 2013, apesar dos investimentos significativos em tecnologia, gerando críticas sobre a distribuição dos lucros com a sociedade e os funcionários.

title: Vanguard makes history with first $1 trillion equity fund
summary: Vanguard's Total Stock Market Index Fund has become the first equity fund to surpass $1 trillion in assets, highlighting the growth of index-based investing. This milestone is attributed to rising U.S. stocks, falling fees, and increased investor education on fund fees and active management underperformance. The fund, which includes both a mutual fund and an ETF, was created in 1992 and the ETF has seen significant inflows.

title: Minera Zaldívar obtiene préstamo sindicado por 180 millones de dólares
summary: Compañía Minera Zaldívar, a subsidiary of Antofagasta Minerals, secured a $180 million syndicated loan from international financial institutions. The funds are earmarked for general corporate purposes. Legal advisors included Sullivan & Cromwell and Jara Del Favero Abogados for the borrower, and Philippi Prietocarrizosa Ferrero DU & Uria – Chile and Milbank for the lenders and administrative agent.

title: Jaime Guardiola, el banquero tenaz
summary: Jaime Guardiola, a banker with a long career at BBVA and later Sabadell, is highlighted for his tenacious leadership during turbulent financial times. He successfully expanded BBVA's international presence and, upon returning to Spain, transformed Sabadell into a top Spanish bank by acquiring distressed entities. Despite challenges like the TSB acquisition post-Brexit, his legacy includes pioneering solutions for mortgage defaults and leaving Sabadell in a leading position amidst new crises.

title: Morgan Stanley Hires Merrill ‘Growth’ Champ in California
summary: Morgan Stanley has recruited Benjamin J. Meyers, a 33-year-old financial advisor from Merrill Lynch in La Jolla, CA. Meyers, known for his aggressive cold-calling strategy, generated $1.5 million in annual revenue from a $200 million book and was a consistent recipient of Merrill's Excellence in Growth Award. His move signifies Morgan Stanley's continued active recruiting efforts, a practice they had previously paused, and highlights a debate within the industry regarding cold-calling effectiveness and wirehouse vs. RIA models.

title: How Aditya Puri built HDFC Bank, brick by brick
summary: This article features an exclusive conversation with Aditya Puri, the former CEO of HDFC Bank, detailing his 26-year tenure. Puri discusses his approach to leadership, institution-building, and change management, highlighting the bank's culture, customer focus, and strategic vision. He emphasizes that HDFC Bank's success was a collective effort and outlines future growth opportunities, particularly in semi-urban and rural India.

title: Wells Fargo hires former Bank of America executive Michelle Moore for digital banking role - Bizwomen
summary: Wells Fargo has hired former Bank of America executive Michelle Moore as its digital platform leader, effective December 31st. Moore will report to Ather Williams III and will be based in Charlotte, focusing on digital banking strategy and "digital experiences" within the consumer banking business. This hire aligns with Wells Fargo's emphasis on digital banking to reduce annual costs and build out a digital-first retail concept.

title: BofA Chairman of Global Corporate, Investment Banking to Depart
summary: Anne Clarke Wolff, Bank of America Corp.'s chairman of global corporate and investment banking, is leaving the firm. She plans to pursue a new career path, as confirmed by a memo from Matthew Koder, head of the investment-banking division. A company spokesman verified the memo's contents.

title: Trump’s long-time banker at Deutsche Bank resigns
summary: Donald Trump's long-time banker, Rosemary Vrablic, has resigned from Deutsche Bank, effective year-end. This departure comes as the German lender seeks to distance itself from the outgoing US president, to whose company Vrablic had arranged hundreds of millions of dollars in loans. Another colleague, Dominic Scalzi, also resigned.

title: Trump's personal banker resigns from Deutsche Bank
summary: Rosemary Vrablic, President Donald Trump's longtime personal banker at Deutsche Bank, has resigned, effective at year-end. Vrablic was instrumental in managing Trump's relationship with the German lender, which provided hundreds of millions of dollars in loans to his company, including for his Chicago tower. Her departure comes amidst scrutiny of her dealings, including a real estate transaction with a company linked to Jared Kushner.

title: Euronet Worldwide acquires BoI’s non-branch ATM fleet
summary: Euronet Worldwide Inc. has acquired Bank of Ireland's fleet of 700 non-branch ATMs in the Republic of Ireland, with the transfer of ownership set for February 28, 2021. Euronet will manage and upgrade the acquired network, rebranding it and integrating it with its existing ATMs in the region. This acquisition is part of Euronet's strategy to consolidate ATMs and expand product offerings, proving its role as a catalyst in ATM consolidation.

title: STI highlights from 2020
summary: The Straits Times Index (STI) experienced an 8% decline in 2020 through December 2nd, but its Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) saw significant growth, with combined assets under management (AUM) nearly doubling to S$2.08 billion. This growth was driven by increased investor participation, especially in the June and September quarters. The article also highlights the impact of new joiners like Keppel DC Reit and Mapletree Industrial Trust, and the cornerstone role of local banks, DBS, OCBC, and UOB, despite their initial declines.

title: Merrill Loses $2.8-Mln Producer to UBS, $2-Mln Team to Independence
summary: Merrill Lynch lost a $2.8 million producer to UBS Wealth Management USA in Louisiana and a $2 million team to Raymond James Financial's independent broker channel in New Jersey. The advisors cited frustration with Merrill's cross-selling mandates and annual account-growth targets tied to compensation. This move reflects a broader trend of advisors leaving Merrill and other wirehouses due to evolving business models.

title: Horarios de los bancos en Chile en Nochevieja y Año Nuevo: BancoEstado, BBVA, BCCH, Banco Chile...
summary: Banks in Chile will be closed on December 31st (Nochevieja) and January 1st (Año Nuevo) due to legal holidays for bank employees and the New Year's Day observance. Banking services will resume on Monday, January 4th, with normal operating hours. This article details the impact of these holiday closures on banking operations in Chile.

title: Arturo Tagle apunta a un cambio en el gobierno corporativo de BancoEstado
summary: Arturo Tagle, former president of BancoEstado, proposes significant changes to the bank's corporate governance, including modernizing its organic law from 1977. He emphasizes the need for a substantial capital increase to comply with Basel III regulations and to continue supporting underserved segments of the population and small businesses, as well as investing in new technologies. Tagle also commends the banking sector's prompt and effective response to the COVID-19 pandemic, noting their voluntary actions to assist clients.

title: Bank of America Profit Doubles After It Releases Reserves for Bad Loans
summary: Bank of America's first-quarter profit doubled to $8.05 billion after it released $2.7 billion in reserves previously set aside for bad loans, significantly beating analysts' expectations. This move, similar to those by JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Wells Fargo & Co., reflects increased optimism about an economic rebound. Despite higher trading revenue and investment banking fees boosting earnings, increased noninterest expenses, including one-time costs, led to a 2.9% drop in Bank of America's stock.

title: Stock Pickers Built These ETFs to Be More Nimble. They’re Off to a Slow Start. - WSJ
summary: New semitransparent active ETFs, designed to be more nimble and offer cheaper alternatives to mutual funds, are facing a slow rollout despite their innovative features. Major brokerages like Bank of America, UBS, and Wells Fargo are hesitant to offer them to wealth-management clients, citing the need for further scrutiny and long-term performance data.
