The article also provides historical dividend data and context regarding the PRA's previous directive to suspend bank dividends during the pandemic.

title: Firstrust, M&T participate in grant programs to help local small businesses
summary: Firstrust and M&T Bank are participating in grant programs designed to assist local small businesses in their expansion efforts. This initiative comes as several local banks are finding ways to provide assistance to businesses beyond the Paycheck Protection Program. The article highlights these banks' commitment to supporting the local business community.

title: Gap to Replace Longtime Credit-Card Issuer Synchrony With Barclays
summary: Gap Inc. is ending its 22-year partnership with Synchrony Financial, its longtime credit-card issuer, and moving its business to Barclays PLC. Barclays will now manage Gap's private-label and co-branded credit cards, including those for Athleta, Banana Republic, and Old Navy. The portfolio includes approximately 11 million open card accounts with a total balance of roughly $3.8 billion as of the end of March.

title: Morgan Stanley Drafts Merrill’s Willie Thomas for Menlo Park Post
summary: Morgan Stanley has hired William "Willie" Thomas, a former Merrill Lynch manager and NFL player, to lead its Menlo Park, California branch. Thomas previously oversaw Merrill's "Boca Tropics" market and will join Morgan Stanley after a garden leave, filling a role whose previous occupant, John Harsch, shifted to managing a private wealth branch. This move highlights Morgan Stanley's renewed recruiting efforts, contrasting with Merrill Lynch's focus on internal growth from its market executives.

title: CPI data Buy the Rumor Sell the Fact DXY EURUSD
summary: The article discusses the impact of the US March CPI data on the DXY and EUR/USD, noting that while the year-over-year figure was strong (2.6%), it was distorted by the low CPI prints from March-May of the previous year due to lockdowns. Traders anticipated this distortion, leading to a "buy the rumor, sell the fact" reaction. This resulted in the US Dollar Index (DXY) falling and EUR/USD rising immediately after the data release, despite the seemingly dramatic inflation jump.

title: CIBC CEO urges action on increasing rental housing supply
summary: CIBC CEO Victor Dodig emphasized the urgent need for increased housing supply in Canada, particularly rental stock, to address rising house prices and accommodate immigration. While supporting regulatory measures like toughening mortgage stress tests, Dodig stressed that long-term solutions lie in building more purpose-built rental housing and increasing density in urban areas. He also noted that low interest rates and generational wealth transfers contribute to the current housing market dynamics.

title: JPMorgan Chase’s mortgage margins narrow in Q1
summary: JPMorgan Chase saw its mortgage margins narrow in the first quarter of 2021 despite a 21% increase in originations over the previous quarter. Production revenue from mortgage fees declined, and gain-on-sale margins fell significantly due to market factors and a shift towards lower-margin correspondent lending. CEO Jamie Dimon anticipates a "Goldilocks moment" for the economy.

title: Goldman, JPMorgan Traders Show the Reddit Crowd How It’s Done
summary: Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase & Co. reported massive revenue windfalls from trading and dealmaking, kicking off bank earnings season with surprisingly strong results. Despite predictions that good times for Wall Street were over, particularly after retail investor activity early in the year, these major banks demonstrated their continued profitability. The strong performance was partly fueled by the renewed optimism of small investors.

title: Consumers Shifted Credit Payment Behaviors in the U.S. and Other Global Markets as a Result of COVID-19
summary: A TransUnion Global Payment Hierarchy study revealed that the COVID-19 pandemic significantly altered consumer credit payment behaviors in the U.S. and other global markets. The study found that consumers prioritized different credit products during the pandemic, with mortgage payments becoming paramount in the U.S. and credit cards gaining importance in various regions, especially for those with limited card access. These shifts highlight the critical role of accessible credit and the impact of economic crises on financial decision-making.

title: BofA Shares Slide as Tepid Loan Growth Counters Trading Bonanza
summary: Bank of America (BAC) saw its shares decline by as much as 4.2% despite strong performance from its trading and investment banking divisions. This drop was attributed to a decrease in loan balances and higher-than-expected pandemic-related costs, which outweighed the revenue surge from trading and banking fees. The bank also released $2.7 billion of reserves, signaling an improving economic outlook.

title: Bank of America management offers optimistic outlook on economy, reserves
summary: Bank of America executives expressed an optimistic outlook for economic growth, citing strong consumer spending and financial markets after better-than-expected first-quarter profits. The bank released $2.7 billion in loan loss reserves and expects to release more as the economy improves, despite challenges from low interest rates and one-off expenses. Analysts remain positive on the bank’s future growth prospects, anticipating a rise in net interest income.

title: KKR-backed AppLovin raises $2 billion in U.S. IPO at over $28 billion valuation
summary: Mobile app and gaming company AppLovin Corp successfully priced its initial public offering at $80 per share, raising $2 billion and valuing the company at $28.64 billion. Backed by KKR & Co Inc, AppLovin is listing on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol "APP." This IPO highlights the surging demand for video games during the COVID-19 pandemic, with AppLovin boasting over 410 million daily active users and more than 200 free-to-play mobile games.

title: Bank of America Profit Doubles After It Releases Reserves for Bad Loans
summary: Bank of America announced its profit doubled in the first quarter of the year, reaching $8.05 billion, largely due to releasing reserves previously set aside for bad loans. This marks a significant increase from $4.01 billion a year prior when banks were building up reserves at the start of the pandemic. The first-quarter results surpassed analysts' expectations, despite revenue remaining flat.

title: Bank of America Profit Doubles After It Releases Reserves for Bad Loans
summary: Bank of America announced a doubling of its profit in the first quarter of the year, reaching $8.05 billion, largely due to releasing reserves previously set aside for potential bad loans. This performance significantly surpassed its earnings of $4.01 billion from a year prior, when banks were heavily provisioning for the economic impact of the pandemic. While profits soared, the bank's revenue remained flat, beating analysts' expectations.

title: Morgan Stanley had $911 million in first-quarter losses tied to Archegos fund meltdown
summary: Morgan Stanley reported a nearly $1 billion loss in the first quarter of 2021 stemming from its prime brokerage relationship with Bill Hwang's Archegos Capital Management. The loss included $644 million from a "credit event" and an additional $267 million in related trading losses as the firm rapidly de-risked its positions. CEO James Gorman defended the decision to quickly unwind positions as "necessary and money well spent," while CFO Jon Pruzan suggested the bank might have been misled by Archegos.

title: Northern Trust to launch FX trading engine in Singapore
summary: Northern Trust is set to launch an electronic FX pricing and trading engine in Singapore, becoming the latest major bank to join the Monetary Authority of Singapore's (MAS) initiative to develop the region into a global FX trading hub. This move expands Northern Trust's FX solutions in Asia-Pacific, following prior efforts to grow its FX trading business through acquisitions and partnerships with firms like BEx and Lumint. The new eFX platform aims to benefit regional market participants with improved speed, enhanced pricing discovery, and more efficient execution.

title: Bank of America CEO Moynihan says supports ‘a well-focused infrastructure plan’ - CNN interview
summary: Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan stated in a CNN interview that he supports a "well-focused infrastructure plan" for the U.S. He also commented on the potential impact of a 28 percent corporate tax rate, noting it would depend on the new tax law's details.

title: Bank of America tops charts with $15 billion bond deal, the biggest ever from a bank
summary: Bank of America Corp. raised $15 billion in the corporate bond market, marking the largest bond deal ever issued by a bank. This six-part sale surpassed a previous record and saw strong investor demand, allowing for a reduction in interest rate spreads.

title: Citibank: Why one of the world's largest and most iconic banks is wrapping up its retail business in India
summary: Citigroup announced its plan to exit the retail banking business in India, a market it has been in for 119 years. This move is part of the bank's global strategy to reallocate resources to higher-returning opportunities in wealth management and institutional businesses in four key locations (Singapore, Hong Kong, UAE, London). The exit also reflects the intense competition faced by foreign banks in India from domestic heavyweights, and comes amidst a trend of other foreign banks scaling back or leaving the Indian market due to high capital and regulatory requirements.

title: Bank of America to Set Record for Largest Bank Bond Sale at $15 Billion
summary: Bank of America is preparing to issue $15 billion in bonds, which would be the largest bond sale ever by a bank. This move comes shortly after JPMorgan Chase & Co. set a record with a $13 billion bond offering. The significant investor demand, totaling around $25 billion, suggests BofA will secure favorable borrowing rates.

title: Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, and JPMorgan Chase Had Huge Bond Sales
summary: Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, and JPMorgan Chase conducted significant bond sales this week, capitalizing on a decrease in Treasury yields. JPMorgan Chase alone issued $13 billion in bonds. These sales occurred following their earnings reports, indicating a strategic move to raise capital in a favorable market.

title: Morgan Stanley reveals $911 million Archegos loss as profit jumps
summary: Morgan Stanley reported a $911 million loss due to the collapse of Archegos Capital Management, which impacted its first-quarter profit, despite a 150% overall jump fueled by strong trading and deal-making. The bank lost $644 million from selling Archegos-related stocks and $267 million in derisking efforts. While the Archegos event overshadowed its otherwise stellar performance, Morgan Stanley's profit comfortably beat expectations thanks to record capital markets activity and an unprecedented boom in dealmaking.

title: Broadway Financial Completes Merger to Create Largest Black-Owned Bank in the US
summary: Broadway Financial Corp. completed its merger with Washington, D.C.-based CFC Banc Corp. on April 1, forming CityFirstBroadway, now the largest Black-led bank in the U.S. with over $1 billion in assets. The new institution plans to expand commercial lending, develop affordable housing, and offer loans to small businesses in underserved urban areas. This merger occurred despite a significant decline in the number of Black-owned financial institutions nationwide.

title: Bank of America looks to expand Leader on Loan program in new markets
summary: Bank of America is planning to expand its "Leader on Loan" program into new markets. This program allows bank executives to assist local organizations, leveraging their business expertise for community benefit. The expansion aims to accelerate work at various non-profit and community-focused groups.

title: XPO Logistics Announces Mark Manduca as Chief Investment Officer for GXO Logistics Spin-Off
summary: XPO Logistics announced the appointment of Mark Manduca as Chief Investment Officer for GXO Logistics, its intended spin-off logistics business. Manduca will be responsible for analyzing GXO's growth opportunities, optimizing its asset portfolio, overseeing UK pension investments, and communicating GXO's investment case globally. He brings extensive experience as a top-ranked European transport research analyst from leading investment banks.

title: Herman Miller, Knoll $1.8B deal to create furniture leader
summary: Herman Miller Inc. announced its acquisition of Knoll Inc. for $1.8 billion in a cash-and-stock deal. This merger aims to bolster Herman Miller's market position as offices globally prepare for employees' return, and as companies reconfigure workspaces for social distancing or permanent work-from-home setups. The combined entity will boast 19 brands and operate across over 100 countries.

title: U.S. Banks: Goldman Sachs reveals Black workforce numbers for the first time
summary: For the first time, Goldman Sachs has released detailed numbers on its Black workforce in the U.S. The report, part of its sustainability efforts, shows that 24 Black men and 25 Black women are among the 1,548 U.S. executives, senior officials, and managers, accounting for 6.8% of the total U.S. workforce, a slight increase from the previous year. CEO David Solomon acknowledged that there is "still a long road ahead" but committed to making diversity a personal priority.

title: Barclays Drops $630 Million Prison Finance Deal After Pressure from Investors and Sustainability Orgs
summary: Barclays has withdrawn from a $630 million municipal bond deal for private prison company CoreCivic Inc. and the State of Alabama. This decision followed intense pressure from sustainability organizations and investors who highlighted the financial and reputational risks associated with financing private prisons, particularly given Barclays' prior commitment not to do so. The American Sustainable Business Council and Social Venture Circle, among others, lauded Barclays' withdrawal, emphasizing their continued advocacy against investments supporting mass incarceration and human rights abuses.

title: XPO Logistics Announces Mark Manduca as Chief Investment Officer for GXO Logistics Spin-Off
summary: XPO Logistics announced that Mark Manduca will serve as Chief Investment Officer for GXO Logistics, its logistics business spin-off. Manduca, previously a top-ranked European transport research analyst, will be responsible for analyzing GXO's growth opportunities, optimizing its asset portfolio, and overseeing UK pension investments. This appointment comes as XPO prepares to spin off GXO Logistics as a separate, publicly-traded company in the second half of 2021.

title: Recursion Pharmaceuticals Announces Closing of Initial Public Offering
summary: Recursion Pharmaceuticals announced the closing of its initial public offering on April 20, 2021, which included the full exercise of the underwriters' option to purchase additional shares. The company sold 27,878,787 shares of Class A common stock at $18.00 per share, generating gross proceeds of $501.8 million. The shares began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol "RXRX" on April 16, 2021.

title: S&P Global Market Intelligence Global Bank Ranking Reveals World's Largest Banks Unscathed by COVID-19 Pandemic
summary: S&P Global Market Intelligence's annual Global Bank Ranking found that the world's largest banks, particularly those in Asia Pacific and China, remained largely unaffected by the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. The number of banks with over $1 trillion in assets increased from 29 to 39, with Chinese banks benefiting from a swift economic recovery. While Asian banks continue to dominate the top five, U.S.-based JPMorgan Chase & Co. and French BNP Paribas SA saw significant asset growth, with newly added banks like State Street Corp. and Canadian Desjardins Group entering the top 100 list.

title: KnowBe4 Announces Pricing of Initial Public Offering
summary: KnowBe4, Inc. announced the pricing of its initial public offering of 9,500,000 shares of Class A common stock at $16.00 per share. The company is offering 9,000,000 shares, with selling stockholders offering 500,000 shares. The shares are expected to begin trading on Nasdaq under the symbol "KNBE" on April 22, 2021.

title: El BBVA plantea despedir a 3.798 empleados y el cierre de 530 oficinas
summary: BBVA plans to lay off 3,798 employees and close 530 branches due to digital transformation aimed at ensuring competitiveness and sustainability. This move has been met with strong opposition from trade unions, who are calling for mobilization. The bank's plan affects its central services and branch network, with similar large-scale layoffs also announced by other Spanish banks like CaixaBank, Santander, and Sabadell, totaling around 19,000 dismissals in the sector.

title: National Grid Is Said to Pick Banks for $7 Billion Gas Asset Sale
summary: National Grid Plc has reportedly hired Barclays Plc, Goldman Sachs Group Inc., and Robey Warshaw LLP to advise on the sale of a majority stake in its gas grid business. This stake could be valued at up to 5 billion pounds ($6.9 billion). The move comes as the utility prepares for a low-carbon future, utilizing the same advisors who recently assisted in its largest-ever acquisition.

title: As Ally makes big move in uptown Charlotte, online bank sees more growth ahead
summary: Ally Financial is solidifying its presence in Charlotte with the debut of the Ally Charlotte Center, consolidating multiple offices into one hub. The $182 billion financial-services company's move signifies its growth and establishment as a major player in the region, joining other large banks on Tryon Street. This expansion is part of Ally's continued strategy for growth, including in areas like auto lending and innovation labs.

title: When Truist, Bank of America, Wells Fargo and others are bringing employees back to the office
summary: Major financial institutions like Truist, Bank of America, and Wells Fargo are planning to bring employees back to their offices. The transition to on-site work is expected to commence in the summer and continue through the fall for most large financial-services companies in the region. This move signifies a shift back from remote work arrangements adopted during the pandemic.

title: KKR-backed KnowBe4 valued at over $3.5 bln in strong Nasdaq debut
summary: Cybersecurity firm KnowBe4 Inc, backed by private equity firm KKR & Co Inc, made a strong Nasdaq debut with its shares opening nearly 25% above their offer price, valuing the company at over $3.5 billion. The company, which specializes in simulating phishing attacks and security awareness training, priced its offering of 9.5 million shares at $16 each, raising $152 million. This successful IPO reflects the increased demand for cybersecurity services during the COVID-19 pandemic as more employees work remotely.

title: Wells Fargo to close two locations in Philadelphia area to help cut costs
summary: Wells Fargo is closing 24 bank locations nationwide, including two in the Philadelphia area (King of Prussia Mall and Villanova University), as part of a cost-cutting measure to save billions. This move follows similar closures by other banks like PNC and TD Bank, driven by an increase in mobile and online banking rather than solely the COVID-19 pandemic. Wells Fargo CEO Charles Scharf aims to reduce annual expenses by at least $10 billion.

title: Bradesco (BBDC4) institui novo programa de recompra de 97,1 mi de ações
summary: Bradesco (BBDC4) announced a new share buyback program, revoking an earlier one. The new program authorizes the acquisition of up to 97.190.795 shares (both ordinary and preferred) by April 26 of the following year, representing 1% of the total shares in circulation. The bank aims to use existing Profit Reserve funds for the buyback, which is expected to increase shareholder returns and demonstrates confidence in its capital position.

title: Timothy Baker Obituary - Ogdensburg, NY
summary: Timothy J. "Tim" Baker of Ogdensburg, NY, a 14-year pancreatic cancer survivor, passed away on April 24, 2021. He had a distinguished career at St. Lawrence National Bank, retiring in 2016 as Senior Vice President, and was very active in numerous local organizations including the Knights of Columbus, Elks Club, and youth sports. He is survived by his wife Shannon Kelly, siblings, and many nieces and nephews, and a Mass of Christian Burial will be held on April 28.

title: Sunday Summary: Marc Holliday Believes 2021 Office Life Will Be Off the Hook!
summary: SL Green Realty CEO Marc Holliday is optimistic about the return to office life in 2021, citing a "vast reawakening" in New York. One Vanderbilt is 77% leased, with an expectation of reaching 90% by year-end. The article also highlights other positive developments in real estate, including retail rent recovery and proptech investments, despite some setbacks like foreclosures for Aby Rosen's properties.

title: Bank of Hawaii achieves record earnings, deposits and assets
summary: Bank of Hawaii Corp. reported record earnings, deposits, and assets in the first quarter of 2021, driven by a release of $14.3 million from its loan-loss reserve and an anticipated economic recovery in Hawaii. The bank's net income rose to $59.9 million, with earnings per share of $1.50, exceeding analyst estimates. Bankoh also saw record high deposits of $19.56 billion and assets of $21.95 billion, while continuing to invest in digital banking services.

title: Just released – these are the world's biggest banks
summary: A new report from S&P Global Market Intelligence has revealed the world's 100 biggest banks, with China's Industrial & Commercial Bank of China Ltd. retaining the top spot. The report also details how Australia's major banks, including Commonwealth Bank of Australia, ANZ, Westpac, and National Australia Bank, ranked globally, noting shifts in their positions compared to the previous year. JPMorgan Chase & Co. reclaimed its position as the sixth-largest financial institution, surpassing HSBC Holdings.

title: Walker & Dunlop Jumps to Fourth Largest Lender to Commercial Real Estate
summary: Walker & Dunlop, Inc. announced it has become the fourth largest lender to the U.S. commercial real estate industry, according to 2020 Mortgage Bankers Association rankings. The company has achieved a 25% compound annual growth rate in lending volume over the last decade, reaching $24.7 billion in 2020, and was also recognized as the largest provider of capital to the multifamily sector. CEO Willy Walker attributes this success to recruiting top talent, investing in technology, and strategic brand growth, positioning the company for continued expansion despite its smaller size compared to larger competitors.

title: BofA Hit Hardest as EU Fines Bond-Trading Trio $34 Million
summary: The European Union fined Bank of America, Credit Suisse, and Credit Agricole a total of 28.5 million euros ($34 million) for colluding in bond-trading chatrooms. Bank of America received the largest penalty, while Deutsche Bank avoided a fine by being the first to report the illegal activity. The collusion involved U.S. supra-sovereign, sovereign, and agency bonds.

title: Safehold Announces Pricing of $400 Million of 2.800% Senior Unsecured Notes Due 2031
summary: Safehold Inc. announced that its operating partnership has priced a public offering of $400 million in 2.800% senior notes due 2031. The notes were priced at 99.127% of the principal amount and are expected to settle on May 7, 2021. The net proceeds will be used to repay borrowings and for general corporate purposes, including ground lease investments.

title: Bank of America's 'Erica' trademark win partly upheld by 10th Circuit
summary: The 10th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals partly upheld Bank of America's trademark win for its ERICA mobile banking assistant, ruling it did not infringe on one of Erik Underwood's trademarks and upholding the cancellation of another. However, the court remanded a decision regarding Underwood's "E.R.I.C.A." mark, stating the lower court applied the wrong standard and Underwood may still have protectable rights. The ruling clarifies the criteria for trademark "use in commerce" under the Lanham Act.

title: Cinépolis ‘ve la luz’: recibe nuevo crédito (de BBVA, Santander y HSBC) y reestructura deuda
summary: Cinépolis, Mexico's largest cinema chain, has secured a deal to restructure over $1 billion in debt and receive $300 million in new financing from banks including BBVA, Santander, and HSBC. The controlling family also contributed $100 million. This move aims to help the company recover from the pandemic's impact, which severely affected global cinema operations.

title: KKR Signs Lease at San Francisco Tower Vornado Owns With Trump
summary: KKR & Co has renewed its lease for office space at a San Francisco tower located at 555 California St., which is co-owned by Vornado Realty Trust and the Trump Organization. This renewal, along with those from Bank of America Corp. and Goldman Sachs Group Inc., has brought the 52-story building's occupancy rate to 98%. Vornado Realty Trust reported this information during its recent earnings call.

title: ACT IPO News - Mortgage insurance spinoff Enact Holdings sets terms for $497 million IPO
summary: Enact Holdings, a mortgage insurance company being spun out of Genworth Financial, announced terms for its $497 million IPO. The company plans to offer 22.6 million shares at a price range of $20 to $24, valuing the company at $3.6 billion at the midpoint. Enact, which is a leading private mortgage insurance provider in the US, generated $1.1 billion in sales for the 12 months ended December 31, 2020, and is expected to list on Nasdaq under the symbol ACT.

title: World’s Best Banks 2021: North America
summary: North American banks demonstrated resilience and innovation in 2020 amid the challenges posed by the Covid-19 pandemic. Royal Bank of Canada was recognized as the overall Best Bank in North America for its customer service and technological advancements, while Bank of America maintained its position as Best Bank in the United States by enhancing digital capabilities and client experience. Butterfield Bank was named Best Bank in Bermuda, highlighting its conservative underwriting and diversified portfolio.

title: Inside Volatility Trading: The Constant Change of Volatility
summary: This article discusses the nature of volatility in capital markets, emphasizing it as a constant measure of change, despite being often misunderstood and associated with negative outcomes. It highlights the recent decrease in broad market volatility and VIX Index levels, draws parallels to historical market events, and explores potential risks in the Commercial Real Estate sector post-COVID-19. The author also touches upon the technical aspects of volatility trading, the surge in investment fund inflows, and broader economic shifts.

title: BofA Promotes Brunner, Farman to Run M&A Amid Deal Windfall
summary: Bank of America Corp. has appointed Kevin Brunner and Ivan Farman as co-heads of its global mergers and acquisitions business. These promotions follow a record surge in investment-banking fees for the company. Brunner and Farman previously led the M&A business for BofA in the Americas.

title: MP Materials (MP) Is an Attractive Play on Rare Earths
summary: MP Materials (MP) is presented as an attractive long-term investment due to its position as the largest rare-earth materials producer outside of China. The article discusses why the stock has fallen recently despite strong earnings and highlights the strategic importance of rare earths, especially given global reliance on China. It also includes analyst ratings and a price prediction, suggesting a significant upside.

title: Dasa realiza IPO e capta R$ 3,3 bi
summary: Dasa, Brazil's largest laboratory network, completed an Initial Public Offering (IPO) on April 9, 2021, raising R$ 3.3 billion by selling over 57 million ordinary shares at R$ 58 each. The funds will be allocated for organic and inorganic growth, including the acquisition of Grupo Leforte and for working capital. Legal firms like Simpson Thacher & Bartlett, Mattos Filho, Davis Polk & Wardwell, and Machado Meyer Advogados advised on the transaction.

title: Hilton and Its Board Made False Statements to Shareholders About Diamond Resorts Acquisition, Lawsuit Claims
summary: A lawsuit has been filed against Hilton Grand Vacations Inc. and its board of directors, alleging false statements and misleading information provided to shareholders regarding the acquisition of Diamond Resorts International. The lead plaintiff, Marina Clough, claims that a proxy statement omitted and misrepresented critical financial projections, analyses from Bank of America Securities, and potential conflicts of interest, thereby violating the Securities Exchange Act. The lawsuit seeks an enjoinment, damages, and legal fees, arguing that shareholders were deprived of necessary information to assess the transaction properly.

title: Evelyn Varner Named Head of Advice Enablement for Wells Fargo Wealth & Investment Management (WIM)
summary: Wells Fargo & Company has appointed Evelyn Varner as the head of Advice Enablement for its Wealth & Investment Management (WIM) division. In this new role, Varner will be responsible for developing the vision and execution strategy for how advice is delivered across WIM, focusing on digitally-enabled, holistic, and goals-based advice. She will work with various client-facing businesses within WIM and utilize her 16 years of experience in the financial services industry to enhance advisor and client experiences.

title: Rockefeller zeroes in on Merrill Lynch, Morgan Stanley advisers
summary: Rockefeller Capital Management, led by CEO Greg Fleming, has predominantly recruited financial advisors from Fleming's former firms, Merrill Lynch and Morgan Stanley, since its launch in 2018. Over 74% of its new advisors have come from these two wirehouses, totaling 105 out of 142 hires. The firm is actively expanding across the U.S. and attracts elite advisors with competitive compensation packages, including high recruiting bonuses, while offering more control and flexibility compared to larger institutions.

title: Oatly Group AB Launches Initial Public Offering
summary: Oatly Group AB announced the commencement of its initial public offering, consisting of 84,376,000 American Depositary Shares (ADSs) offered by the company and selling shareholders. The estimated price per share is between $15.00 and $17.00, and the ADSs will be listed on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol "OTLY." Morgan Stanley, J.P. Morgan, and Credit Suisse are acting as lead book-running managers for the offering.

title: Local Bank of America exec Charles Bowman shifts roles as part of retirement plan
summary: Bank of America executive Charles Bowman has transitioned roles, stepping down as Charlotte market president but retaining his position as North Carolina president, as he prepares for retirement in 2022. Kieth Cockrell will take over as Charlotte market president. This move is part of his long-term retirement plan, following almost 15 years in the Charlotte market president role.

title: JPMorgan Is America’s Largest Company In 2021, But Amazon Is Rising In The Ranks
summary: Despite a pandemic, America's largest companies grew significantly in 2021, with JPMorgan Chase maintaining its position as the largest for the third consecutive year. Meanwhile, Amazon climbed into the top five, reflecting the growing importance of e-commerce, while traditional giants like AT&T and ExxonMobil saw significant drops in rankings. This year's Global 2000 ranking illustrates the resilience and shifts within the U.S. corporate landscape amidst economic volatility.

title: Centerview Hires Three BofA Bankers in Technology Push
summary: Centerview Partners has reportedly hired three senior Bank of America investment bankers, including co-head Jack MacDonald, to bolster its technology sector team. This move also includes experienced technology bankers Steve Miller and Gary Kirkham, indicating Centerview's strategic push into the technology investment banking space.

title: On Bitcoin’s Energy Consumption
summary: This article quantitatively analyzes Bitcoin's energy consumption, comparing it to the gold industry and the traditional banking system. It argues that while Bitcoin's energy use is substantial, it is verifiable and serves to secure the network, offering financial freedom and potential benefits to the energy sector. The piece concludes that given Bitcoin's utility and the inherent subjectivity of energy value judgments, its energy consumption is acceptable.

title: Bank of America reaches $75 mln settlement over excessive fees
summary: Bank of America has agreed to a $75 million settlement in a class-action lawsuit accusing it of charging excessive overdraft fees. The settlement addresses charges for repeatedly attempting to process single transactions, and as part of the agreement, the bank will cease imposing multiple fees on "retry" payments for at least five years, saving customers an estimated $318 million.

title: Bank of America names Harlem native Tavarez president of New York City
summary: Bank of America has appointed Harlem native Jose Tavarez as president of Bank of America New York City and Westchester County. Tavarez has been with the bank for 25 years. This move highlights Bank of America's continued strategic appointments in key regional markets.

title: Reputation rankings show Wells Fargo's massive rehabilitation campaign may have worked
summary: Wells Fargo's significant public rehabilitation campaign launched in 2018 appears to have successfully improved its reputation. After hitting historic lows in ethics scores following a series of scandals, the bank's reputation has recovered considerably, though it still lags behind some competitors. This improvement is part of a broader trend of banks generally seeing improved public perception, despite remaining largely "unloved."

title: YPF Energía Eléctrica canjea obligaciones por 100 millones de dólares
summary: YPF Energía Eléctrica (YPF Luz) completed a debt swap, issuing new Class VI negotiable obligations for $14.6 million at a fixed annual rate of 10.24% to refinance existing Class I obligations with a capital balance of $100 million. The offer, which received a 45.34% acceptance rate from holders, was advised by Estudio O'Farrell and internal lawyers for the issuer, and Tanoira Cassagne Abogados for the placing banks. The proceeds will be used for refinancing liabilities, capital contributions in controlled companies, physical assets, and working capital in Argentina.

title: Protecting security and privacy in the coming open-banking world
summary: Symcor, a company with a long history of supporting Canadian industries through digital transformations and addressing industry-wide needs, is uniquely positioned to help advance open banking in Canada. The company emphasizes its expertise in secure data exchange and its ability to align various stakeholders to provide trusted digital solutions, particularly as the market moves towards a "Made in Canada" open-banking framework. Symcor highlights its focus on security and agility, leveraging its core competencies to ensure trust and mitigate fraud in the evolving data economy.

title: Personalities of Pittsburgh: John H. Montgomery on becoming CEO at Community Bank during the pandemic
summary: John H. Montgomery became CEO of Community Bank (CB Financial Services Inc.) during the pandemic, a significant leadership change. The article discusses his Pittsburgh ties and his perspective on the evolving banking landscape. It also includes related articles concerning local bank activities in the Pittsburgh area.

title: XMLV: Shedding Volatility in the Market's 'Sweet Spot'
summary: The Invesco S&P MidCap Low Volatility ETF (XMLV) offers investors reduced volatility in the mid-cap segment, which has historically outperformed other market caps. Mid-caps are considered the market's "sweet spot" due to their strong economic contributions and responsiveness to GDP growth. XMLV's focus on low-volatility mid-cap stocks, particularly in cyclical sectors like financial services, industrials, and materials, positions it well for continued economic expansion.

title: Carver Federal Savings Bank's Customers Can Now Access Wells Fargo's Nationwide Network of ATMs
summary: Carver Federal Savings Bank announced that its customers can now make surcharge-free withdrawals at Wells Fargo's nationwide ATM network, effective immediately. This partnership provides Carver customers with increased access to their money at over 80,000 ATMs worldwide when combined with the Allpoint ATM Network. This initiative is part of Wells Fargo's broader commitment to invest in Minority Depository Institutions and foster economic growth in African-American communities.

title: BofA Joins Paxos Blockchain Stock-Settlement Network
summary: Bank of America Corp. has joined Paxos Trust Co.'s blockchain network to settle stock trades in minutes, marking a significant step in Wall Street's adoption of blockchain technology. This move makes BofA the largest addition to the Paxos Settlement Service, which previously included Credit Suisse Group AG and Nomura Holdings Inc.’s Instinet. The initiative aims to modernize equity trade settlement, potentially challenging traditional systems by enabling near real-time transactions.

title: Berkshire sheds nearly all of Wells Fargo, a holding since 1989
summary: Berkshire Hathaway has divested almost all of its Wells Fargo shares, ending a 31-year investment that was once highly successful but was tarnished by customer mistreatment scandals. The holding, which was worth $32 billion in 2018, is now down to $26.4 million. Warren Buffett cited the bank's "dumb" incentive system and slow response to problems as reasons for the divestment, though Berkshire maintains holdings in other banks like Bank of America.

title: Dime Community Bank Scores New York Islanders & UBS Arena Partnership
summary: Dime Community Bank announced a partnership to become the official retail and commercial bank of the New York Islanders and the new UBS Arena at Belmont Park. As a founding partner of UBS Arena, Dime will also have its name on the arena's largest private club, The Dime Club. This collaboration offers unique access and benefits for Dime customers and employees, strengthening the bank's presence across its New York City/Long Island network.

title: Investors Are Most Overweight European Stocks in BofA Survey
summary: A Bank of America survey reveals that fund managers overseeing $592 billion in assets are now most overweight European stocks globally, marking the highest exposure since 2018. Euro-area stocks surpassed emerging markets as the top favorite, while UK equities also saw increased allocation. Conversely, investor allocation to US stocks declined.

title: Bank of America to Raise U.S. Minimum Hourly Wage to $25 by 2025 - WSJ
summary: Bank of America announced plans to increase its hourly minimum wage to $25 by 2025, which would position it above its major banking counterparts and help address worker shortages. Furthermore, the bank will require all its U.S. vendors to pay employees dedicated to the bank at least $15 an hour. This move aligns with broader discussions around minimum wage increases and their economic impact.

title: Bank of America, NACA commit to $15B in mortgages for low- to moderate-income buyers by 2027
summary: Bank of America and the Neighborhood Assistance Corp. of America (NACA) have announced a commitment to provide $15 billion in mortgages for low- to moderate-income homebuyers by May 2027. This expanded partnership aims to support affordable homeownership.

title: JPMorgan Achieves Carbon Neutrality in Operations, Sets Carbon Reduction Financing Targets for High Emitting Sectors
summary: JPMorgan Chase announced it achieved carbon neutrality in its operations for 2020 and established new 2030 carbon intensity targets for high-emitting sectors like Oil & Gas, Electric Power, and Auto Manufacturing. These targets are part of its commitment to align financing activities with the Paris Agreement and facilitate $2.5 trillion in sustainable finance over the next decade. The company also outlined new sustainability goals for its own operations, including reducing greenhouse gas emissions and water consumption.

title: Ana Botin and Andrea Orcel come face to face in Santander court battle
summary: A court battle has begun in Madrid between Santander chairman Ana Botín and former UBS banker Andrea Orcel over Santander's decision to not hire Orcel as CEO. Botín argued that Orcel never received a formal contract because terms were still being discussed, while Orcel is suing for tens of millions of euros in lost pay. The case was paused after UBS witnesses failed to appear.

title: Cuatrecasas asesora a Banco Santander y otras entidades financieras en la novación de la financiación ICO de Tendam
summary: Cuatrecasas has advised Banco Santander and a syndicate of financial institutions on the novation of Tendam Retail's ICO financing. This agreement refinances a €132.5 million loan, extending its maturity by three years to 2026, under government measures to support business solvency during the COVID-19 pandemic. The legal team from Cuatrecasas included Miguel Cruz Ropero, Rafael Mínguez Prieto, and Nuria Burillo Llorente, who represented the financial entities involved.

title: Bank of America names leaders as it adjusts operations in consumer and small business unit
summary: Bank of America is reorganizing its consumer and small business unit to a new model it believes will offer more comprehensive client service. As part of these operational adjustments, the company has named new leaders for the unit. This move aims to enhance client experience and service delivery within these key segments.

title: Deutsche Bank Taps BofA Alums for Asia Investment Banking
summary: Deutsche Bank has hired three new bankers for its Asia Pacific investment banking team, including two former Bank of America employees. Zonia Lau will lead healthcare coverage for China, and David Hopwood will head natural resources in Australia, strengthening the bank's sector-specific expertise in the region.

title: EU fines UBS, Nomura, UniCredit $452 mln over bond cartel
summary: The European Union has fined UBS, Nomura, and UniCredit 371 million euros ($452 million) for their involvement in a European government bond trading cartel that operated between 2007 and 2011. Traders from these banks, along with Bank of America, RBS (NatWest), Natixis, and WestLB, allegedly shared information on prices and volumes before bond auctions via Bloomberg chatrooms. While the three fined banks plan to appeal the decision, NatWest avoided a penalty by alerting the EU competition watchdog.

title: KeyCorp's Share Price Has More than Doubled Over the Last Year. Is There Any More Upside?
summary: KeyCorp's stock has seen significant growth in the past year, with earnings projected to be strong in 2021 due to lower credit expenses and robust investment banking activity. While the current valuation suggests some upside, factors like loan growth uncertainty and analysts' expectations for a dip in 2022 earnings could temper long-term projections. However, the bank's digital platform, Laurel Road, offers a potential catalyst for future growth and valuation by capitalizing on a differentiated strategy.

title: Big banks look for post-pandemic rebound of credit card revenue
summary: Major U.S. banks are anticipating a rebound in credit card revenue as pandemic restrictions ease and stimulus payments end. Lenders like Capital One, Citigroup, and JPMorgan are increasing promotions and easing credit standards to encourage spending, particularly in travel and entertainment, after card balances declined during the pandemic. This strategic shift aims to capitalize on renewed consumer activity, as credit cards remain a highly profitable business for banks despite high APRs.

title: Bank of America’s Merrill Lynch to ban trainee brokers from making cold calls
summary: Bank of America's Merrill Lynch Wealth Management unit is implementing a new adviser-training program that will prohibit trainee brokers from making cold calls, a long-standing practice in the industry. Instead, trainees will be directed to use internal referrals or LinkedIn for client acquisition, reflecting a shift towards digital prospecting. This change aims to modernize client outreach, improve completion rates for the training program, and better integrate Merrill's advisers with Bank of America's broader customer base.

title: Fincrime Briefing: Congress scrutinizes Deutsche Bank on AML, fines fuel EU de-risking, malware hijacks crypto blockchain, and more
summary: This Fincrime Briefing covers several key financial crime topics including a U.S. congressional probe into Deutsche Bank's AML controls, a wave of EU bank fines leading to de-risking, and a new malware strain hijacking Bitcoin's blockchain for resilience. The article details instances of alleged money laundering, the impact of regulatory crackdowns on banks' willingness to engage with high-risk regions, and the evolving tactics of cybercriminals using decentralized networks.

title: Goldman Sachs Adds Kimberley Harris as Sixth Woman on Board of Directors
summary: Goldman Sachs announced the appointment of media lawyer Kimberley Harris to its board of directors, increasing the number of women on its board to six out of thirteen. This move aligns with the financial industry's growing push for diversity and Goldman's internal targets to elevate women into senior leadership roles. Harris brings extensive experience from NBCUniversal, Comcast Corporation, and government service to her new position.

title: BBVA incorpora al Banco Provincial a nuevo servicio internacional de tesorería para multinacionales y Pymes
summary: BBVA launched its new international treasury service, BBVA Pivot, designed for multinational companies and SMEs with international operations, simplifying treasury management by unifying access to payments and collections. This service is available in 15 countries and 24 currencies, including Venezuela through BBVA Provincial. BBVA Pivot aims to act as a global banking partner for businesses expanding into new markets, offering a unified digital experience and expert support.

title: NatWest Markets plans closures and cuts in Italy and Spain
summary: NatWest Markets, the investment arm of NatWest Group Plc, is planning to close its Madrid branch and reduce operations in Milan as part of a continuing effort to scale back its investment bank. These proposed reductions are expected to lead to job cuts for over a dozen employees out of approximately 30 across both locations. The bank aims to streamline its corporate offerings and cover Iberian customers from other European branches, maintaining its retreat from investment banking that began after the 2008 financial crisis.

title: Graduating from Secured Credit Cards to General Purpose: KeyBank Hits a Chord
summary: This article highlights KeyBank's successful secured credit card program, which helps clients build or rebuild credit and graduate to general-purpose cards. It details how the program saved KeyCorp over $1.1 million in acquisition costs and significantly improved participants' FICO scores, positioning it as a good model for other issuers. The piece emphasizes the importance of secured cards as a responsible lending option, especially given the economic impacts of COVID-19.

title: BMO upholds winning streak
summary: Bank of Montreal (BMO) Financial Group has maintained its leading position in the Canadian retail structured products market, reporting 340 product issuances as of April 30, 2021. This continues a trend of increased issuance that began in Q4 2020. The bank also reported a significant increase in net income for Q2 2021, reaching CAD1.3 billion, and a substantial reduction in provision for credit losses compared to the previous year.

title: $5 Billion In Loans Makes Goldman One Of SoftBank’s Biggest Lenders
summary: Goldman Sachs has become one of SoftBank's largest lenders, providing over $5 billion in loans, making it the fourth-largest lender to the Japanese conglomerate for the 12-month period ending March 31. This news follows SoftBank's announcement of seeking an initial public offering (IPO) for its QR code payment app, PayPay, and aims to expand its financial services footprint in Asia. SoftBank plans to double PayPay's customer base to drive a cashless economy in Japan.

title: What are Citizens Bank and Cathay Bank, the buyers of more than 90 of HSBC's US branches?
summary: HSBC is exiting its US retail banking business for mass-market customers and small businesses, selling 90 branches to Citizens Bank and Cathay Bank. Citizens Bank will acquire 80 branches on the East Coast, focusing on expanding its presence in major metropolitan areas, while Cathay Bank will take over 10 branches on the West Coast to broaden its California network. This strategic move allows HSBC to concentrate on wealthy clients and international corporations, shifting resources to higher-growth markets in Asia.

title: What are the banks snapping up 90 of HSBC’s branches in America?
summary: HSBC is selling 90 of its US retail bank branches to Citizens Bank and Cathay Bank as part of its strategy to exit mass-market retail banking in the US and focus on wealthy clients and international corporations, particularly in Asia. Citizens Bank is a long-standing US financial institution, while Cathay Bank is a large bank founded by Chinese Americans, and this acquisition will expand their existing footprints. The move reflects HSBC's pivot to growing markets in Asia, shifting capital from underperforming businesses in the US and Europe.

title: FA IPO News - Silver Lake-backed HR platform provider First Advantage files for a $100 million IPO
summary: First Advantage, an HR platform provider backed by Silver Lake, has filed for an initial public offering aiming to raise $100 million. The company offers technology solutions for screening, verifications, safety, and compliance, performing over 75 million screens for more than 30,000 customers in 2020. Headquartered in Atlanta, GA, First Advantage booked $530 million in revenue for the 12 months ended March 31, 2021, and plans to list on Nasdaq under the symbol FA.

title: HDFC Bank fined Rs 10 crore by RBI in car loan case
summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has imposed a hefty penalty of Rs 10 crore on HDFC Bank. This fine was levied due to the bank's practice of wrongfully selling third-party non-financial products to its auto loan customers. The issue came to light following a whistleblower complaint, which also led to the sacking of six employees and the resignation of the head of the bank's auto loan business last year.

title: Banking: The biggest N.C.-based banks and credit unions
summary: North Carolina-based banks and credit unions experienced a significant rebound despite initial fears of an economic slump due to the pandemic, with many reversing reserves and seeing deposits surge from federal stimulus. This article highlights several key institutions and their performance, including TRUIST FINANCIAL, FIRST CITIZENS BANCSHARES, LIVE OAK BANK, and TRULIANT FEDERAL CREDIT UNION, and notes the stability and growth within the state's financial sector. It also details notable events and financial achievements of various banks, as compiled for Business North Carolina's annual list.

title: Ally Bank ends all overdraft fees, first large bank to do so
summary: Ally Financial has announced it is eliminating all overdraft fees across its banking products, making it the first major bank to do so. This move is significant for the industry, which has historically relied on these fees for revenue, often impacting lower-income households. Ally cited the disproportionate effect of overdraft fees on Black and Latino households as a key reason for the change, aiming to alleviate financial anxiety for its 3.6 million affected accounts.

title: Ally Bank eliminates overdraft fees
summary: Ally Bank has permanently eliminated overdraft fees, a move praised by consumer advocates and some lawmakers. The bank's CEO, Jeffrey Brown, stated that these fees disproportionately burden lower-income households and people living paycheck to paycheck. Overdraft fees historically generate billions for banks, but Ally's decision highlights a growing trend among some institutions to remove these charges.

title: Nikki Graham retiring, David Bader to become new Austin market president for Bank of America
summary: Nikki Graham is retiring from Bank of America after 27 years, transitioning to a philanthropic role at The Hector and Gloria Lopez Foundation. David Bader will succeed her as the new Austin market president for Bank of America. This leadership change marks a significant development for Bank of America's presence in the Austin market.

title: BofA names Kevin Tracy new Rhode Island president
summary: Bank of America Corp. has appointed Kevin Tracy as the new Rhode Island market president, succeeding William F. Hatfield who is retiring in July. Tracy, who has been with the company for 35 years, will be responsible for managing and growing the bank's $8.6 billion in deposits and its 29 branches in the region. He is recognized for his contributions to small businesses, including facilitating $160 million in Paycheck Protection Program loans in 2020.

title: Ally Bank ends overdraft fees, a first for large U.S. banks
summary: Ally Bank has announced it is eliminating overdraft fees on all its bank products, becoming the first large U.S. bank to do so. This move addresses the financial burden these fees place on customers, particularly Black and Latino households, and comes amid increasing pressure from lawmakers and regulators to reform overdraft practices. While the banking industry collected over $12 billion in overdraft fees last year, Ally, which did not rely heavily on these fees, expects no major impact on its profit forecasts.

title: BofA Puts More Capital Into Sales, Trading Teams, CEO Says
summary: Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan announced the bank will allocate more capital to its sales and trading teams. This decision follows the teams' strong performance during the pandemic's market volatility. Moynihan highlighted their consistent ability to perform well even under wild circumstances.

title: Ally Bank is eliminating overdraft fees, which disproportionately affect poor households and people of color
summary: Ally Bank, the largest digital bank in the US, announced it is eliminating overdraft fees for all customers, with no requirements or restrictions. CEO Jeffrey Brown stated this move aims to support financially vulnerable consumers, as 95% of the $12.4 billion in overdraft fees paid in 2020 came from disproportionately Black and Latinx individuals. This decision addresses the burden of overdraft fees, which can prevent people from improving their financial stability.

title: Lisa Pollina to step down as Non-Exec Director of IG Group
summary: Lisa Pollina has informed the Board of electronic trading major IG Group Holdings plc of her intention to step down as a Non-Executive Director on September 1, 2021. Pollina currently serves as an investment adviser to Ares Management and a Non-Executive Director of Munich RE, bringing extensive experience from her previous roles at RBC Capital Markets and Bank of America Securities. Her career also includes serving on various public and private corporate Boards and contributing to the Federal Reserve Bank's Working Group on Financial Markets.

title: Wall Street Reins In Hedge Funds’ Short Bets on Meme Stocks
summary: Major Wall Street firms like Goldman Sachs, Bank of America, Citigroup, and Jefferies are quietly tightening rules for hedge funds shorting popular meme stocks such as GameStop and AMC. These adjustments to risk controls in their prime-brokerage operations aim to protect the banks from the extreme volatility seen in these companies. The moves come as meme stock volatility also draws attention from lawmakers.

title: MOVES Morgan Stanley hires ex BofA banker Rizzo to drive European client push - sources
summary: Morgan Stanley has hired former Bank of America banker Luigi Rizzo as vice chairman of investment banking for EMEA to bolster its client-facing efforts across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. Rizzo, who previously led Bank of America's European corporate and investment banking, will advise clients on strategic combinations, especially as M&A markets rebound post-COVID. His appointment comes as Morgan Stanley seeks to capitalize on a strong M&A market, with global dealmaking volumes hitting record highs.

title: Bank of America Reshuffles Global Natural Resources Team
summary: Bank of America has announced leadership changes within its global natural resources unit, impacting its operations in Europe and North America. Maria Garijo del Cura and James Sleeman have been appointed as co-heads of EMEA natural resources investment banking, based in London. These appointments were communicated internally by Ray Wood, the bank's head of global natural resources investment banking.

title: 10 Largest Class Action Settlements in American History
summary: This article lists and describes the ten largest class action settlements in American history, detailing the circumstances and monetary values of each. These settlements range from issues like defective breast implants and accounting fraud to major events like the Volkswagen emissions scandal and the BP Gulf of Mexico oil spill, with the largest being the 1998 Big Tobacco settlement. The piece highlights how these lawsuits have impacted consumers and speculates on future large settlements, particularly in technology and privacy.

title: US legaltech provider Intapp files for potential initial public offering
summary: Intapp, a US cloud-based professional services software firm, is preparing for an initial public offering (IPO) on the Nasdaq Global Market under the ticker symbol “INTA”. The company, which specializes in client lifecycle software and serves 96 of the AM Law 100 firms, reported $187 million in total revenues for the 2020 fiscal year. Shearman & Sterling is advising Intapp on the IPO, while Latham & Watkins is advising the underwriters.

title: MOVES Ex BofA exec Elfring joins JPMorgan as EMEA vice chair -memo
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. has appointed Bob Elfring, a former Bank of America executive, as vice chairman of investment banking for Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. Elfring will focus on strengthening JPMorgan's presence outside Britain, particularly in the Benelux region, leveraging his extensive knowledge of the Dutch market. His appointment aims to bolster JPMorgan's efforts in the recovering M&A market.

title: Top Banker Quits Italy State Bank as Mario Draghi Revamps Leadership
summary: Bank of America Corp. is hiring top investment banker Vito Lo Piccolo from Italy’s state-backed lender Cassa Depositi e Prestiti SpA. Lo Piccolo will join BofA's investment banking division as a managing director, covering M&A and capital markets, starting in July. This move coincides with an overhaul of Cassa Depositi e Prestiti's leadership under Prime Minister Mario Draghi.

title: Regions Bank places $1B bet on home renovation market
summary: Regions Bank is acquiring EnerBank USA for $960 million in cash, aiming to significantly expand its presence in the home improvement lending market. EnerBank, a specialized lender with $2.8 billion in loan balances, works with a network of 10,000 contractors. This acquisition is part of Regions' strategy to deepen client relationships and reach new customers in the growing home renovation sector, which is projected to increase to $433 billion in 2021.

title: GlobalFoundries Adds JPMorgan, BofA to Its Jumbo IPO Roster
summary: GlobalFoundries has expanded its initial public offering (IPO) banking syndicate by adding JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Bank of America Corp. to lead roles. Citigroup Inc. and Credit Suisse Group AG have also been brought on in more junior capacities. The chipmaker's IPO could reportedly value the company at around $30 billion.

title: 1stdibs.com, Inc. Announces Pricing of Initial Public Offering
summary: 1stdibs.com, Inc. announced the pricing of its initial public offering of 5,750,000 shares of common stock at $20.00 per share, expecting to raise $115 million. The shares are anticipated to begin trading on The Nasdaq Global Market under the ticker symbol “DIBS” on June 10, 2021, with the offering closing on June 14, 2021. The underwriters also have a 30-day option to purchase additional shares.

title: Exxon’s Board Defeat Signals the Rise of Social-Good Activists
summary: Exxon Mobil experienced a significant defeat as activist investor Engine No. 1 successfully installed three directors on its board, aiming to push the energy giant to reduce its carbon footprint. This unprecedented win was supported by major institutional investors like BlackRock, Vanguard, and State Street, who typically do not side with activists on such matters. The victory signals a rising trend of social-good activists who believe that environmental consciousness can also benefit a company's financial performance.

title: Moody's keeps stable view on banks in China
summary: Moody's Investors Service maintains a stable outlook on China's banking sector, citing the solid asset quality of Chinese lenders and the economy's sustained recovery from the COVID-19 pandemic. The firm upgraded the ratings outlook for several regional commercial lenders from negative to stable, but also highlighted potential long-term risks associated with the uncertain technological implementation of the green transformation. The banking sector has been proactively addressing credit risk, with significant disposal of nonperforming loans.

title: 8 BRILLIANT WAYS TO MANAGE FINANCIAL STRESS DURING HARD TIMES
summary: This article provides eight strategies for managing financial stress, especially during challenging times like the COVID-19 pandemic. It advises controlling expenses, finding alternative income sources, prioritizing essential bills, diligently watching savings, availing moratorium benefits on loans, approaching lenders for debt solutions, being aware of insurance needs, and selectively utilizing provident funds. The core message emphasizes proactive financial management to navigate economic uncertainties and reduce anxiety.

title: Starbucks Stadium? Coffee chain applies for naming rights
summary: Starbucks Corp has applied to the U.S. trademark office for the right to use its name on sports stadiums or training facilities. This move could allow Starbucks to join other major companies in naming sports venues, either through active sponsorship deals or to protect its intellectual property for future use. The U.S. Patent and Trademark Office will review the application and assign a lawyer by early September.

title: BofA’s Pay to Card Brings the Bank Into the Fast-Developing Market for Speedy Payouts
summary: Bank of America has launched Pay to Card, a new service allowing fast payouts to consumers globally, responding to increased demand from the gig economy and e-commerce growth. The service processes payments within five minutes domestically and often within half an hour internationally, leveraging debit card details for consistency across borders. Analysts see BofA having an advantage due to its existing business clients and consumers compared to fintechs that have developed similar payout platforms.

title: Starbucks applies for stadium, arena naming rights
summary: Starbucks has filed an application with the U.S. Trademark Office for naming rights to stadiums and training facilities. This move indicates the coffee giant's interest in promoting its brand through sports and entertainment venues, a common marketing strategy employed by other major corporations like AT&T and FedEx. The company's market capitalization exceeds $132 billion, and its shares saw a slight increase on the day the article was published.

title: Mike Branca Joins Regions Bank to Lead Total Rewards
summary: Regions Bank announced that Michael “Mike” Branca has been named head of Total Rewards, where he will oversee the development and administration of compensation and benefits plans. Branca brings 31 years of financial services experience, including leadership roles at Wells Fargo, Bank of America, and MBNA. He replaces Jill Shelton, who will retire at the end of the year after 16 years with Regions and a 40-year career in human resources.

title: Remote work unwind: Goldman spearheads Wall St return to office
summary: Goldman Sachs is leading a push for Wall Street employees to return to the office, requiring nearly all New York staff back from Monday, June 14, 2021. This contrasts with other firms like Citigroup, which are offering more flexibility and hybrid models. The varying approaches are causing both optimism for the city's economy and anxiety among employees regarding fairness, flexibility, and career impact.

title: California bank is shutting 2 of its 5 branches in SLO County
summary: Bank of the Sierra is closing two of its five branches in San Luis Obispo County (Arroyo Grande and Atascadero) on June 18, which is part of a larger plan by Sierra Bancorp to close five branches outside its primary market area. This decision is attributed to changes in customer behavior due to the COVID-19 pandemic and an efficiency review. The closures reflect a national trend of banks shutting down brick-and-mortar locations, with a record net loss of 2,284 branches in 2020.

title: South Africa
summary: Barclays Private Bank has established an office in Johannesburg, South Africa, to provide offshore private, investment, and corporate banking expertise to South African clients. They leverage their global strength to help ultra-high net-worth individuals, their families, and family offices achieve financial ambitions, offering personalized service, wealth management strategies, and a wide choice of banking, investment, and advisory services. Potential clients are required to establish an investment portfolio of at least £5 million (or local currency equivalent).

title: High Court rejects claims against Barclays that claimants relied on fraudulent misrepresentation of LIBOR loans
summary: The High Court has ruled against local authorities in their claims against Barclays regarding LIBOR-related fraudulent misrepresentations. The court stated that claimants must prove they were aware of the alleged misrepresentations for their claims to succeed, rejecting the argument that an assumption of honesty was sufficient. This decision reinforces previous rulings that conscious thought about the representation is a necessary component for establishing reliance in misrepresentation claims.

title: BMO Harris Bank Selects FIS for Modernization of Core and Digital Banking Platforms
summary: BMO Harris Bank is partnering with financial technology leader FIS for a multi-year program to transform its core banking systems, aiming to support its growth in the U.S. market. This modernization will enable BMO to offer more convenient, mobile-first banking experiences, introduce new products quickly, and increase operational efficiency. The agreement includes FIS's Modern Banking Platform, Payments One, Digital One, and managed services, enhancing BMO's retail digital platform and customer channels.

title: Morgan Stanley Looks to Shed Wirehouse Comparisons, Take on Schwab
summary: Morgan Stanley is seeking to redefine its competitive landscape, moving away from traditional wirehouse comparisons like Merrill Lynch, UBS, and Wells Fargo, and instead aligning itself with direct wealth management platforms, particularly Charles Schwab. CEO James Gorman and wealth management head Andy Saperstein highlighted the firm's growth in net new assets and advisor recruitment as evidence of its successful shift. The strategy involves leveraging advisor-led, direct investment, and workplace platforms, and using machine learning to enhance client engagement and advisor referrals.

title: Morgan Stanley, Bank of America CEOs break relative silence on office returns
summary: CEOs of Morgan Stanley and Bank of America have signaled a strong desire for employees to return to the office, setting Labor Day as a benchmark for this transition. James Gorman of Morgan Stanley and Brian Moynihan of Bank of America emphasized the importance of in-person work for culture, learning, and client interaction, while also addressing vaccination status and compensation expectations. Their push aligns with other major bank CEOs who have expressed increasing impatience with remote work arrangements.

title: What Can Loan-Level Data Reveal About US Auto-Loan ABS?
summary: Loan-level data for US auto-loan asset-backed securities (ABS) offers granular insights into default probability and overall collateral risk, which could be overlooked by standard pool-level analysis. Issuers have been required to disclose this data since 2016, allowing for more precise analysis. Incorporating loan-level data for factors like vehicle type, loan-to-value ratio, gross coupon, and issuer significantly improves the accuracy of models for predicting auto-loan ABS performance.

title: Bank of America Says All Vaccinated Staff to Return to Office in September
summary: Bank of America expects all vaccinated employees to return to the office after Labor Day in early September. The company will then develop plans for unvaccinated workers. CEO Brian Moynihan stated that over 70,000 employees have voluntarily disclosed their vaccination status.

title: Bank of America adds branches in Kentucky, rounding out years-long expansion strategy
summary: Bank of America is continuing its multi-year retail expansion strategy by opening new branches in Lexington, Kentucky. This move signifies the bank's ongoing commitment to broadening its physical presence in key markets. The expansion further solidifies its position in the region.

title: Carver Bancorp and Bank of America Announce Closing of Social Impact Credit Facility with BlackRock
summary: Carver Bancorp, Inc., Bank of America, and BlackRock have closed a Senior Secured Social Impact Revolving Credit Facility. This marks the first time Carver, a Minority Depository Institution, has participated as a co-lender in such a facility. The initiative aims to drive economic change in underserved communities, fostering financial inclusion and empowering minority communities.

title: Bank of America Makes Juneteenth a Holiday, Joining JPMorgan, Wells Fargo
summary: Bank of America and JPMorgan Chase are making Juneteenth a company holiday starting next year, following President Joe Biden's signing of the federal holiday into law. Employees will receive a floating paid day off this year as June 19 falls on a Saturday. Wells Fargo is also observing Juneteenth as a federal holiday starting in 2022.

title: Goldman Sachs welcomes bankers back to the office with live music, food trucks
summary: Goldman Sachs welcomed bankers back to its New York offices with live music, food trucks, and free fitness classes to ease their return after CEO David Solomon's strong push against remote work. Other Wall Street firms like Barclays, JPMorgan, and Morgan Stanley are also planning their returns, with varying approaches to office mandates and COVID-19 restrictions. Morgan Stanley's James Gorman notably warned employees to return by Labor Day or face pay cuts, emphasizing the importance of in-office presence.

title: 'Don't lose sight of why': Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan on importance of ESG in business
summary: Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan emphasized that investing in environmental, social, and governance (ESG) issues should not be seen as a burden but as a fundamental aspect of a company's business model. He stated that ESG principles should be core to how businesses operate. The article highlights Moynihan's perspective on the importance of integrating ESG into corporate strategy.

title: Juneteenth, Now a Federal Holiday, Puts Companies to Work on a Response
summary: Following President Biden's signing of a bill making Juneteenth a federal holiday, companies across the U.S. are scrambling to determine how to acknowledge it. This includes deciding whether to offer paid time off, with some, like Goldman Sachs and Bank of America, quickly implementing new policies. The new holiday has prompted a rapid response from employers.

title: Bank of America makes Juneteenth a holiday, joining JPMorgan, Wells Fargo
summary: Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase, and Wells Fargo will recognize Juneteenth as a paid holiday, joining other financial institutions in response to President Biden signing it into law. While these banks will offer floating holidays this year and add it to regular schedules next year, financial markets like the NYSE and Nasdaq are still determining whether to close. This move reflects a broader industry response to racial inequality following the murder of George Floyd.

title: JPMorgan, UBS, Wells Fargo to allow US employees take day off for Juneteenth
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co, UBS, and Wells Fargo & Co are allowing their U.S. employees to take a floating day off to observe Juneteenth, following President Biden's declaration of it as a federal holiday. Although Juneteenth falls on a weekend this year, employees can coordinate a paid day off with managers. This move by major financial institutions acknowledges the new federal holiday, which marks the end of legal enslavement of Black Americans.

title: Bank of America, JPMorgan, Wells Fargo make Juneteenth a bank holiday
summary: Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase, and Wells Fargo have announced that Juneteenth will become a bank holiday starting next year, following President Biden's signing of a measure to make June 19 a federal holiday. JPMorgan and Wells Fargo are also offering a floating paid holiday this year to commemorate the day. This move comes as companies address the legacy of racism, with some institutions like Mastercard and Citi previously implementing similar policies or extra paid days.

title: El mea culpa de Ebensperger sobre el rol de los empresarios: “Lo hemos hecho mal y tenemos clara evidencia de mejorar”
summary: Eduardo Ebensperger, CEO de Banco de Chile, admitió que los líderes empresariales "lo hemos hecho mal" y tienen una clara oportunidad de mejorar, en este momento crucial para Chile antes de la instalación de la Convención Constitucional. Hizo un llamado a la empatía, el diálogo, y a reconocer los avances del país sin caer en descalificaciones, enfatizando que el sistema financiero es sólido pero necesita estabilidad fiscal para asegurar el crecimiento futuro.

title: William Kaufman, Travelers Cos. Seal $185M Loan for 437 Madison Avenue
summary: The William Kaufman Organization and The Travelers Companies have closed a $185 million refinance loan for 437 Madison Avenue, with Wells Fargo providing the new debt. This loan retires $145 million in existing debt from Bank of America and Apple Bank. Eastdil Secured brokered the deal on behalf of the owners.

title: Blackstone Bets $6 Billion on Buying and Renting Homes - WSJ
summary: Blackstone Group Inc. is acquiring Home Partners of America Inc., a company that buys and rents single-family homes, in a $6 billion deal. This acquisition signals Wall Street's belief that the U.S. housing market will remain robust. Home Partners of America owns over 17,000 houses and offers tenants the option to eventually purchase the homes they rent.

title: Morgan Stanley says no vaccine, no entry. (Published 2021)
summary: Morgan Stanley announced that starting July 12, employees, clients, and visitors must attest to being fully vaccinated against the coronavirus to enter its New York City and Westchester County buildings. Unvaccinated staff will be required to work remotely. This policy aims to allow the bank to relax other pandemic protocols like mask-wearing and social distancing, aligning with moves by other major financial institutions.

title: European banks should start merging, says Deutsche Bank’s top Qatari investor
summary: Deutsche Bank's largest Qatari shareholder, Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabor Al Thani, has urged consolidation within Europe's financial services industry. He believes that European banks need to merge now to gain the necessary scale to compete with their larger US and Chinese counterparts, stating that they are currently "too small to survive by themselves." Sheikh Hamad, through Paramount Services Holdings, holds a significant stake in Deutsche Bank.

title: Poole College Advisory Board Spotlight: Judy Whiting
summary: Judy Whiting, with over 30 years of experience at Bank of America and now with Truist Bank, has joined the Poole College of Management Advisory Board. A North Carolina native, Whiting brings extensive financial expertise and a desire to contribute to the state's development, emphasizing Poole College's commitment to providing value to North Carolina citizens and the business community. She is currently collaborating with Dr. Richard Warr on a Research Impact Task Force to enhance the college's engagement with local industry.

title: Eye on Crypto: Fiserv Enables Crypto Transactions at FIs, And a Crypto ATM Firm Eyes 6,000 Machines
summary: Fiserv announced a new service allowing financial institutions to enable their customers to buy, sell, and hold Bitcoin through their bank accounts, integrating with NYDIG. This aims to help banks meet growing interest in cryptocurrency, retain customers, and increase non-interest income. Concurrently, Bitcoin Depot, a cryptocurrency ATM deployer, plans to expand its network to 6,000 machines by the end of the year, anticipating increased demand for crypto access.

title: TD Bank to Launch Low-Cost Deposit Account, Expanding Account Offerings in Support of Unbanked Households
summary: TD Bank announced the upcoming launch of TD Essential Banking, a low-cost, no-overdraft-fee deposit account designed to serve unbanked and underbanked households. This initiative is part of broader efforts to expand product offerings, including changes to overdraft policies and consumer lending, and to enhance financial education tools. The goal is to provide more accessible and affordable financial services to underserved communities.

title: Wells Fargo’s Next Play: The Self-Directed Channel
summary: Wells Fargo is considering a significant push into the self-directed investment channel, potentially through acquiring a brokerage platform or rebranding its WellsTrade platform. This move aims to capture more assets and next-generation investors, following similar strategies by competitors like Morgan Stanley and Bank of America. The expansion's feasibility may depend on the Federal Reserve lifting a regulatory asset cap on Wells Fargo.
