The company outlined its strategic plan for continued growth, including channel expansion and innovation, and provided optimistic net sales guidance for 2022. Despite inflationary pressures impacting gross margin, Zevia maintained its commitment to providing affordable, zero-sugar, plant-based beverages and demonstrated significant progress in its ESG metrics.

title: Citigroup to Get Rid of Overdraft Fees, the Biggest Bank to Do So (Published 2022)
summary: Citigroup announced it will eliminate overdraft and returned item fees by summer, becoming the largest bank to do so. This decision follows similar moves by smaller lenders like Capital One and Ally Financial, and comes amidst increasing pressure from regulators who argue these fees disproportionately affect financially vulnerable customers. Other banking giants like Bank of America have cut their overdraft fees, but none have fully eliminated them.

title: Rocket Companies Report Down Earnings, But Issue Special Dividend
summary: Rocket Companies reported a significant drop in annual revenue and net income for 2021 compared to 2020, as well as lower fourth-quarter results. Despite the decrease in earnings, the company announced a special dividend of $1.01 per share and a share repurchase program worth $300 million. CEO Jay Farner highlighted a record year in loan origination and the strategic importance of the Truebill acquisition for client engagement and long-term goals.

title: List of Banks and Lenders with SBA Loan Guarantee Agreements
summary: This article provides a comprehensive list of banks and lenders in New Hampshire that offer small business loans under SBA loan guarantee agreements. It details contact information including addresses, phone numbers, and websites for each institution. The list serves as a valuable resource for small businesses seeking financing options in the region.

title: Goldman Probed by SEC Over Messages Sent Using Unapproved Services
summary: Goldman Sachs Group Inc. is being investigated by the SEC for employees' use of unapproved messaging services for business communications. This probe follows similar actions against other major financial institutions, including JPMorgan, which faced $200 million in fines, and HSBC, which is also being investigated by the CFTC for similar issues. Goldman Sachs is cooperating with the SEC and providing requested documents.

title: SunTrust Bank Permanently Closed
summary: The SunTrust bank branch at 8700 Georgia Ave. in downtown Silver Spring has permanently closed following the consolidation of operations into Truist after BB&T Bank acquired SunTrust in 2019. This closure is part of Truist's "core conversion" process, which has led to some customer issues, including temporary loss of access to debit cards and bank accounts. These conversions are affecting all former BB&T and SunTrust customers as they transition to Truist products and digital platforms.

title: Safehold Announces Public Offering and Concurrent Private Placement
summary: Safehold Inc. announced a public offering of 1,750,000 shares of its common stock, with underwriters having an option to purchase an additional 262,500 shares. Concurrently, Safehold will sell shares to iStar Inc. in a private placement. The net proceeds will be used for additional ground lease investments, to repay borrowings, and for general corporate purposes.

title: Morgan Stanley Forgoes Subtlety in Recruiting Video Targeting Merrill Lynch Brokers
summary: Morgan Stanley Wealth Management created a nearly five-minute recruiting video directly targeting Merrill Lynch brokers using testimonials from former Merrill advisors. The video critiques Merrill Lynch's culture and product offerings while praising Morgan Stanley's support for its wealth management division. This aggressive tactic is seen as an attempt by Morgan Stanley to capitalize on its positive recruiting trend and Merrill Lynch's recent attrition.

title: BlackRock Inc. stock underperforms Friday when compared to competitors
summary: BlackRock Inc. (BLK) shares fell 4.95% on Friday to $696.59, underperforming the broader market as the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average also declined. This marked the second consecutive day of losses for the stock, placing it significantly below its 52-week high. Competitors like Bank of America Corp., INVESCO Ltd., and Affiliated Managers Group Inc. also saw their shares fall, although BlackRock's decline was substantial.

title: SERNAC lanza primer comparador de tarjetas de crédito
summary: SERNAC has launched the first-ever Credit Card Comparator in Chile, a tool designed to help consumers compare all associated charges of credit cards available in the market. This tool aggregates information from 194 cards, highlighting significant differences in maintenance fees, cash advance charges, and foreign transaction fees. The initiative aims to empower consumers to make more informed financial decisions, prevent over-indebtedness, and encourage competitive practices among financial institutions.

title: International Arbitration After the Pandemic
summary: The article discusses the resurgence of international arbitration after the COVID-19 pandemic, driven by growth in cross-border trade and investment. It highlights the rapid expansion of international disputes and the rebalancing of dispute resolution activity towards Asian centers. The publication also anticipates new disputes from COVID-19 disruptions, energy transition, and financial distress, while noting reforms in Investor State Dispute Settlement.

title: SIRIANNI: Morgan Stanley’s Moment
summary: Tony Sirianni discusses Morgan Stanley's revamped recruiting strategy and unique position in the wealth management industry. He highlights Morgan Stanley's success in attracting advisors, contrasting its approach with Merrill Lynch and other wirehouses, particularly its focus on a strong, advisor-centric culture. The article suggests Morgan Stanley has carved out a distinct identity as a large full-service firm, appealing to veteran wire advisors who might be dissatisfied with bank-owned platforms.

title: The Buzz Online
summary: This article, "The Buzz Online," highlights various professional appointments, promotions, and achievements in New Hampshire. Key updates include new hires and promotions at banks like St. Mary's Bank, Meredith Village Savings Bank, and Merrimack County Savings Bank, as well as academic honors at Plymouth State University and a significant medical appointment at Dartmouth-Hitchcock's Norris Cotton Cancer Center. Additionally, it announces a donation to NHTI's Paramedic Emergency Medicine program and the launch of the 41st Annual Prouty.

title: Huntington Bancshares Inc. stock outperforms competitors despite losses on the day
summary: Huntington Bancshares Inc. (HBAN) shares fell 4.54% on Monday, closing at $14.09, amidst a broader market decline where the S&P 500 and Dow Jones also experienced losses. Despite this, HBAN outperformed several competitors, including Bank of America Corp. (BAC), Fifth Third Bancorp (FITB), and F.N.B. Corp. (FNB), which saw larger percentage drops. The stock closed $3.70 below its 52-week high, with trading volume exceeding its 50-day average.

title: Onnet Fibra Colombia, de KKR y Telefónica, recibe financiamiento
summary: Onnet Fibra Colombia, a joint venture between KKR and Telefónica Colombia, secured a syndicated loan equivalent to $221 million from several banks including Scotiabank Colpatria S.A., Bancolombia S.A., BBVA Colombia, and The Bank Of Nova Scotia. These funds will finance KKR's acquisition of Telefónica Colombia's fiber optic assets for $500 million. Onnet Fibra Colombia, which began operations in January 2022, provides a neutral fiber-to-the-home (FTTH) network with a current coverage of 1.2 million homes and aims to reach 4.3 million customers by the end of 2024.

title: Regulators put UnitedHealth-Change Healthcare Merger on Life Support
summary: The Department of Justice has filed a lawsuit to block UnitedHealth Group's $13 billion acquisition of Change Healthcare, Inc., disagreeing with the companies' claim that the merger would benefit consumers through streamlined healthcare processes and reduced costs. The DOJ argues that the deal would allow UnitedHealth to gain unfair access to competitors' sensitive information and control healthcare technology innovations, highlighting a shift in antitrust enforcement under the Biden administration.

title: ‘Black Panther’ Director Ryan Coogler Mistaken for Bank Robber in Atlanta
summary: Ryan Coogler, the director of "Black Panther," was briefly detained by police in Atlanta after Bank of America employees mistook him for a bank robber. Coogler was attempting to discreetly withdraw a large sum of cash, which led the teller to incorrectly believe a robbery was in progress. Bank of America has since apologized to Coogler for the incident.

title: Huntington to cut overdraft fees from $36 to $15 starting in July
summary: Huntington Bank announced it would reduce overdraft and non-sufficient funds fees from $36 to $15 starting in July, following similar moves by other major banks. Additionally, the bank will introduce a feature in April allowing customers immediate access to up to $500 from check deposits. This strategy, estimated to cost the bank $14 million per quarter initially, is expected to attract new customers and reduce attrition in the long term.

title: Russia risks "imminent" default on its debt, Wall Street analysts say
summary: Russia is facing an "imminent" default on its debt due to groaning under Western sanctions, according to credit ratings agencies and Wall Street firms. Fitch downgraded Russia's debt for the second time in a week, citing the high likelihood of default and the impact of sanctions on its ability and willingness to repay. With $700 million in payments due in March and a 30-day grace period, a default could occur as early as mid-April, further isolating Russia from international financial flows.

title: Goldman Sachs CEO Says Ostracizing Russia Isn’t the Finance Industry’s Job
summary: Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon stated that it is not the finance industry's job to ostracize Russia, but rather to follow government sanctions. He emphasized that businesses should implement policies set by the government, agreeing with the sanctions against Russia's actions in Ukraine. Despite this stance, the article highlights Goldman Sachs's historical involvement in Russia's economic policy and its mixed record on activism.

title: New agriculture practices are preserving Brazil’s forests
summary: CHS Brazil is implementing new agricultural practices and participating in programs to combat deforestation in Brazil. They are committed to ensuring crops are grown on existing agricultural land, not illegally cleared forest land, and have received a "green" loan for their sustainable sourcing practices. The company also collaborates with NGOs and involves employees in reforestation efforts.

title: Old-School Leveraged Loan Market Is a Step Closer to Ditching Faxes
summary: A consortium of Wall Street banks, including Bank of America, Citigroup, and JPMorgan Chase, has launched Versana, a new platform aimed at modernizing the $1.38 trillion U.S. leveraged loan market. This initiative seeks to centralize data management for lenders, moving away from current manual tracking methods that still occasionally involve faxes. Credit Suisse has also joined the portal, which is expected to improve efficiency and reduce settlement times in the notoriously complex market.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Morgan Stanley Calls Brokers Back to Offices, Sets 90-Day Cap on WFH
summary: Morgan Stanley Wealth Management is implementing a new policy limiting most of its 16,000 brokers to 90 days of remote work per year, effective July 1. This move aims to bring staff back to offices and ensure compliance with supervisory obligations. Brokers can apply for alternative remote work locations based on criteria like length of service or production club membership, subject to additional supervision.

title: Why Mubadala Bought Taco Bell's K-Mac in History-Making Deal
summary: Mubadala Investment Co., a state-owned holding company from Abu Dhabi, made a significant investment in K-Mac Enterprises, a U.S.-based Taco Bell operator. This deal, which occurred last October, marks the first time a Middle East sovereign wealth fund has invested in a U.S. restaurant franchisee. The move highlights Mubadala's strategy to diversify investments away from oil and signals a growing trend of sovereign wealth funds seeking premier platforms in the U.S. restaurant sector.

title: Bank of America Adviser Ousted After Rant Is Hired by Brokerage Aegis Capital
summary: James Iannazzo, a former Bank of America financial adviser who was fired after a widely circulated video showed him in a tirade at a smoothie shop, has been hired by Aegis Capital Corp. FINRA data confirms his registration with the New York-based broker-dealer as of March 15. His specific role at the new company was not disclosed.

title: Lloyds share price: to break the 100p resistance barrier?
summary: The Lloyds Banking Group share price has struggled since the 2008 financial crisis, remaining a "penny stock" below the 100p resistance level. However, recent strong full-year results and rising UK interest rates, particularly from the Bank of England, could help the bank break this psychological barrier. While increasing rates pose some risks of mortgage defaults, historically, Lloyds' share price has closely tracked UK interest rates, suggesting a potential recovery closer to pre-crisis norms.

title: Expedia Group CPO on risk management & strategic sourcing
summary: Reagan Smith, Head of Global Corporate Procurement at Expedia Group, discusses his journey into procurement, his biggest career influences, and his passion for elevating the indirect procurement function. He emphasizes continuous learning, challenging established practices, and aligning procurement strategies with business needs for success. Smith also shares personal anecdotes, including his pride in advocating for the LGBTQ community.

title: Georgia Power Foundation pledges $2.5 million to the HUB for Community Innovation project
summary: The Georgia Power Foundation has pledged $2.5 million to the HUB for Community Innovation project, bringing its total funding to $21 million out of a $33.5 million goal. This investment is part of Georgia Power's five-year, $87 million commitment to advancing racial equity and social justice. The HUB will house four local nonprofits and aims to revitalize the Harrisburg and Laney Walker neighborhoods.

title: Alaska Air Group and Bank of America Renew Long-Term Partnership Agreement
summary: Alaska Air Group and Bank of America have renewed their co-branded credit card agreement through 2030, extending a decades-long partnership. This collaboration aims to enhance guest benefits and further drive strategic growth for both companies, particularly in West Coast regions. Additional cardholder benefits are anticipated to be introduced in the latter half of 2022.

title: Alaska Air Group provides update on long-term growth strategy
summary: Alaska Air Group is hosting its Investor Day to outline its long-term growth strategy, emphasizing successful pandemic recovery, industry outperformance in guest experience, and financial strength. The company plans to grow 4-8% annually through 2025 by deepening its network, transitioning to a single, more efficient fleet, and enhancing its loyalty program through an extended partnership with Bank of America. They also reiterate commitments to sustainable practices and provide a positive full-year 2022 outlook with specific financial metrics.

title: JD.com’s logistics unit seeks up to US$1.1 billion via placement
summary: JD Logistics, the logistics unit of JD.com, is seeking to raise up to US$1.1 billion through a new share placement. The company is offering US$400 million worth of new shares to investors at a discount, while its parent company, JD.com, plans to purchase an additional US$700 million worth of shares, pending shareholder approval. The funds are intended for network and solution improvements and increasing cash reserves.

title: Equity Market Gloom Triggers BofA’s Contrarian ‘Buy Signal’ for Stocks
summary: Bank of America's internal indicator has triggered a contrarian 'buy signal' for global equities, similar to its activation in March 2020. Historically, global equities have seen an average 8% increase in the 12 weeks following such signals. This signal suggests potential upside for stocks in the coming weeks.

title: Bank of America Corp. stock rises Friday, outperforms market
summary: Shares of Bank of America Corp. (BAC) increased by 1.53% to $43.73 on Friday, outperforming the broader market which also saw gains in the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average. This rise ended a two-day losing streak for the company's stock. Despite the positive movement, Bank of America Corp. closed below its 52-week high, and its performance relative to competitors like JPMorgan Chase & Co., Citigroup Inc., and Wells Fargo & Co. was mixed.

title: Wells Fargo & Co. stock outperforms market on strong trading day
summary: Wells Fargo & Co. (WFC) stock rose 2.40% to $52.56, outperforming the broader market with the S&P 500 Index gaining 0.51% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rising 0.44%. The stock also outperformed its competitors like JPMorgan Chase & Co., Bank of America Corp., and Citigroup Inc. This marks the second consecutive day of gains for Wells Fargo.

title: Operator of Domino’s Pizza China Files for Hong Kong Listing amid Three-year Net Loss
summary: DPC Dash, the exclusive master franchisee for Domino’s Pizza in mainland China, Hong Kong, and Macao, has applied for a Hong Kong stock exchange listing. Despite reporting increasing net losses for the past three years due to expansion costs and the 30-minute delivery promise, the company plans to open 120 new stores in 2022, primarily in Beijing and Shanghai. The filing also highlighted that over 73% of its revenue comes from delivery orders and acknowledged business risks related to Covid-19 restrictions.

title: Energy Transfer to sell LNG to China's ENN
summary: Energy Transfer LP's liquefied natural gas unit has signed 20-year agreements to supply a total of 2.7 million tonnes of LNG to China's ENN Natural Gas and ENN Energy Holdings Limited, with deliveries expected to begin in 2026. The deal comes as global demand for natural gas, especially in Europe due to sanctions on Russian fuel, is driving U.S. LNG projects toward final investment decisions. The purchase price is indexed to the Henry Hub benchmark plus a fixed liquefaction charge.

title: Capital One Is one of the 2022 TIME100 Most Influential Companies | TIME
summary: Capital One has been named one of the 2022 TIME100 Most Influential Companies primarily for its decision to eliminate overdraft and insufficient-fund fees. This move, which accounted for $150 million of its $30.4 billion revenue last year, has influenced other major U.S. banks like Bank of America, Wells Fargo, and Citigroup to follow suit amidst regulatory pressure. The article highlights the significant impact of these fees on financially vulnerable families and Capital One's role in shifting industry standards.

title: Así se comportan las acciones del Grupo Aval y Banco de Bogotá tras separar su filial
summary: Following the separation of their Panamanian subsidiary Leasing Bogotá S.A. Panamá (LBP) and the creation of BAC Holding International (BHI), the shares of Grupo Aval and Banco de Bogotá experienced significant movements. Preferential shares of Aval dropped 21.74%, and ordinary shares of BanBogotá lost 19.67% upon their return to the market. However, when accounting for the exchange of shares with the new entity, BHI, shareholders of Banco de Bogotá saw a 20% increase in value, and Grupo Aval shareholders experienced a 14% increase compared to pre-suspension levels.

title: Lanzan OPA por 15% de BAC Holding International, título que llegaba hoy al mercado
summary: An unexpected tender offer (OPA) was launched for 5% to 15% of BAC Holding International shares, just as the company was set to begin trading on the Colombian Stock Exchange (BVC). The shares, priced at $293 in the OPA, were suspended before their debut. This move follows the separation of Banco de Bogotá and Leasing Bogotá S.A. Panamá, a strategy aimed at reducing volatility from exchange rates and improving corporate efficiency.

title: Capital One Is one of the 2022 TIME100 Most Influential Companies
summary: Capital One has been recognized as one of the 2022 TIME100 Most Influential Companies for its groundbreaking decision to eliminate overdraft and insufficient-fund fees. This move, which cost the bank $150 million in revenue last year, has set a trend among major U.S. banks, with others like Bank of America, Wells Fargo, and Citigroup announcing similar plans. The elimination of these fees is particularly impactful for financially vulnerable families.

title: An Inclusive Leader, Korn Ferry Senior Advisor Has Had a Career of Firsts
summary: Caroline Nahas, a senior advisor to Korn Ferry and UCLA Anderson's first woman board chair, reflects on her pioneering career filled with "firsts" in leadership. She discusses her inclusive leadership style, the importance of fostering a supportive environment for employees, and her philanthropic philosophy shaped by a personal experience of generosity during her college years. Nahas emphasizes the rich diversity of Los Angeles and her commitment to bringing UCLA Anderson to greater levels of excellence.

title: Jugada de Luis Carlos Sarmiento para blindar sus negocios por las elecciones en Colombia
summary: Luis Carlos Sarmiento Angulo, owner of Grupo Aval, has initiated a strategy to reorganize his financial holdings, specifically separating Banco de Bogotá and Grupo Aval from Leasing Bogotá S.A. Panamá, leading to the creation of BAC Holding Internacional. This move involves Rendifin, a Sarmiento-controlled company, attempting to acquire 15% of BAC Holding Internacional through a public acquisition offer. The primary motivation for this restructuring is reportedly the electoral uncertainty in Colombia and the implementation of Bitcoin in El Salvador, aiming to safeguard his businesses in both nations.

title: Dakota Gold Corp. Announces Merger Closing as Part of a Specific Focus on Revitalizing the Homestake District in Lead, South Dakota
summary: Dakota Gold Corp. announced the completion of its merger between Dakota Territory Resource Corp. and JR Resources Corp., focusing on revitalizing the Homestake District in Lead, South Dakota. The company's common stock is expected to begin trading on the NYSE American under the symbol "DC" on or about April 5, 2022, following a significant expansion of its land package and establishment of an ESG fund. This strategic move aims to leverage the Homestake District's 145-year gold mining legacy for new discoveries and opportunities.

title: Trucking Companies Bet on Intermodal Growth
summary: Trucking companies are increasingly investing in intermodal operations as a key growth strategy, driven by factors such as unwinding supply chains, rising fuel costs, and environmental initiatives. Analysts anticipate a market share shift from truck to domestic intermodal, supported by improving railroad operations. Major players like J.B. Hunt, Schneider National, Hub Group, and Knight-Swift Transportation are expanding their intermodal fleets and services to capitalize on this trend and diversify their revenue streams.

title: OPA de Sarmiento Angulo: ¿Qué ganan y qué pierden los que vendan y los que no?
summary: Luis Carlos Sarmiento Angulo, through his company Rendifin, has launched a Public Acquisition Offer (OPA) to buy between 5% and 15% of BAC Holding International (BHI) shares from shareholders of Grupo Aval and Banco de Bogotá. Credicorp Capital analyzed the offer, suggesting it provides liquidity for those who sell, while warning that retaining shares could lead to decreased liquidity for BHI due to a reduced floating stock, potentially impacting its inclusion in indices like MSCI Colcap. The price offered in the OPA is $293 per share, close to the book value, and an analysis shows that minority shareholders who hold both Aval/Bogotá shares and BHI shares have seen an increase in combined value post-spin-off.

title: German authorities raid Barclays’ office in tax fraud investigation
summary: German authorities have raided Barclays' Frankfurt offices as part of an investigation into Cum-Ex tax trades. The probe also involved searches of two suspects' homes and is related to a trading strategy that exploited Germany's tax laws, costing the government $11.2bn before being banned in 2012. Barclays is cooperating with the authorities, and the raids follow a similar investigation into Bank of America Corp.'s Merrill Lynch offices.

title: Jamie Dimon, U.S. Bank and BMO show value is a buyer-led construct
summary: The article discusses how the perceived "value" of executives and acquired companies is largely determined by the buyer, not an intrinsic worth. It highlights Jamie Dimon's substantial compensation package from JPMorgan Chase, which significantly exceeded initial estimates due to stock performance and board decisions, alongside contrasting M&A deals where similar asset sizes yielded vastly different acquisition prices. The piece concludes by noting that value can also depreciate or be withheld, citing examples of executive compensation disputes at Barclays and Goldman Sachs.

title: Morgan Stanley spins off $15 billion RIA business
summary: Morgan Stanley is selling its $15 billion registered investment advisory (RIA) business, Eaton Vance WaterOak Advisors, which it acquired last year as part of its Eaton Vance acquisition, to CI Financial and Pathstone. This move signals Morgan Stanley's continued intention to exit the RIA space and focus on core verticals, following a previous sale of ETrade's RIA custody business. The sale involved dividing the assets between two buyers, highlighting a creative approach to acquisitions in the growing RIA sector.

title: ¿Movimientos de BHI en la bosa afectaron a los accionistas de Aval y Banco de Bogotá?
summary: The article discusses the market activity surrounding BAC Holding Internacional (BHI) shares, an Oferta Pública de Adquisición (OPA) by a company related to Luis Carlos Sarmiento Angulo, and its impact on the shareholders of Grupo Aval and Banco de Bogotá. It highlights that despite temporary suspensions due to the OPA and an earlier spin-off process, the shareholders of Grupo Aval and Banco de Bogotá did not incur losses, but rather saw an increase in the value of their holdings after considering the BHI shares received. Grupo Aval also declared a significant dividend, offering a high dividend yield in the market.

title: Arkansas Eyes Upon Texas Lending
summary: Arkansas banks are increasingly expanding their operations into Texas, drawn by its larger banking market and growth opportunities. Major players like Home BancShares (Centennial Bank), Simmons First National Corp., and Bank OZK have made significant acquisitions and branch expansions. Other banks like Farmers Bank & Trust, Encore Bank, Bodcaw Bank, and Diamond Bank are also establishing a presence, utilizing both acquisitions and new branch development.

title: Jamie Dimon’s 2021 Letter to Shareholders
summary: Jamie Dimon's 2021 letter to shareholders addresses the significant global challenges of a pandemic, the war in Ukraine, and inflation, while also highlighting JPMorgan Chase's record revenue and strong financial performance in 2021. Dimon emphasizes the company's commitment to clients, employees, and communities, and discusses key themes such as American competitiveness, energy security, and the evolving competitive landscape for banks. The letter underscores the importance of strong leadership, continuous investment, and maintaining a robust balance sheet for sustained success.

title: India’s Most Valuable Bank Set to Grow With Home-Lending Deal
summary: India's largest home-lending company, Housing Development Finance Corp., and its largest private-sector bank, HDFC Bank Ltd., have announced a merger. This share-based deal will create a financial giant with a combined loan book of $235 billion, aiming to capitalize on India's rising housing demand and benefit from increased scale and cross-selling opportunities. Market participants and analysts view this long-awaited merger as a strategic move to accelerate growth for the combined entity.

title: Banking & Finance Roundup: Seacoast to acquire Miami’s Apollo Bank
summary: This article covers the banking and finance news roundup for the week, highlighting Seacoast's acquisition of Apollo Bank in Miami. It also lists other related articles about regional banking news, including Pitcairn hiring a local executive and Amerant Bank joining a blockchain network.

title: Hancock Whitney to drop overdraft and other charges, following banking drift away from fees
summary: Hancock Whitney Bank is eliminating fees for nonsufficient funds and some overdraft charges by the end of 2022, expecting to cut about $11 million in charges. This move aligns with a broader industry trend where major banks like Citibank, Capital One, and Bank of America are also dropping such fees, driven by consumer protection scrutiny and advancements in digital finance. The bank also plans to introduce services allowing earlier access to pay to help customers avoid overdrafts.

title: BAC Holding International corp inscribió más de 43.220 millones de acciones en la BVC
summary: BAC Holding International (BHI) has registered over 43.22 billion shares on the Colombian Stock Exchange (BVC) following its separation from Banco de Bogotá and Grupo Aval. This move came alongside a tender offer (OPA) by Luis Carlos Sarmiento for up to 15% of BHI's shares at $293 each. The market is awaiting authorization from the Superfinanciera for the OPA, which aims to reduce volatility from currency exchange rates for Grupo Aval and Banco de Bogotá.

title: Nutresa, Éxito y Ecopetrol, las acciones que más crecen en la BVC en lo corrido del año
summary: Grupo Nutresa, Éxito, and Ecopetrol have been the top-performing stocks on the Colombian Stock Exchange (BVC) so far this year, with significant growth rates. Factors contributing to this performance include Gilinski's tender offers for Nutresa, a potential tender offer and share repurchase for Éxito, and rising oil prices for Ecopetrol amid global conflicts. Other companies like Bancolombia, Grupo Sura, and Grupo Bolívar have also seen notable increases.

title: Putnam’s Collins Draws On Nature For ESG Investing Inspiration
summary: Katherine Collins, head of sustainable investing at Putnam Investments, integrates biomimicry and insights from nature, specifically honeybees, into her ESG investment strategies. After a career in traditional finance and a master's degree from Harvard Divinity School, Collins applies a unique lens to identify companies demonstrating leadership in sustainability. Her approach focuses on balancing risk and opportunity, evidenced in her co-management of Putnam Sustainable Leaders (PNOYX) and Putnam Sustainable Future (PMVYX) funds.

title: Dave & Buster’s Announces Acquisition of Main Event for $835 Million; Chris Morris to become CEO of Combined Entity Upon Closing
summary: Dave & Buster's Entertainment, Inc. announced its acquisition of Main Event from Ardent Leisure Group Limited and RedBird Capital Partners for $835 million. Chris Morris, the current CEO of Main Event, will become CEO of the combined entity upon closing. This acquisition aims to expand Dave & Buster's demographic reach by targeting families with younger children while also creating significant growth opportunities for both brands.

title: Auto Industry Outlook Dims: Bank of America
summary: Bank of America Securities analysts have revised their outlook for the auto industry, projecting a dimmer picture for 2022 due to ongoing supply chain issues, geopolitical tensions, and COVID-19 resurgences. They forecast a 7% decline in U.S. auto sales for 2022 and a 10% drop in North American production. The report also highlights several auto suppliers like Adient, Lear, Visteon, and Aptiv that received upgrades, while used car retailers CarMax and America's Car-Mart saw their ratings downgraded.

title: Constellation Brands to repurchase $500M of its own stock
summary: Constellation Brands announced an accelerated share repurchase program with Bank of America to buy back $500 million of its stock, which is expected to increase existing shareholders' ownership concentration. This move comes as the company reported a rise in fourth-quarter net income and acquired the remaining interest in Austin Cocktails. The company also confirmed its plans to move its headquarters to downtown Rochester, bringing hundreds of jobs.

title: Michael O’Higgins FX Class Representative Ltd and Mr Phillip Evans v Barclays Bank PLC and others
summary: The Competition Appeal Tribunal (CAT) refused to certify opt-out collective proceedings against several global banks for alleged follow-on competition damages related to foreign exchange trading. The CAT cited concerns about the strength of the proposed claims and the practicability of opt-in proceedings. While neither opt-out application was certified, the CAT indicated it would have granted carriage to Mr Evans had the dispute been relevant for an opt-out claim.

title: Canada’s selfie generations lead the way in financial self-assessments
summary: A BMO Investment Survey reveals that younger Canadians, particularly Gen Z and Millennials, are more engaged in consistently assessing their financial goals than older generations. While these groups are actively tracking their finances and seeking professional advice from recommendations, a significant portion also relies on financial influencers and social media for investing decisions. The survey also highlights that many young Canadians hold predominantly cash savings due to a lack of investment knowledge, yet a good number are contributing to TFSAs for early financial independence.

title: Morgan Stanley aims to serve the richest of the rich as family offices grow to $5.5 trillion in assets
summary: Morgan Stanley has launched a new unit dedicated to serving family offices, which are investment entities for the world's richest individuals and families. The bank is targeting this rapidly growing segment, which has expanded to over $5.5 trillion in assets globally, by offering tailored technology solutions and aims to reach $10 trillion in client assets. This move positions Morgan Stanley to cater to both newly wealthy individuals and established ultra-high net worth clients, differentiating itself through institutional-quality services and a matchmaking platform for private investments.

title: Dow gains, S&P 500 ends lower as market weighs Fed rate hikes
summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite fell on Friday as investors grappled with aggressive Federal Reserve interest rate hikes aimed at tackling inflation. Bank shares, which had significantly declined, saw gains as the 10-year Treasury yield reached a three-year high. Value stocks continued to outperform growth stocks as the market anticipates a potential recession or a "soft landing" engineered by the Fed.

title: Keurig Dr Pepper announces strategic refinancing, offering
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper (NASDAQ: KDP) announced a strategic refinancing initiative, including a public offering of senior notes and concurrent tender offers, to strengthen its balance sheet and improve liquidity. The proceeds will primarily be used to fund the tender offers and redeem outstanding senior unsecured notes, or for general corporate purposes if the offers are not consummated. This move follows the company's successful deleveraging over the past three years.

title: Bank Of America Loses Saudi Investment Bank Head to EFG Hermes
summary: EFG Hermes has appointed Saud Altassan, formerly Bank of America's head of investment banking in Saudi Arabia, as its new CEO for the country. This move comes as financial institutions aim to capitalize on a burgeoning deals market in the region. Altassan brings extensive experience from Bank of America, Swicorp, NCB Capital, and Banque Saudi Fransi to his new role.

title: Copper Hires BofA Team to Build Prime Brokerage Crypto Product
summary: Copper Technologies Ltd. has hired a team of executives from Bank of America Corp., led by Michael Roberts, to establish a unit focused on developing infrastructure for prime brokerage crypto platforms. This move aims to cater to the increasing demand from institutional investors and banks for direct access to cryptocurrencies. The London-based digital asset custodian seeks to build out new offerings to meet this market need.

title: S&P Global Market Intelligence Global Bank Rankings: European Banks Slid Down Rankings as They Scaled Back Operations in the U.S. amid Competition - Apr 11, 2022
summary: European banks experienced a decline in global asset size rankings in 2021 due to scaled-back operations in the U.S. and slower economic growth in their home markets, with their total assets contracting by 2.16%. In contrast, Chinese banks maintained their top positions with expanded balance sheets, driven by government initiatives to boost lending. Major U.S. banks also saw their asset sizes grow, pushing them higher in the rankings, though future growth may slow due to the absence of government stimulus and the Federal Reserve's efforts to combat inflation.

title: Saline County Court Filings – 041222
summary: This article lists the court filings in Saline County on April 11, 2022. It includes cases categorized as arrest warrants, various civil actions (other, contract, seller plaintiff debt collection), decendent estate administration, divorces, felonies, guardianship of an adult, order of protection, paternity, and other probate cases. The article serves as a record of local legal proceedings.

title: Morgan Stanley Claws Back $3.1 Million From Ex-Broker in NYC
summary: A FINRA arbitration panel has ordered former Morgan Stanley broker Nicolas P. Lumermann to pay the firm over $3.1 million in a promissory note dispute, denying his claim of constructive discharge. Lumermann, who transitioned to online gaming after leaving the firm, was held liable for the unpaid balance plus interest. The panel did not provide a reason for its decision but denied Morgan Stanley's request for legal fees.

title: VALLEY BANK AND LPGA COGNIZANT FOUNDERS CUP ANNOUNCE THREE-YEAR BRAND AMBASSADOR SPONSORSHIP STARTING WITH THE 2022 TOURNAMENT AT UPPER MONTCLAIR COUNTRY CLUB IN CLIFTON FROM MAY 11-15
summary: Valley Bank has announced a three-year partnership with the LPGA Cognizant Founders Cup as the Brand Ambassador Sponsor, beginning with the 2022 tournament at Upper Montclair Country Club in Clifton, NJ. This sponsorship aims to engage golf fans and local residents to assist with tournament operations and supports the LPGA's mission to empower women through golf. In addition to the Brand Ambassador Program, Valley Bank will also sponsor the Mentor Monday program, connecting students with business leaders in the golf industry.

title: Li Lu Top 10 Holdings – Q4 2021, Buys FB, BAC
summary: This article details superinvestor Li Lu's top 10 holdings as of Q4 2021, derived from his 13F-HR documents. His portfolio, valued at over $2.6 billion, shows significant investments in Micron Technology, Bank of America, and Facebook, alongside other major tech companies. The report also highlights his new buys, Facebook and Bank of America, and his sell in Pinduoduo.

title: BofA Says Fund Managers Most Gloomy on Record on Recession Woes
summary: A Bank of America survey reveals that fund managers are experiencing record-high pessimism regarding global growth, with recession fears becoming the primary concern among investors. Optimism for global growth has reached an all-time low, signaling significant worries within the investment community about an impending economic downturn.

title: RBB President and CEO Resigns After Internal Investigation
summary: Royal Business Bank's (RBB) president and CEO, Alan Thian, has resigned immediately following an internal investigation that found he violated bank policies, particularly concerning personnel decisions. The violations, while not having a financial impact, negatively affected employee morale. This departure, combined with the earlier exit of the chief lending officer, may also complicate RBB’s planned acquisition of Gateway Bank.

title: JPMorgan Chase Unveils Plans for New Global Headquarters Building in New York City
summary: JPMorgan Chase has unveiled the design for its new global headquarters at 270 Park Avenue in New York City. The 60-story skyscraper will be the city's largest all-electric tower with net zero operational emissions, housing up to 14,000 employees. This project is expected to create 8,000 construction jobs and contribute significantly to New York City's economy, while also setting new standards for sustainability and employee wellness in a modern workplace.

title: Wells Fargo commits $210M to racial equity in wake of criticism
summary: Wells Fargo has pledged $210 million to advance racial equity in homeownership following criticism over its low approval rates for Black refinancing applicants. Of this, $150 million will be used to lower rates and costs for Black homeowners seeking to refinance through a new Special Purpose Credit Program. The bank aims to address systemic inequities and will report its progress annually.

title: Fidelity Investments Launches Crypto, Metaverse ETFs — Says 'We Continue to See Demand'
summary: Fidelity Investments has launched two new exchange-traded funds (ETFs) focused on the crypto and metaverse sectors. The company stated that it continues to observe strong demand for digital asset exposure and innovative technologies like the metaverse. This move by Fidelity allows investors to gain exposure to these emerging markets through traditional investment vehicles.

title: Bank of America profit falls less than expected on boost from loan growth, deposits
summary: Bank of America reported a quarterly profit decline of $1 billion, yet still beat Wall Street's earnings targets due to healthy loan growth. The company's first-quarter earnings fell to $7.1 billion, or 80 cents a share, from $8.1 billion, or 86 cents a share in the previous year. Following the announcement, Bank of America shares rose by 3.3%.

title: Interns see 37% pay bump at a number of top banks: data
summary: Top global investment banks have significantly increased intern pay, with a 37.2% jump between 2021 and 2022, according to data from Wall Street Oasis. This surge is attributed to an intense war for talent, as financial firms compete with tech and consulting companies to attract entry-level workers and address prior complaints about long workweeks. The pay raises appear to be effective, as Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley both reported substantial increases in internship applications.

title: Where Bank of America execs see growth potential despite growing economic uncertainties
summary: Bank of America executives are focusing on growth opportunities in a post-Covid economy despite increasing uncertainties. The article highlights the bank's strategy amidst recent financial results and broader economic shifts, emphasizing areas where they anticipate continued expansion.

title: Charles Schwab (SCHW) Q1 revenue down 1%; earnings miss estimates
summary: The Charles Schwab Corporation reported lower earnings and revenues for the first quarter of 2022, missing Wall Street's forecasts. Total revenues decreased 1% to $4.67 billion, and adjusted net profit dropped to $0.77 per share. The company's stock experienced a decline following the earnings release.

title: Bancolombia recibió crédito de US$ 150 millones atado a su desempeño sostenible
summary: Bancolombia secured a US$150 million loan from Bank of America with interest rates tied to its sustainability performance. The bank committed to disbursing over nine trillion pesos in sustainable loans by 2024 and reducing 12,900 tons of CO2 emissions. This financing reflects international banking's confidence in Bancolombia's commitment to environmental, social, and corporate governance impacts.

title: Goldman Sachs Boosts Hiring of Dealmakers in Singapore
summary: Goldman Sachs is increasing its hiring of senior investment bankers in Singapore to strengthen its dealmaking capacity in Southeast Asia. The firm has recruited Chua Hui Yin from JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Andrew Teo from Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp. for key roles in corporate finance and investment banking. These additions aim to capitalize on the growing M&A and IPO activity in the region.

title: Treasury Bond Massacre, Mortgage Rates Hit 5.35%, Highest since 2009, and it’s Only April
summary: This article discusses the significant spike in Treasury yields and mortgage rates, with the 30-year fixed mortgage rate reaching 5.35%, the highest since 2009. Author Wolf Richter attributes this to the Federal Reserve's rate-hike plan to combat 8.5% CPI inflation. The bond market is experiencing a "massacre" for long-term bond funds, while future buyers will benefit from higher yields, and the housing market is expected to see a serious impact.

title: WesBanco Named One of the World’s Best Banks by Forbes
summary: For the fourth consecutive year, WesBanco Bank has been recognized by Forbes as one of the World’s Best Banks, ranking 30th globally. The recognition is based on customer satisfaction surveys across various criteria including trust, customer service, digital services, and financial advice. WesBanco's President and CEO, Todd F. Clossin, attributes this success to the company's commitment to delivering large bank capabilities with a community bank feel, focusing on long-term customer relationships and investing in innovative digital technology.

title: Canadian megabank CIBC opens startup-focused investment office in Bellevue
summary: Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC) is expanding its CIBC Innovation Banking arm by opening a new office in Bellevue. This office will focus on providing growth capital to local startups. CIBC Innovation Banking was established in 2018 following the acquisition of Wellington Financial.

title: Bank of America Taps StanChart Banker to Run Saudi Franchise
summary: Bank of America has appointed Yazaid Al-Salloom of Standard Chartered Plc to lead its operations in Saudi Arabia, according to individuals familiar with the situation. Al-Salloom will also be responsible for Kuwait and Bahrain for the U.S. bank. He is taking over from Motashar Al Murshed, who recently transitioned to a Saudi government body.

title: First Internet Bank Appoints Genevieve Lua As VP
summary: First Internet Bank announced the appointment of Genevieve Lua as Vice President, Business Development Officer, to its Small Business Administration Lending team. Lua brings extensive lending experience from Bank of America and JPMorgan Chase, and will help entrepreneurs navigate the SBA loan process. First Internet Bank emphasizes providing flexible financial solutions for small businesses.

title: Bank of America to Make Its Credit Cards From Recycled Plastic
summary: Bank of America announced on April 21, 2022, that all its plastic credit and debit cards will be manufactured from recycled material starting in 2023. These cards will contain at least 80% recycled plastic and will feature a recycling logo. The bank claims to be the first U.S. institution to implement this change across all its card products, aiming to reduce its environmental impact through lower greenhouse-gas emissions, energy, and water consumption.

title: Morgan Stanley Plucks $6-Mln Merrill Team in Nashville
summary: Morgan Stanley Wealth Management successfully recruited a team from Merrill Lynch in Nashville, generating around $6 million in annual revenue and managing $870 million in client assets. This move is part of Morgan Stanley's aggressive recruiting efforts, offering significant bonuses and targeting Merrill's advisors. The article also mentions a separate, smaller team that moved from Merrill to Morgan Stanley in North Carolina and New York.

title: American National Bank recruits nearly dozen business bankers from Old National
summary: American National Bank recently recruited 11 business bankers from Old National Bank, signaling a strategic move to aggressively expand its commercial banking operations in the Twin Cities. This recruitment highlights a competitive shift in the local banking landscape.

title: How big banks are building a branch workforce of the future
summary: This article discusses how major banks like U.S. Bank are adapting their retail branch workforces to the evolving digital landscape. It highlights the transformation of retail bank employees to meet the demands of a more digitally-centric banking environment. The piece also includes related articles focusing on banking hiring trends and remote work policies among large financial institutions.

title: BBVA se sumó al Programa Creadores de Mercado en Argentina
summary: BBVA in Argentina has been designated as a "Market Maker" within the national Ministry of Economy's Market Maker Program (PCM). This role involves generating liquidity and facilitating the buying and selling of National Treasury bonds, showcasing BBVA's commitment to the local capital market. The program aims to foster the secondary market for Public Debt Instruments and increase liquidity through stable pricing and yields.

title: RBC and CIBC join banking group helping to finance Elon Musk’s bid for Twitter
summary: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) and Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC) have committed US$1.15-billion to finance Elon Musk's US$44-billion takeover of Twitter Inc. The Canadian banks are participating in the lowest-risk part of the financing, a US$12.5-billion loan secured by a portion of Musk's Tesla shares. This indicates their involvement in the major acquisition while taking on the least financial risk among the lenders.

title: 5 Best Business Checking Account Promotions in 2023
summary: This article compiles the top business checking account promotions available in 2023 from various banks, highlighting the bonuses offered, how to earn them, and any restrictions. It also provides guidance on maximizing these promotions, understanding associated fees, and what features business owners should look for in a checking account beyond just sign-up bonuses. The piece emphasizes the importance of reading terms and conditions carefully to ensure eligibility for the offers.

title: Barclays warns inflation and cost of living crisis is hurting customers
summary: Barclays has warned that the cost of living crisis and surging inflation are already impacting its customers, leading the bank to set aside an additional £141m for potential loan defaults. These concerns echo those from other major UK banks like Lloyds and HSBC, who are also preparing for tougher economic conditions exacerbated by the war in Ukraine and supply chain issues. Despite these warnings, Barclays still reported a rise in pre-tax profits, though profits were impacted by legal costs related to the over-selling of American financial products.

title: Better Buy: Bank of America vs. Toronto-Dominion Bank
summary: This article compares Bank of America (BAC) and Toronto-Dominion Bank (TD) for conservative income investors, concluding that TD Bank is likely the better buy. The analysis focuses on dividend yield, dividend history, regulatory environment, Tier 1 Capital ratios, and growth prospects. TD Bank is highlighted for its higher yield, consistent dividend during the Great Recession, conservative Canadian regulatory framework, stronger Tier 1 capital ratio, and significant growth potential in the U.S. market.

title: Prosecutors search Deutsche Bank HQ in money laundering investigation
summary: German prosecutors, federal police, and financial regulators searched Deutsche Bank's headquarters in Frankfurt in connection with a money laundering investigation. The search is linked to suspicious transactions that Deutsche Bank itself reported to the authorities, and the bank stated it is cooperating fully. This incident is part of a larger effort by Deutsche Bank, under CEO Christian Sewing, to repair its reputation following a history of regulatory failings related to money laundering.

title: The long-shot campaign to get big banks out of fossil fuels
summary: Climate activists are intensifying pressure on major banks like Citigroup, Wells Fargo, Bank of America, and Goldman Sachs to cease financing new fossil fuel projects. Although recent shareholder resolutions failed, gaining only about 10 percent of the vote, advocates see this as a foundational step. They are drawing on the success of the fossil fuel divestment movement and hope to eventually sway large asset managers to support their cause, despite current skepticism from bank boards and the energy market's volatility exacerbated by global events.

title: The Next Big Visa-Mastercard Rival Is…Zelle?
summary: Payments industry experts are questioning if the Zelle P2P network will expand to point-of-sale transactions, potentially challenging Visa and Mastercard. Bank of America and Wells Fargo are reportedly lobbying for this expansion, which could help banks circumvent debit card fee restrictions from the Durbin Amendment. However, concerns exist about cannibalizing profitable credit card business and the lack of consumer protections and rewards offered by Zelle compared to cards.

title: Frank Sorrentino III Of ConnectOne Bank On The Future Of Money and Banking
summary: Frank Sorrentino III, Chairman, CEO, and Founder of ConnectOne Bank, discusses the evolving landscape of banking and money, emphasizing the role of digitalization and technology in serving small to mid-market clients. He shares insights on ConnectOne Bank's journey, including its IPO and recent Fintech acquisitions, and offers advice for a successful career in the modern finance industry. Sorrentino highlights the importance of innovation balanced with regulation and envisions significant growth in payments and digital asset custody.

title: México: los principales bancos extranjeros son dueños de las concesiones para la extracción de agua
summary: Major foreign banks hold water extraction concessions in Mexico, allowing them to extract millions of cubic meters annually, often from overexploited aquifers. This financial interest in water is highlighted by the trading of water futures on Wall Street, turning a vital resource into a speculative commodity. The article emphasizes the disparity where a small percentage of users control a large portion of water for profit, exacerbating scarcity and high costs for the general population, especially in marginalized areas, and criticizes government complicity in granting these concessions.

title: Bank OZK hires new managing director for Trust and Wealth group
summary: Bank OZK has announced the hiring of Chris Henry as the new Managing Director for its Trust and Wealth Group. Henry will be responsible for leading and expanding the bank's trust and wealth management services, including estate planning and administration. He brings experience from First Bank and Trust Company and Bank of America Private Bank, holding CFP® and CTFA designations.

title: Fundtruffle - Tellsons’s MacFarlane shares his view on inflation and the markets
summary: Cranley MacFarlane, co-manager of Tellsons’s Endeavour Fund, discusses current market conditions amidst high inflation, rising interest rates, and global supply chain disruptions. He highlights how companies like PepsiCo and Bank of America are demonstrating resilience, while also noting the easing of supply chain issues in some regions. MacFarlane emphasizes the defensive strength of holdings in sectors less affected by inflation, such as healthcare.

title: Georgia Power issues landmark Equality Progress Sustainability Bond
summary: Georgia Power has issued the first-ever corporate Equality Progress Sustainability Bonds (EPSBs) totaling $800 million as part of a larger $1.5 billion senior unsecured bond offering. These EPSBs are designed to advance racial equality, economic opportunity, and environmental sustainability, with at least 50% of net proceeds allocated to social spending primarily benefiting minority- and/or female-owned suppliers. This initiative aligns with Southern Company's "Moving to Equity" framework and Georgia Power's commitment to increase spending with diverse suppliers to 30% by 2030, reinforcing their leadership in ESG-bond issuances.

title: UK bank and building society overview: who owns who?
summary: This article explains the ownership structures of UK banks and building societies, highlighting how many operate under the same banking licences. Understanding banking groups is crucial for consumers to ensure their money is protected by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS), which has an £85,000 limit per banking licence. The article lists major banking groups, single-licence banks, building societies, and foreign-owned banks with UK licences, emphasizing the importance of this knowledge for financial protection and ethical banking choices.

title: Scoping Out Scope 3 Emissions
summary: A report by Citi Research's Anita McBain highlights the growing importance of Scope 3 emissions as new reporting requirements aim to improve transparency in emission reporting across global value chains. The article discusses the complexities of disclosing Scope 3 emissions compared to Scope 1 and 2, and the significant business benefits companies can achieve by addressing them. It also examines current Scope 3 disclosure trends by country, noting that while the U.S. has the largest volume of disclosed emissions, a smaller proportion of its companies consider Scope 3 relevant compared to Japan.

title: The Old Tech FAANG Is Dulled, But a New Version Has Promise
summary: Bank of America strategists have introduced "FAANG 2.0," a new grouping of sectors designed for a world facing inflation, war, and geopolitical shifts, replacing the underperforming original tech FAANG stocks. This new version, comprising fuels, aerospace and defense, agriculture, nuclear and renewables, and gold and metals/minerals, has shown significantly better market performance year to date compared to both the S&P 500 and the original tech FAANG stocks. The article highlights the rationale behind this shift, citing energy security, increased military spending, rising food prices, and gold's role as a refuge asset in the current global climate.

title: Untalan wins Executive of the Year
summary: Edward G. Untalan, executive vice president and Guam-Northern Marianas region manager of First Hawaiian Bank, was awarded the 2021 Guam Business Magazine Executive of the Year. The award was presented at the Hyatt Regency Guam. Untalan has a long-standing career in financial services, beginning in 1987, and has held significant positions at the Bank of Guam, Guam Economic Development Authority, and First Hawaiian Bank.

title: Exclusive| HDFC Bank may get RBI glide path to pare holding in HDFC Credila, HDB Financial after merger
summary: HDFC Bank is seeking the RBI's permission to retain all subsidiaries after its merger with HDFC Ltd. However, the RBI has expressed concerns regarding two lending subsidiaries, HDFC Credila and HDB Financial Services, as their operations could be absorbed by the bank. If the RBI does not allow their continuation in current form, HDFC Bank is expected to seek a glide path to divest its stake in these two entities.

title: ICICI Bank vs Bank of Baroda vs PNB vs Canara Bank: Comparison of home loan interest rates
summary: Following the RBI's repo rate hike by 40 basis points to 4.40%, several major banks have increased their home loan interest rates. This report compares the new RLLR (Repo Linked Lending Rate) and I-EBLR (ICICI Bank External Benchmark Lending Rate) for ICICI Bank, Punjab National Bank, Bank of Baroda, and Canara Bank, effective primarily in May and June 2022. The hike leads to higher EMIs for existing and new borrowers.

title: PE giant Brookfield buys Watermark REIT for $3.8B
summary: Brookfield Real Estate Funds has acquired non-traded REIT Watermark Lodging Trust for $3.8 billion in an all-cash transaction. Watermark's portfolio comprises 25 luxury and upper upscale hotels, including Ritz-Carlton properties, located in U.S. drive-to leisure destinations and gateway urban cities. The acquisition reflects confidence in large-scale hotel deals despite recent interest rate increases and debt capital market volatility.

title: The Thought Process Behind Humana’s Kindred at Home Transactions
summary: Humana's Kindred at Home transactions, including its acquisition and partial divestiture of the hospice segment, were driven by the belief that more care will shift to the home and the potential for significant cost savings. Despite the complexities of a fragmented industry and labor pressures, the deals aimed to leverage Kindred's national platform and capitalize on high hospice M&A valuations. The company plans to use proceeds from the sale for debt repayment and share repurchases, anticipating continued growth in its home-care business.

title: Fuel Rewards Program Adds More Brands
summary: Shell Oil Co. and PDI have expanded the Fuel Rewards program by adding Bank of America and Advance Auto Parts, joining other notable brands like T-Mobile and AAA. This expansion allows members to earn cents-per-gallon rewards on everyday purchases, further maximizing savings at the pump. The program, powered by PDI Marketing Cloud Solutions, boasts over 25 million members and has helped them save more than $2 billion on fuel to date.

title: If you get unemployment, disability or family leave benefits in N.J, look out for a new debit card
summary: New Jersey residents receiving unemployment, temporary disability, or family leave benefits via debit card will receive new cards from a new provider, Garden State Community Bank, starting May 11, 2022. The Labor Department warns that these cards will arrive in a plain white envelope and should not be discarded as junk mail. Recipients currently using Bank of America cards have until August 25, 2022, to use or transfer remaining funds before the old cards are deactivated.

title: BMO Capital Markets Head Fears Deep Recession on Rate Hikes
summary: The CEO of BMO Capital Markets, Dan Barclay, expressed concerns that rising interest rates, intended to combat inflation, might not be effective due to supply-side issues and could instead lead to a deep global recession. He believes current inflation is driven by post-pandemic supply chain issues and the war in Ukraine, rather than demand. Central banks' shrinking balance sheets further contribute to this risk.

title: Not 'junk mail': NJ unemployment, disability recipients getting new debit cards
summary: New Jersey residents receiving unemployment, temporary disability, or family leave benefits via debit card should expect new replacement cards from New York Community Bank, as the state has changed providers from Bank of America. The Department of Labor and Workforce Development warned that the plain white envelope, possibly from Omaha, Nebraska, might resemble junk mail but contains the new card. Claimants have until August 25 to withdraw funds from their old Bank of America cards, which will be deactivated the following day.

title: Watch the Mail: NJ Issuing New Debit Cards for Labor Benefits
summary: New Jersey is transitioning to new debit cards for unemployment insurance, temporary disability, and family leave benefits. New cards from New York Community Bank (Garden State Community Bank) will be mailed in plain white envelopes from Omaha, NE, and recipients are advised not to discard them as junk mail. The new cards can be used starting May 18, 2022, following Bank of America's decision not to renew its contract.

title: República Dominicana participa en la XI Conferencia BBVA de Latinoamérica
summary: The Dominican Republic, represented by Vice Minister of Public Credit María José Martínez, participated in the XI BBVA Latin America Conference in New York. Martínez presented the Dominican economy's resilience, its management of public debt, and the positive impact of recent bond issuance on debt-to-GDP ratios. The conference gathered public and private debt issuers, analysts, and international investors to discuss economic perspectives and investment opportunities in the region, aligning with the Dominican Republic's strategy to achieve investment grade.

title: BAC Holding International confirmó nueva participación de Rendifin de 10% tras OPA
summary: Following a Public Acquisition Offer (OPA) on BAC Holding International (BHI), Rendifin's stake has increased from 4.48% to 10.81%. The OPA, led by Luis Carlos Sarmiento through Rendifin, resulted in 4,100 partners selling their BHI shares, with Sarmiento acquiring 72.04% of his target and 10.8% of the company's outstanding shares for $1.11 trillion. This move aims to reduce volatility for Grupo Aval and Banco de Bogotá due to exchange rates in Central America, particularly in light of El Salvador's adoption of Bitcoin.

title: Judge Dismisses No-poach Suit Against Live Oak, Apiture; NCino’s Continues
summary: A federal class-action lawsuit alleging a no-hire agreement has been dismissed against Live Oak and Apiture after they settled for $4.65 million. However, the case against nCino, a related financial technology firm, is proceeding. The lawsuit claims that an unwritten "gentlemen's agreement" among executives of these interconnected companies suppressed wages for eligible workers in Wilmington.

title: Paxos and State Street Partner to Deliver Reduced Costs and T+0 Settlement in Innovative Pilot - Paxos | Newsroom
summary: Paxos, a regulated blockchain infrastructure platform, has partnered with State Street to integrate its custodial services into the Paxos Settlement Service. This collaboration, which included Credit Suisse, successfully piloted same-day (T+0) settlement of shares, demonstrating how Paxos' platform can revolutionize market operations by reducing costs and increasing efficiency. The initiative highlights the potential of blockchain technology to automate trade lifecycles and advance towards faster, fairer financial markets.

title: Bank of America Clients Hoard Cash at Highest Level in Two Decades
summary: A Bank of America survey reveals that investors are holding the highest levels of cash since September 2001 due to sinking global growth optimism and rising stagflation fears. Hawkish central banks and the threat of a global recession are identified as the biggest tail risks. This bearish sentiment, particularly toward technology stocks and European markets, has triggered Bank of America's contrarian buy signal for equities.

title: Frontdoor president and CEO Rex Tibbens to step down, board chair, former H&R Block chief William Cobb to take over
summary: Frontdoor announced that its president and CEO, Rex Tibbens, will step down from his role in June. William Cobb, who currently serves as the company's board chair and previously led H&R Block, will succeed Tibbens as CEO. This leadership change comes amidst various financial and market challenges impacting Frontdoor, as suggested by related articles on inflation, housing trends, and supply chain issues.

title: Morgan Stanley's Parametric moves the wirehouse into ETF management
summary: Morgan Stanley's asset management subsidiary, Parametric Portfolio Associates, is entering the ETF market as a subadviser for two new Innovator ETFs, marking Morgan Stanley's first direct involvement in ETF management. This move signifies Parametric's expansion beyond separate accounts and direct indexing, offering strategies designed for downside protection without capping upside potential. Industry experts view this as a significant step for Morgan Stanley given its extensive advisor network, despite its earlier history with ETFs.

title: Ocwen, Freddie Mac, Deephaven make leadership appointments
summary: This article details numerous leadership appointments across the mortgage industry, including key promotions and new hires at companies like Ocwen, Freddie Mac, Deephaven, Xactus, Academy Mortgage, Better, Freedom Mortgage, BSI Financial, Mid America Mortgage, Vice Capital Markets, Movement Mortgage, Mortgage Connect, Open Mortgage, Incenter, and Guaranteed Rate. These changes involve various roles such as CFO, head of multifamily, chief sales officer, CTO, president, head of capital markets, head of strategy, chief people officer, and director of diversity lending, highlighting a dynamic period of executive shifts in the sector.

title: Bank of America ups minimum wage to $22 per hour as next step to 2025 goal
summary: Bank of America is increasing its minimum wage to $22 per hour, effective June, as part of its ongoing efforts to reach its 2025 goal. This move is a step towards Bank of America's commitment to raising its baseline compensation for employees.

title: BlackRock Inc. stock rises Monday, still underperforms market
summary: BlackRock Inc. (BLK) stock rose 1.84% on Monday, closing at $611.51, in a positive broader market session. Despite the gain, the stock remained $361.65 below its 52-week high and underperformed some competitors like Bank of America Corp. while outperforming INVESCO Ltd. and Affiliated Managers Group Inc.

title: UGA honors companies that hired the most UGA grads
summary: The University of Georgia recognized the top 25 employers of its Class of 2021 at an event in Sanford Stadium. These companies hired graduates across various industries, from technology and finance to retail and healthcare. UGA's Career Center provides resources for employers to connect with its diverse talent pool.

title: Lowe’s jumps Bank of America as top Fortune 500 company in Charlotte area
summary: Lowe's Cos. Inc. has surpassed Bank of America Corp. as the highest-ranked Fortune 500 company in the Charlotte area. Despite dropping four spots overall to No. 35, Lowe's recorded $96.2 billion in revenue, outperforming Bank of America, which placed at No. 36 with $93.8 billion in revenue. This marks a significant shift in the regional corporate landscape.

title: BofA Halts Equity Trading With Segantii on Block Trade Concerns
summary: Bank of America Corp. has suspended equity trading with hedge fund Segantii Capital Management due to concerns regarding its involvement in large stock sales. This decision was made in early 2021. Citigroup has also halted equity trading with Segantii but continues to engage in other financial instrument trading with the firm.

title: JPMorgan's co-head of UK investment banking has quit for PE
summary: David Lomer, co-head of M&A at JPMorgan and co-head of UK investment banking, has resigned to move into private equity. His departure follows the banking industry's bonus season and comes at a time when financial sponsors are a robust area in the M&A market. The move is significant given JPMorgan's fluctuating M&A revenues and his previous leadership roles within the firm.

title: Diversificar, la clave para no asumir riesgos en un portafolio de inversión
summary: This article emphasizes that structural diversification is crucial for balancing return and risk in an investment portfolio, protecting capital over the long term against unpredictable economic scenarios. It explains how different assets perform in varied economic cycles, such as growth, recession, inflation, and deflation, and introduces Harry Browne's "permanent portfolio" as a practical application of structural diversification. The piece concludes that while diversification may not always top short-term performance rankings, it offers stability and protection, allowing investors to navigate economic uncertainty more effectively.

title: Umivale Activa incorpora a SEAT S.A. a su Junta Directiva
summary: Umivale Activa, a mutual society collaborating with Social Security, held its Board of Directors meeting in Gijón, where Dr. Patricia Such, Director of Health, Safety, and Emergencies for SEAT, CUPRA, and Volkswagen Group companies in Spain, was appointed as the new vice-president. SEAT S.A. now joins the governing body responsible for the Mutua's management and administration. The article also highlights Dr. Such's extensive experience in occupational medicine and her leadership in combating COVID-19 within SEAT S.A., as well as Umivale Activa's key figures and commitment to health and safety management.

title: Concentrated, Yet Fragmented — Indian Banking Has A Split Personality
summary: The Indian banking sector, despite the recent merger of HDFC Bank and HDFC Ltd. leading to increased concentration at the top with SBI and the merged HDFC Bank dominating, remains fragmented beyond the top two players. A BQ Prime analysis indicates that while the two largest banks control a significant portion of advances, the rest of the sector is dispersed among numerous smaller banks. Experts suggest that having a few large "pillar banks" is beneficial for a growing economy, and the presence of many smaller lenders signifies a competitive environment rather than excessive concentration, with continued consolidation expected.

title: $131 Million in Settlements Approved for Distribution in Credit Card Interchange Fees Class Action
summary: Courts have approved the distribution of $131 million in net settlements for a class action against Visa, Mastercard, and several banks regarding credit card interchange fees. The lawsuit alleged a conspiracy to fix fees and restrict merchants' ability to surcharge higher-cost cards. Canadian businesses that accepted Visa or Mastercard between March 23, 2001, and September 2, 2021, are eligible to claim settlement benefits, with an easier process for small merchants.

title: PNC changing 1,000-plus branches to automated model
summary: PNC Financial Services Group Inc. is converting 60% of its branches, over 1,000 locations, to an automated model. This conversion is already underway and is projected to be completed by the end of 2026. This strategic shift will impact how customers interact with branches and reflects a broader trend toward automation in banking.

title: PNC Financial Services Group Inc. mixing tech and comfort at automated branches
summary: PNC Financial Services Group Inc. is integrating technology with comfort in its automated branches, adapting to evolving customer banking habits. The article highlights PNC's strategy of tweaking space usage to better serve modern banking needs. This approach reflects a broader trend among banks to enhance customer experience through technological advancements and reconfigured physical spaces.

title: Football Club FC Barcelona in Talks to Sell TV Rights to BofA, Confidencial Says
summary: FC Barcelona is reportedly in advanced talks to sell a portion of its television rights to Bank of America for 600 million euros ($645 million). This move aims to bolster the Spanish football club's finances. The club previously explored a deal with CVC Capital Partners but withdrew to consider BofA's offer.

title: A paradigm shift has begun in markets, says Morgan Stanley's Ted Pick. Here's what to expect
summary: Morgan Stanley co-President Ted Pick states that global markets are experiencing a fundamental paradigm shift after 15 years of low interest rates and cheap corporate debt. This transition, influenced by the pandemic, war, and inflation, is expected to unfold over 12 to 24 months, leading to a new business cycle. Pick anticipates markets will be dominated by concerns of inflation ("fire") and recession ("ice"), requiring careful navigation from clients and impacting various banking businesses differently.

title: Fundos Mútuos de Privatização: o que são e como funcionam?
summary: Os Fundos Mútuos de Privatização (FMP) permitem que recursos do FGTS sejam usados para investir em ações de empresas estatais em processo de privatização ou capitalização, como a Eletrobras. Este mecanismo oferece diversificação para o saldo do FGTS e amplia o capital para ofertas públicas, embora concentre o risco em um único ativo e exija um prazo mínimo de resgate de um ano. A tributação é isenta para rendimentos até o limite do FGTS.

title: Bain Capital Hires BofA’s Top European Health Care Dealmaker
summary: Bain Capital has hired Christina Dix, Bank of America's head of health care investment banking for Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. Dix will join Bain Capital as a managing director and co-lead its European health care investments alongside Ben Kunstler. She previously worked at Bank of America for almost twenty years.

title: Lucid Unveils Lucid Financial Services with Bank of America
summary: Lucid Group, Inc. launched Lucid Financial Services, a new digital platform offering flexible financing options including lease and loan purchases for Lucid Air customers, in partnership with Bank of America. This service provides a seamless online experience for financing applications and aims to transform vehicle financing with a fully digital journey. The program is initially available to U.S. customers receiving Lucid Air Grand Touring models, expanding to Touring and Pure models later in the year.

title: Talkspace CFO: Cerebral's Controlled Substances Pivot Could Create More Daylight in Virtual Mental Health Market
summary: Talkspace CFO Jennifer Fulk believes that Cerebral's pivot away from prescribing controlled substances could create new opportunities for Talkspace in the virtual mental health market. Talkspace has never prescribed controlled substances and sees Cerebral's recent issues as a potential advantage due to its focus on a full-stack behavioral health care platform. The article also touches on Talkspace's financial turnaround plan and analyst speculation about it being an acquisition target.

title: Gap Inc. Launches New Credit Card Program in Partnership with Barclays and Mastercard
summary: Gap Inc. has launched a new credit card program in partnership with Barclays US Consumer Bank and Mastercard. This program allows cardmembers to earn points across Gap Inc. brands and anywhere Mastercard is accepted, with special reward tiers and benefits. The initiative also includes a "Do Good" component for charitable donations and features credit cards made with recycled ocean-bound plastic.

title: Bud, an open banking fintech used by HSBC, raises £64m
summary: Bud, a London-based open banking fintech that utilizes AI to automate lending decisions and provide customized financial products, has successfully raised $80m (£63.8m) in a Series B funding round. The capital will be used to enhance its platform and support international expansion. Bud's services are currently employed by major financial institutions like HSBC and Credit Karma.

title: S&P Global, Argus invest in oil blockchain VAKT that’s planning tokenization
summary: S&P Global and Argus Media have invested in VAKT, a blockchain-based post-trade solution for the oil sector, which previously raised $57 million.
