These benchmark pricing firms join existing heavyweight shareholders from the energy and banking sectors. The key motivation for their involvement is VAKT's confirmed plan to tokenize oil contracts in the future, promising enhanced information and intelligence flows for energy and commodity markets.

title: Police investigate Friday morning Anderson bank robbery
summary: Anderson police are investigating an armed bank robbery that occurred Friday morning at Old National Bank. A man in his 20s passed a note demanding money and fled on foot with an undisclosed amount of cash. No arrests have been made, and police are asking for the public's help with information.

title: BOA’s CFO Says Spending Remains Strong as Bank’s Loans Grow
summary: Bank of America's CFO, Alastair Borthwick, stated that customer spending and borrowing remain strong despite economic headwinds. He noted that consumer spending increased by 9% in June from the previous year and that corporate balance sheets are healthy. Borthwick also indicated that the bank does not foresee a recession and expects single-digit loan growth, particularly in the wealth-management business.

title: Netflix stock downgraded to ‘Sell’ by Goldman Sachs analysts
summary: Goldman Sachs analysts have downgraded Netflix (NFLX) stock to 'Sell' amidst a significant year-to-date plummet and broader market sell-offs affecting growth stocks. The article discusses the differing opinions among analysts regarding whether investors should buy the dip or sell, highlighting concerns about free cash flow and content spending versus the potential for future growth initiatives like cracking down on password sharing and an ad-supported model.

title: EXCLUSIVE Baidu in talks to sell majority stake in iQIYI, China's answer to Netflix -sources
summary: Baidu Inc is reportedly in talks to sell its controlling stake in iQIYI Inc, China's equivalent of Netflix, in a deal that could value iQIYI at approximately $7 billion. Baidu aims to divest its entire 53% holding as it considers iQIYI a non-core asset and shifts focus to AI and autonomous driving. The potential sale has garnered interest from entities like PAG and China Mobile despite iQIYI's recent stock performance amid a broader Chinese tech sell-off.

title: $6.5-Million Merrill Stock Plan Team in D.C. Goes Indie with Cetera
summary: A Merrill Lynch team in Washington D.C., generating $6.5 million in annual revenue and managing $600 million in assets, has moved to Cetera Financial Group. Led by Dean A. Packard, Scott C. Lowder, and John Vytas Maginnis, the team chose independence to avoid prospecting restrictions common at larger wirehouses and to increase their take-home revenue. This move is part of a broader trend of high-value advisor departures from Merrill Lynch, though Merrill has also been active in recruiting private bankers from competitors.

title: Visa Inc. completes €3.0bn cross-border offering of senior notes | Vietnam | Global law firm
summary: Visa Inc. has completed a €3.0 billion cross-border offering of senior notes, facilitated by Norton Rose Fulbright's Toronto office. The offering included notes due in 2026, 2029, and 2034, with net proceeds intended for general corporate purposes. The issuance involved a syndicate of underwriters including major financial institutions.

title: Indagare Offers Luxury Travel Experiences to Bank of America Clients
summary: Bank of America has partnered with Indagare, a members-only luxury travel-planning company, to offer exclusive travel experiences to its ultra-high-net-worth clients, specifically Diamond Honors members. These experiences include unique in-person and virtual trips to world-renowned locations, designed to provide "behind-the-scenes" access and unforgettable memories. This initiative is part of the enhancements to Bank of America's Preferred Rewards program, aiming to reward clients for their deep relationship with the bank.

title: Big US Banks Led by JPMorgan (NYSE:JPM) Set to Return $80 Billion to Investors
summary: US banking giants, led by JPMorgan Chase & Co., are expected to return $80 billion to shareholders after the Federal Reserve's stress tests. This amount is less than the previous year's elevated returns, which followed a pandemic-induced buyback pause. JPMorgan is projected to lead with $18.9 billion in shareholder returns, with Bank of America and Wells Fargo also making significant returns.

title: Shyft Group Names Vice President, Investor Relations and Group Treasurer
summary: The Shyft Group has appointed Randy Wilson as Vice President, Investor Relations and Group Treasurer, effective June 20, 2022. Wilson brings extensive experience in investor relations, finance, capital markets, and sustainability, most recently leading Investor Relations at Terex Corporation. In his new role, he will oversee all aspects of investor relations and treasury functions for The Shyft Group.

title: BofA (BAC) Offers Versailles, Petra Travel Perks to Lure Ultra Wealthy
summary: Bank of America is introducing exclusive travel perks, including trips to Versailles and Petra, for its ultra-high-net-worth clients. This initiative, in partnership with luxury-travel firm Indagare, aims to attract and retain affluent customers with over $10 million in their accounts, highlighting the competitive nature among financial institutions for wealthy clientele.

title: Virtual reality and indoor ‘tree houses’: Truist unveils banking tech center in uptown
summary: Truist Bank has opened a new 100,000-square-foot Innovation and Technology Center in uptown Charlotte, aiming to fuse tech and finance for a better banking experience. The center features virtual reality labs, "tree houses," and collaborative spaces, intending to propel Truist into the future of digital banking despite recent low rankings in consumer satisfaction for its digital services. The bank also launched an "Innovators in Residence" program with partners like Verizon and Amazon Web Services to explore new technologies.

title: Southern First rolls out new HQ to customers, community
summary: Southern First Bank has unveiled its new five-story, 107,000-square-foot headquarters in Greenville, designed to be warm, welcoming, and progressive, aiming to redefine traditional bank architecture. The new building provides ample space for employees, clients, and community events, reflecting the bank's commitment to its community and its future growth. CEO Art Seaver emphasizes the building as a statement of belief in the future and a tool for recruiting top talent, affirming the bank's long-term vision and client-first mentality.

title: How JPMorgan Chase, Target, Citi, Bank of America, and PayPal are Reporting on Their Complex, Big-Dollar Racial Equity Commitments
summary: This article examines how major corporations like JPMorgan Chase, Target, Citi, Bank of America, and PayPal are reporting progress on their substantial racial equity commitments, ranging from $535 million to $30 billion. It details the specific actions and investments each company has made to advance racial equity, such as supporting Black-owned businesses, increasing affordable housing, and investing in diverse suppliers. The piece emphasizes the importance of transparent reporting on these complex, multi-year pledges.

title: Updated: BofA, Morgan Stanley, Wells Join List of Banks Covering Employees’ Abortion Travel Costs
summary: Following the U.S. Supreme Court's overturning of Roe v. Wade, Bank of America, Morgan Stanley, and Wells Fargo have announced they will reimburse employees' travel expenses for abortion-related healthcare. These banks join others like JPMorgan Chase, Deutsche Bank, Goldman Sachs, and Citigroup, in implementing policies to support employees seeking such services in states where they may become restricted. The move aims to align benefits with diverse healthcare needs amidst changing legal landscapes.

title: JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs and Other Big Banks Will Now Cover Travel Expenses for Employee Abortions
summary: Following the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade, several major banks including JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, Bank of America, and Morgan Stanley announced they will cover travel expenses for employees seeking abortions. These companies already offer abortion coverage in their medical benefits but are extending it to include travel to ensure equitable access to healthcare for their nationwide workforce, especially considering new state-level restrictions on abortion access. Citigroup had made a similar announcement earlier in the year in response to Texas laws.

title: ICICI Bank Offers Among The Best Risk-Reward Globally, Says Jefferies
summary: Jefferies believes ICICI Bank offers one of the best risk-reward ratios globally due to its high return-on-assets and strong positioning for Indian bank credit growth. The firm maintains a 'buy' rating on the stock with a target price of Rs 1,070, citing projected profit CAGR of 17% over FY22-24 and an ROE of 16%. ICICI Bank is also one of only two Nifty Bank constituents with unanimous 'buy' recommendations from analysts.

title: JPMorgan, Citi, Goldman, Wells Fargo and Bank of America will cover out-of-state abortion costs for employees
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co., Bank of America Corp., Goldman Sachs Group Inc., Wells Fargo & Co. and Citigroup Inc. have all announced that they will cover out-of-state travel expenses for employees seeking abortions. This decision comes in the wake of the U.S. Supreme Court's ruling to overturn Roe v. Wade. These major banks join other large corporations in offering such benefits.

title: Yen’s True Value Could Offer Support Once BOJ Pivots, BofA Says
summary: Bank of America analysts suggest that the Japanese yen's fair value could provide significant support once the Bank of Japan shifts its monetary policy or if the US economy nears a recession. Despite trading at a 24-year low against the dollar, BofA's models indicate the yen is undervalued, with the USD/JPY's equilibrium estimated to be around 90.74, about 49% stronger than its current trading level. This analysis highlights the potential for a substantial rebound in the yen's value.

title: Katrina Evans
summary: Katrina Evans, Executive Vice President at KeyCorp, is highlighted for her 30-plus years of adventurous leadership and significant contributions to the company. She has spearheaded growth in marketing, communications, and analytics, orchestrated expansion of a multibillion-dollar community benefits plan, and fostered diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives. Her leadership style emphasizes authenticity and empowering others.

title: Are Bank Stocks Undervalued?
summary: Despite fears of a potential recession driving down bank stock prices, many high-quality banks appear undervalued, trading at a significant discount compared to historical recession lows. Rising net interest margins due to Federal Reserve rate hikes could provide a tailwind, which analysts believe is not being fully priced into current valuations. Long-term investors may find attractive opportunities in these undervalued bank stocks, particularly those with wide economic moats like Wells Fargo, JPMorgan Chase, U.S. Bancorp, and Bank of America.

title: Sociedad Minera Cerro Verde obtiene préstamo sindicado
summary: Sociedad Minera Cerro Verde, a Peruvian mining company, secured a syndicated loan of $350 million from a consortium of international banks. The funds will be used to repay a debt originally incurred in 2014 and modified in 2017. Several law firms advised on the transaction for both Cerro Verde and the lending banks.

title: News | Google in Talks To Buy Chicago’s Thompson Center
summary: Google is in negotiations to purchase the James R. Thompson Center in Chicago's Loop business district, a move that could significantly boost the area. This deal is the latest in Google's history of strategic real estate acquisitions in Chicago, and it could provide space for thousands of additional employees. The acquisition could also influence Prime Group's redevelopment plans for the building and the state of Illinois's prior agreement to buy back office space.

title: Judge narrows San Diego, Baltimore bond collusion cases against big banks
summary: A federal judge has narrowed antitrust claims brought by San Diego and Baltimore against eight major banks, dismissing some breach of fiduciary claims but ruling it was premature to decide on fraudulent concealment claims for San Diego. The cities accuse banks, including Barclays, Citigroup, Goldman Sachs, and JPMorgan Chase, of colluding to manipulate interest rates on tax-exempt municipal bonds (VRDOs) between 2008 and 2016, leading to increased costs for local governments.

title: BP, Shell To Pay Employee Travel Costs After Abortion Ruling
summary: Following the U.S. Supreme Court's reversal of Roe v. Wade, BP Plc and Shell Plc announced they would cover travel expenses for U.S. employees needing to access health services not available near their homes. This makes them the first major oil companies to implement such policies. Both companies maintain significant operations in Texas, a state expected to ban or severely restrict abortions, joining other corporate giants in expanding employee health benefits.

title: Bank of America Forms Natural-Resources, Energy-Transition Group
summary: Bank of America has established a new investment banking group focused on natural resources and the energy transition. This move aligns with a broader trend on Wall Street to cater to clients prioritizing decarbonization and sustainability. The bank aims to support clients with their net-zero carbon-emission goals by offering strategic advice and transaction support.

title: U.S. Banks Are a Bargain. Bank of America and 7 More Stocks to Buy.
summary: Oppenheimer suggests that U.S. financial institutions are significantly undervalued and offer a strong buying opportunity despite market volatility. This assessment comes as Bank of America indicates that lenders with extensive loan portfolios will face impacts from a deteriorating economy. The article highlights that these banks are currently trading at bargain prices.

title: Banks Get Burned by Risky Debt, Imperiling Buyout Activity
summary: Investment banks, including Bank of America, Credit Suisse, and Goldman Sachs, are facing potential losses of billions of dollars on leveraged buyout loans they committed to finance before market conditions deteriorated. These losses are expected to further cool down deal-making activity in the market. The banks agreed to provide these loans when demand for such debt was high, but the market has since soured.

title: Bank shares slightly higher
summary: The RG/BSX Index rose by 0.19 percent to 2,246.62, driven by gains in Argus Group Holdings Ltd. and Bermuda Aviation Services Ltd. Argus saw a 0.6 percent increase, while Bermuda Aviation Services surged by 57.1 percent. The Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son Limited also closed higher, up 0.77 percent.

title: Truist is the latest bank to raise its minimum wage. Here’s how much workers will make.
summary: Truist Financial announced it will raise its minimum wage nationwide to $22 per hour starting October 1, impacting about 14,000 employees. This move positions Truist's new minimum wage among the highest in the banking industry and follows similar increases by other Charlotte-based banks like Bank of America, Wells Fargo, Ally Financial, and Fifth Third Bancorp, amidst a competitive labor market.

title: Mounting pay pressure at banks as Truist, JPMorgan hike minimum wages
summary: Amidst a tight job market and high inflation, major banks like Truist and JPMorgan Chase are increasing their minimum hourly wages for employees, following a trend set by other large financial institutions. These wage hikes are seen as crucial investments to retain talent and reduce turnover, although they may slightly impact bank earnings. The industry recognizes the need to stay competitive by offering better pay and benefits, while also emphasizing culture and career advancement opportunities.

title: Productos Life de Banco Santander superan el millón de clientes
summary: Banco Santander Chile announced that its Life family of accounts has surpassed one million clients, marking a significant milestone in financial inclusion. The Life products, primarily the Cuenta Corriente Life, aim to provide accessible banking services without minimum income requirements. These products, which include various tiers like Plan Santander Life and Plan Santander Life – LATAM Pass, offer a range of benefits and also incorporate the Meritolife program to reward good financial behavior.

title: Highest FD interest rates: SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, POTD compared, check here
summary: Fixed deposit interest rates are rising after the RBI hiked repo rates to combat inflation. While SBI, HDFC Bank, and ICICI Bank have increased their FD rates, the interest rates on small savings schemes like the Post Office Term Deposit (POTD) remained unchanged for the July-September quarter. This article compares the current FD rates offered by banks with those of POTD, showing that for three-five year FDs, POTD offers significantly better interest rates.

title: Proof Point: Canada’s economy is headed for a recession
summary: RBC Economics predicts Canada's economy will experience a moderate and short-lived recession in 2023 due to inflation, labor shortages, and rising interest rates. While the jobless rate will increase, it is expected to be less severe than in previous downturns, and the higher interest rates are deemed necessary to control inflation. The authors suggest that this economic contraction will be reversible once inflation subsides, allowing central banks to ease rates.

title: KT pushes ahead with K Bank IPO
summary: KT Corp is proceeding with an Initial Public Offering (IPO) for its digital banking subsidiary, K Bank, aiming to raise up to $1 billion. This move is part of KT's broader strategy to evolve from a traditional telecommunications company into a digital platform operator, diversifying its revenue streams through financial services, content, e-commerce, and cloud offerings. K Bank, in which KT holds a significant stake through BC Card, narrowed its net loss in 2021 and has established a strategic partnership with Shinhan Financial Group to integrate AI, metaverse, NFT, big data, and robotics technologies with financial services.

title: U.S. bank profits to tumble on higher bad loan reserves
summary: U.S. bank profits are expected to fall significantly in the second quarter due to increased loan loss reserves in anticipation of a potential recession. JPMorgan Chase, Citigroup, Wells Fargo, and Bank of America are projected to see substantial profit declines, as they build up reserves after releasing them during the pandemic recovery. While loan growth and higher interest rates are boosting net interest income, concerns about a severe recession and its impact on actual loan losses remain.

title: Santander and Formula 1® challenge entrepreneurs worldwide to find next-generation sustainable solutions
summary: Santander and Formula 1® have launched a global challenge called "Santander X Global Challenge | Countdown to Zero" for start-ups and scale-ups across 11 countries. This initiative aims to find innovative and sustainable solutions for the automotive industry in areas such as mobility, logistics, transport, and carbon offset alternatives. The six winning projects will share 120,000 euros in prizes and gain access to Santander X 100, a community offering resources for growth, aligning with F1's commitment to achieving Net-Zero Carbon emissions by 2030.

title: Chile eleva su tasa de interés a un máximo histórico de 9,75%
summary: Chile's Central Bank has raised its monetary policy rate to a record high of 9.75% in a unanimous decision to combat inflation, which reached 12.5% in June. This marks the ninth consecutive increase since July 2021 and follows a similar move by the US Federal Reserve, contributing to global financial tightening. The country faces economic risks including a significant depreciation of the Chilean peso and falling copper prices, prompting the government to announce a $120 bonus for vulnerable citizens.

title: Front-running scandal rocks a $31 billion investing giant
summary: India's $465 billion mutual fund industry is facing scrutiny after Axis Asset Management Co., one of the nation's largest asset managers and partly owned by Schroders, sacked two employees, including its chief dealer, amidst a front-running scandal. Regulators are investigating potential breaches of securities law and the case highlights increased compliance challenges in the booming Indian investment sector. The probe has led to a lawsuit for wrongful termination by one of the former employees and raised questions about compliance during pandemic work-from-home periods, predicting tighter regulations for fund managers.

title: JPMorgan Q2 Profit Down 28%; Results Miss Estimates
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. reported a 28% decline in second-quarter profit, hurt by higher noninterest expenses and a net credit reserve build. Both earnings per share ($2.76 vs. $2.91 expected) and revenues ($30.72 billion vs. $31.95 billion expected) missed analysts' expectations. The provision for credit losses was a net benefit of $1.10 billion, reflecting loan growth and a modest deterioration in the economic outlook.

title: Morgan Stanley Hit by Banking Slump as Recession Fears Loom
summary: Morgan Stanley's investment banking revenue significantly declined by 55% to $1.07 billion, worse than analyst predictions, as capital markets slowed amidst rising recession fears. The bank also incurred $413 million in mark-to-market losses on corporate loans. This performance highlights a challenging quarter for Wall Street, attributed to a gloomy economic outlook.

title: Earnings slide ongoing for banks; BofA Q2 profit dips 32%
summary: Bank of America reported a 32% dip in Q2 2022 profits compared to the previous year, following a trend seen among other major U.S. banks like JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, and Citigroup. While profits were lower due to robust 2021 results boosted by released loan loss reserves, the bank's revenue increased to $22.7 billion, driven by higher interest rates and increased lending. The outlook for the second half of the year remains a focus due to potential recession risks from inflation and Federal Reserve actions.

title: Bank of America Hires Barclays Banker Ahuja for Technology Deals
summary: Bank of America Corp. has hired Akhil Ahuja from Barclays Plc to join its technology investment banking team. Ahuja will commence his role as a managing director in October, based in Palo Alto, California, focusing on technology deals for the bank.

title: Bank OZK Agrees to Pay $45M to Settle Claims it Misled Investors
summary: Bank OZK has agreed to a $45 million settlement in a class-action lawsuit. The lawsuit alleged that the bank misled investors about the health of two commercial real estate loans, which resulted in a significant stock drop after a $45 million write-off in 2018. The settlement will provide average payments to those who purchased the bank's stock between February 2016 and October 2018.

title: State Street Corp. stock underperforms Wednesday when compared to competitors
summary: State Street Corp. (STT) stock underperformed on Wednesday, July 20, 2022, falling 0.53% to $66.97, despite a generally positive trading session for the broader market. The stock closed significantly below its 52-week high and lagged behind some of its key competitors like JPMorgan Chase & Co., Bank of America Corp., and Citigroup Inc. Trading volume for State Street Corp. was also below its 50-day average.

title: 5 Best Joint Checking Accounts [2025 ]
summary: This article reviews the five best joint checking accounts for 2025, highlighting options like Ally Bank for overall convenience, Capital One for parents and kids, and Axos Bank for various features. It also details key features to look for in a joint account, such as interest rates and fees, and provides steps for getting approved and improving personal finances.

title: Bank of Montreal establishes tech hub in Irving to fuel U.S. expansion
summary: The Bank of Montreal (BMO) is establishing a new tech hub in Irving, Texas, to support its U.S. expansion and upcoming acquisition of Bank of the West. The new hub will initially hire 50 tech and operations employees and will be located in BMO's existing Irving office. Dallas-Fort Worth was chosen over other cities like Charlotte and Atlanta due to its rapid tech growth and BMO's existing presence in the area.

title: Bank of America branch in Dilworth to remain closed permanently
summary: Bank of America is permanently closing its Dilworth branch at 1235 East Blvd. in Charlotte, which has been temporarily shut down since the Covid-19 pandemic. The closure, effective October 25, reflects a growing trend of customers shifting to digital banking channels for everyday transactions. Several other Bank of America branches remain in the vicinity.

title: Rich Americans Keep Borrowing, Defying Economic Gloom
summary: Wealthy Americans continued to increase their borrowing in the first half of the year, despite rising interest rates and a downturn in the stock market. This trend was evident in the double-digit loan growth reported by the wealth-management divisions of Morgan Stanley and Bank of America, largely driven by mortgages and asset-backed loans. This behavior contradicts the general economic gloom.

title: US Banking Customers Will Soon Demand These Features. Does Your Mobile App Offer Them?
summary: Mobile banking customers are increasingly demanding more sophisticated features in their apps beyond basic tasks, with 54% of US online adults wanting to complete any financial task via mobile. Research from an unnamed source identifies digital wallet integration, customer-facing data management tools, and subscription management tools as three key future "must-have" features. Banks that adopt these features, like Bank of America with its "Erica" tool, can differentiate their offerings and appeal to younger customers.

title: Bank of Montreal Taps North Texas for its Newest Tech Hub
summary: The Bank of Montreal (BMO) is establishing a new tech hub in North Texas, planning to hire 50 new employees to add to its existing 250-person DFW workforce. This move is part of BMO's strategy to expand its U.S. operations and follows similar investments by other major banks like JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, and PNC Bank in the Dallas-Fort Worth region. The Irving tech hub will be BMO's first outside of Toronto and Chicago, focusing on areas like cybersecurity and engineering.

title: State Street Corp. stock underperforms Monday when compared to competitors despite daily gains
summary: State Street Corp. (STT) stock saw a modest gain of 0.35% on Monday, closing at $68.40, marking its third consecutive day of increases amidst a favorable overall market. Despite this, the company's stock underperformed compared to competitors like JPMorgan Chase & Co., Bank of America Corp., and Citigroup Inc., which all recorded higher percentage gains. The stock remained significantly below its 52-week high, and trading volume was below its 50-day average.

title: MasTec Acquires IEA for Wind, Solar Energy Infrastructure Expertise
summary: MasTec has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Infrastructure and Energy Alternatives Inc. (IEA) in a cash-and-stock transaction valued at $14 per IEA share, totaling approximately $1.1 billion. This acquisition aims to expand MasTec's service capabilities in renewable energy infrastructure, particularly wind and solar projects, and is expected to close in late Q4 2022. The deal combines IEA's expertise in utility-scale wind and solar projects with MasTec's existing infrastructure services, anticipating increased scale and capacity to meet growing demand for renewable power generation.

title: U.S. watchdogs scrutinise UBS over staff messaging
summary: U.S. regulators are investigating UBS Group for not properly documenting staff communications, part of a broader probe into financial institutions. This scrutiny follows similar actions against J.P. Morgan Securities, which was fined $200 million for widespread failures in preserving communications, and Bank of America, which set aside $200 million for a related regulatory matter. UBS is cooperating with the ongoing investigations by the SEC and CFTC.

title: My Experience Visiting A Capital One Cafe
summary: The author shares their first experience visiting a Capital One Cafe, highlighting its unique blend of a coffee shop and bank. They found it to be a quiet place to work, offering 50% off beverages for Capital One cardholders, and noted the presence of "Cafe Ambassadors" for banking questions without sales pressure. The article concludes that these cafes present a pleasant alternative to traditional coffee shops like Starbucks, especially for Capital One customers.

title: Fifth Third Bancorp stock underperforms Tuesday when compared to competitors
summary: Shares of Fifth Third Bancorp (FITB) fell by 3.10% on Tuesday, closing at $33.15, underperforming both the broader stock market and its competitors. The decline occurred during a generally rough trading session where the S&P 500 Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average also saw losses. The stock's performance placed it significantly below its 52-week high.

title: China's Real Estate Problems - Northern Trust - Commentaries
summary: China's real estate sector, a major economic driver, is experiencing a significant slump due to developer debt defaults and diminished homebuyer confidence, exacerbated by policies aimed at reining in leverage. This crisis, marked by plunging home sales and mortgage payment boycotts, poses a substantial risk to the Chinese economy, banking system, and local government revenues. Policymakers face a difficult challenge in balancing deleveraging with economic growth and preventing broader financial spillovers.

title: From “Buy the Dip” to “Wait and See”
summary: This article discusses the shift in investor sentiment from "buying the dip" to a "wait and see" approach, driven by high inflation, rising interest rates, and market volatility. It highlights the impact of the Federal Reserve's tightening cycle on asset classes like stocks and cryptocurrencies, investor caution due to corporate bond risks, and suggests considering inverse ETFs like SPDN for managing portfolio beta in turbulent markets.

title: Marriott, RIDA Development, and Ares Management Break Ground on Gaylord Pacific Resort and Convention Center
summary: Marriott International, RIDA Development Corporation, and Ares Management have broken ground on the Gaylord Pacific Resort and Convention Center in Chula Vista, California. This 1.8 million-square-foot project will feature 1,600 hotel rooms, extensive convention space, dining options, and a waterpark, with an expected opening in summer 2025. The $1.275 billion development marks the Gaylord Hotels brand's expansion to the West Coast and is anticipated to create over 10,000 construction jobs and 4,000 permanent jobs, significantly boosting the region's economy.

title: Barclays latest global bank ensnared in U.S. 'Whatsapp' probes
summary: Barclays has announced it set aside $200 million to cover potential costs arising from a U.S. regulatory probe into the use of unauthorized messaging apps like WhatsApp by its employees. This move follows similar actions by other major banks including Credit Suisse, Deutsche Bank, and several Wall Street firms, as regulators intensify their scrutiny of unrecorded communications. The probe highlights a broader crackdown on financial institutions to ensure compliance with record-keeping rules, especially concerning market-sensitive discussions.

title: Extending upmarket in US commercial banking
summary: US midcap and regional banks face challenges from declining net interest margins and increased competition. The article suggests that expanding upmarket by serving larger commercial clients with more sophisticated financial needs, especially through fee-based treasury management and investment banking products, can drive growth and revenue stability. Banks should consider five strategic actions: reviewing processes, targeting differentiation, developing talent, aligning product offerings with client needs, and focusing on client experience.

title: Banamex, la filial mexicana de Citi, podría atraer ofertas de hasta US$8.000 millones
summary: Citigroup's Mexican unit, Banamex, is expected to attract bids between $7 billion and $8 billion as the number of potential buyers narrows. Key bidders include Grupo Financiero Banorte, Carlos Slim's Grupo Financiero Inbursa, mining magnate Germán Larrea, and Grupo Financiero Mifel. Banco Santander previously withdrew after its $6 billion offer was rejected.

title: TD to buy Cowen for US$1.3-billion, doubling down on ambitious U.S. expansion plans
summary: Toronto-Dominion Bank (TD-T) is set to acquire New York-based investment bank Cowen Inc. for US$1.3-billion, accelerating its U.S. capital markets expansion. This acquisition follows TD's US$13.4-billion bid for First Horizon Corp. and aims to strengthen TD's presence in U.S. equities, M&A advisory, and research, areas where it previously faced gaps. The deal is part of TD's aggressive U.S. strategy, coming after a significant investment in First Horizon and a recent executive team overhaul.

title: Una empresas argentina que desarrolla soluciones digitales de pagos recibió una inversión millonaria
summary: Geopagos, an Argentine company specializing in digital payment solutions, has secured a significant investment of US$35 million in its first institutional funding round. The funding, led by Riverwood Capital with participation from Endeavor Catalyst, will be used to develop new omnichannel payment products, enable new acceptance methods, and open its API platform. Geopagos serves major financial institutions and fintechs across 15 Latin American countries, processing over 150 million transactions and more than US$5 billion annually.

title: Barclays hires Isaac Davies as Treasurer, Europe
summary: Barclays has appointed Isaac Davies as Treasurer for its European operations. Davies brings over 30 years of finance experience, including previous roles at Goldman Sachs, Lehman Brothers, and a prior nine-year tenure at Barclays as Asia Pacific Treasurer. Based in Dublin, he will report to Jasper Hanebuth and Mark Washtell, and is expected to rejoin the bank in November 2022.

title: ESIX Could Be Great for ESG, Small-Cap Rebounds
summary: The SPDR S&P SmallCap 600 ESG ETF (ESIX) is highlighted as a potentially strong performer for investors seeking exposure to small-cap equities with ESG principles, especially given anticipated small-cap rebounds and economic forecasts. Despite ESG funds and small-caps lagging in early 2022, analysts are bullish on small-cap prospects due to better earnings guidance and recession preparedness. ESIX offers a balanced mix of growth and value stocks within the small-cap segment, historically a rewarding combination.

title: Geopagos, fintech argentina de aceptación de pagos, levantó US$35 millones • Contxto
summary: Geopagos, an Argentine fintech specializing in payment acceptance solutions, has raised $35 million in its first institutional financing round led by Riverwood Capital. The company, founded in 2013, provides technology for businesses to launch or scale their payment processing operations in 15 Latin American countries. This investment will accelerate Geopagos's growth across the region and increase R&D efforts.

title: Use of credit cards, personal loans surges, but 'it's not a red flag,’ expert says
summary: The use of credit cards and personal loans reached record highs in the second quarter of 2022, driven by an increase in loans to subprime borrowers. TransUnion's Michele Raneri notes that while delinquencies are approaching pre-pandemic levels, a strong job market prevents this surge from being a "red flag." The primary indicator of a consumer's ability to repay is employment, which remains robust despite high inflation and rising interest rates.

title: Morgan Stanley to pay $200 million to resolve U.S. record-keeping probe
summary: Morgan Stanley has agreed to pay $200 million to U.S. regulators to settle investigations into its record-keeping practices, specifically regarding unapproved messaging platforms used by employees. The bank will pay $125 million to the SEC and $75 million to the CFTC. This settlement follows similar issues faced by other major banks like Bank of America, Citigroup, and Barclays, as regulators crack down on the logging of employee communications during the shift to remote work.

title: Morgan Stanley job posting points to wide-ranging crypto plans
summary: Morgan Stanley Wealth Management is seeking a product development manager to focus on building new crypto products across various business lines, as indicated by a recent LinkedIn job posting. This move suggests the financial giant is intensifying its commitment to cryptocurrency offerings, looking to expand beyond the private passive fund it launched in March 2021. The new role aims to create packaged products and indexes, potentially collaborating with over 200 asset management firms to enhance product usage for financial advisors.

title: Idaho Rep. Russ Fulcher joins House members’ letter opposing major banks’ abortion policies
summary: Idaho Rep. Russ Fulcher and 43 other U.S. House members sent a letter to the CEOs of eight major banks, including Bank of America and JPMorgan Chase, to express opposition to their policies covering employee travel expenses for abortions. The letter argues these policies are morally wrong and a violation of fiduciary responsibilities to shareholders, as they use investor resources for a social policy debate. Blaine Conzatti of the Idaho Family Policy Center also opposes such policies and is working on legislation to prohibit Idaho businesses from paying for abortion-related travel.

title: Archroma to Acquire the Textile Effects Business of The Huntsman Corp.
summary: Archroma has agreed to acquire the Textile Effects business from Huntsman Corp. The terms of the deal were not disclosed, but the acquisition is expected to close in the first half of 2023. This merger aims to create a powerhouse in sustainable and innovative textile solutions, combining the rich legacies of several industry pioneers.

title: Bank price finishes higher
summary: The RG/BSX Index remained unchanged at 2,364.05, despite activity from Argus Group Holdings Ltd. The Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son Limited saw a notable increase of 2.32% on the New York Stock Exchange. The article details these specific movements in the stock market.

title: JPMorgan Chase Avoided Public Punishment From CFPB Under Trump After Discovery of Alleged Fake Accounts
summary: JPMorgan Chase (JPM) allegedly avoided public sanctions from the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) during the Trump administration for creating fake accounts, despite the agency identifying serious instances at four banks after the Wells Fargo scandal. The CFPB's enforcement unit investigated Chase for several years but closed the matter in early 2020. This incident highlights a broader trend during the Trump administration where financial institutions like TD Bank (TD) also faced private reprimands instead of public penalties for similar misconduct, drawing criticism from lawmakers like Senator Elizabeth Warren.

title: UBS’s Broker Count Has Slipped to Almost 5,600–Sources
summary: Headcount at UBS Wealth Management USA has fallen to just over 5,600, a significant decline from 2018 figures and below publicly reported numbers for its Americas unit. This reduction is partly strategic, as UBS focuses on more productive advisors, although the firm is also becoming more aggressive in recruiting veteran producers to boost net new fee-based assets. The overall trend of declining sales forces and an aging workforce is not unique to UBS, affecting other wirehouses as well.

title: PNC Drops Another Type of Fee After Overhauling Overdraft Policy
summary: PNC Financial Services Group Inc. has eliminated non-sufficient fund (NSF) fees, joining other large banks in removing charges that have drawn criticism from politicians and consumer advocates. These fees were previously charged when a transaction was returned due to insufficient funds in a customer's account. PNC had already removed NSF fees from its Virtual Wallet Spend feature and is now extending this policy to other personal checking-account options.

title: Wells Fargo plans retreat from mortgage business
summary: Wells Fargo & Co. is planning to significantly reduce its mortgage business after years of regulatory scrutinized and changes in leadership. The bank, which once held a dominant share of the U.S. home loan market, aims to focus on lending to existing customers and scale back operations like correspondent mortgage lending and third-party servicing. This strategic shift reflects a broader industry trend among large banks to moderate their mortgage exposure following the 2008 financial crisis and ongoing regulatory challenges.

title: Citigroup Inc. stock underperforms Tuesday when compared to competitors despite daily gains
summary: Shares of Citigroup Inc. (C) rose 0.20% on Tuesday to $54.18, despite a broadly positive trading session for the stock market. However, Citigroup underperformed compared to key competitors like JPMorgan Chase & Co., Bank of America Corp., and Wells Fargo & Co., which saw larger gains. The company's stock closed significantly below its 52-week high, and trading volume was below its 50-day average.

title: FACTBOX U.S., European banks could lose over $5 bln from risky buyout loans
summary: Major U.S. and European banks are facing significant write-downs on leveraged and bridge loans due to rising interest rates and market turmoil. Bank of America, Citigroup, Wells Fargo, Credit Suisse, JPMorgan, Deutsche Bank, and Barclays have reported substantial losses, collectively exceeding $1 billion, in the second quarter of 2022. This comes as higher rates make it harder for banks to offload debt, leading to mark-to-market losses on these risky buyout loans.

title: TD Bank opens new branch in Charlotte region — 10 years after it closed
summary: TD Bank is re-opening a branch in Fort Mill, S.C., along Charlotte Highway, a decade after closing its previous location there. The New Jersey-based bank maintained the lease on the property and plans to offer an "advice center" format to cater to the growing area. While not expanding further into Charlotte proper for now, TD Bank holds a significant deposit market share in South Carolina and maintains several offices across both Carolinas.

title: Is BJ’s Wholesale stock a ‘buy’ after record Q2 results?
summary: BJ’s Wholesale Club Holdings Inc (NYSE: BJ) reported record results for its fiscal second quarter, leading its shares to an all-time high and prompting a raised full-year outlook. A Bank of America analyst recommends purchasing the stock, citing its strong value proposition in an inflationary environment and robust membership trends. The company's net income and revenue significantly increased year-over-year, and adjusted EPS guidance was raised for the full financial year.

title: Who Owns Ford Motor Company? It’s Complicated
summary: Ford Motor Company, founded in 1903, uses a dual share structure with Class A and Class B shares, where Class B shares have significantly higher voting power despite representing only 2% of outstanding shares. While institutional investors like Vanguard and BlackRock hold the largest stakes in the publicly traded company, Bill Ford, Henry Ford's great-grandson, is the largest individual owner and maintains control through his significant holding of Class B shares. The company is actively restructuring, including separating its traditional ICE business (Ford Blue) from its EV business (Ford Model e).

title: BofA Adds Grubhub Food-Delivery Membership to Its Card Perks
summary: Bank of America has partnered with Grubhub to offer a complimentary one-year Grubhub+ membership to its existing debit and credit cardholders. This perk allows customers to receive online food takeout with no delivery fees, enhancing the bank's card offerings and providing value to its customers. The membership typically costs $9.99 per month.

title: US, European banks could lose over $5bn from risky buyout loans
summary: Top US and European banks face potential losses of over $5 billion from leveraged and bridge loans due to rising interest rates and a slowdown in the leveraged buyout market. Banks like Bank of America are particularly exposed, having committed to financing large buyout deals, while difficulties in offloading debt to investors are forcing underwriters to sell at a discount. The market disruption is primarily attributed to the Federal Reserve's aggressive monetary policy tightening to combat inflation.

title: Highwoods Properties Closes $203M Buy of Legacy Union SIX50 in Charlotte
summary: Highwoods Properties, Inc. has acquired the Legacy Union SIX50 building in Charlotte, NC for $203 million. The 18-story, 367,000-square-foot property is currently 79% leased and sits within the Charlotte CBD's Legacy Union mixed-use development, adjacent to Highwoods-owned Bank of America Tower. Lincoln Harris and Goldman Sachs Asset Management were the sellers, with Lincoln Harris retaining management and leasing responsibilities.

title: First Internet Bank launches small-business account
summary: First Internet Bank has launched a new checking account, "Do More Business Checking," specifically designed for small-business owners. This product allows business owners to earn interest, make unlimited transactions, and link various financial accounts for a comprehensive view of both business and personal finances. The initiative aims to simplify day-to-day operations for small businesses and tap into a significant market opportunity previously dominated by third-party providers and fintechs.

title: Bank share price declines on NYSE
summary: The Royal Gazette/BSX Index increased by 1.59 percent to 2,401.75, primarily driven by insurance stocks. While Argus Group Holdings Ltd and BF&M Ltd saw their share prices rise, The Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son Limited experienced a decline of 3.38 percent on the New York Stock Exchange.

title: 3 Arkansas Banks Add Branches for Growth
summary: Three Arkansas banks, Arvest Bank, Encore Bank, and Citizens Bank, are expanding their physical presence. Arvest is opening new full-service branches in Little Rock and Springfield, Missouri. Encore Bank is upgrading loan production offices in Charlotte, North Carolina, and Nashville, Tennessee, into full-service branches, while Citizens Bank is adding a fourth office in Hot Springs.

title: 5 Handy Online Payment Partners for Your Convenience
summary: This article highlights five convenient online payment partners in the Philippines: BancNet, DragonPay, PesoPay, WeePay, and PayEasy. These platforms cater to various payment methods, including bank accounts, over-the-counter transactions, credit cards, and e-wallets, making online commerce more accessible for both consumers and merchants. The aim is to simplify online transactions by offering diverse options for paying bills and purchasing goods.

title: Dive Deposits: BofA, RBC eye ‘balance’ in data- or emotion-based stances
summary: Bank of America and Royal Bank of Canada are approaching recent narratives with contrasting communication styles. While BofA uses data to highlight a 90% drop in overdraft-related revenue following policy changes, RBC appeals to emotion in its push for employees to return to the office more frequently, emphasizing human connection without concrete mandates. Despite their different methods, both banks mention the concept of "balance" in their statements regarding these distinct issues.

title: MEDC approves incentives for EV battery, parts manufacturing
summary: The Michigan Economic Development Corp. (MEDC) has approved incentives for electric vehicle battery and parts manufacturing. This includes a $2.5 million grant for Dana Thermal Products LLC to establish a new facility in Auburn Hills for EV battery cooling plates, creating 200 jobs. Additionally, the MEDC supported a procedural step for LG Energy Solution to expand its battery manufacturing site in Holland, potentially facilitating $500 million in private bonds for the project.

title: MUFG’s Winter joins Lloyds Bank
summary: Lloyds Banking Group has appointed John Winter, former MUFG CEO for EMEA, as CEO of corporate and institutional banking, effective September 1st. Winter brings almost four decades of experience to the role and will lead the unit supporting corporate and financial institutions with turnover above £100 million. This appointment is part of a broader leadership restructuring effort at Lloyds Banking Group following a new internal structure implemented on July 1, 2022.

title: JPMorgan Chase Applies to Open Its First Downtown Baltimore Branch
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. is set to open its first downtown Baltimore branch at 100 S. Charles St. in 2023, following an application filed with the federal Office of the Comptroller of the Currency. This move is part of the bank's aggressive expansion strategy in the region, aiming to open 70 new branches across Maryland, Washington, D.C., and Virginia by the end of 2025, doubling its initial goal. The new downtown branch will be Chase's seventh in Baltimore City and contributes to 13 total in Greater Baltimore.

title: Ryan McCormack v. Dingdong (Cayman) Ltd. et al: Class Action Complaint
summary: This article reports on a class action complaint filed by Ryan McCormack against Dingdong (Cayman) Ltd. and numerous other defendants, including individuals and financial institutions. The complaint, alleging fraud related to investment and listed securities, was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York on August 25, 2022. The filing identifies the key parties involved and the nature of the allegations.

title: Wind-Down of a Global Broker’s Equity Business
summary: FTI Consulting advised a top-tier global broker in the orderly wind-down of its equity business, which included structured equity finance, inter-dealer equity brokerage, and equity clearing services. The decision was prompted by a mismatch with the company's risk appetite and increased funding requirements. FTI Consulting helped plan, implement, and monitor the wind-down, ensuring all positions were closed and regulators were satisfied, with the process completed ahead of schedule.

title: NJ India, SBI and HDFC are top three distributors in terms of gross commission
summary: NJ India, SBI, and HDFC were the top three mutual fund distributors by gross commission in FY 2022, with NJ India receiving Rs. 1300 crore. SBI led in average AUM, reaching Rs. 1.20 lakh crore, followed by NJ India and HDFC Bank. The data highlights significant commission contributions from associated fund houses for several banks, such as SBI, HDFC, Axis, and ICICI.

title: What is quantitative easing and how does it impact markets?
summary: Quantitative easing (QE) is a monetary policy where central banks purchase assets to increase money supply and stimulate economic growth, typically used when interest rates are low and growth is stagnant. While it can stabilize economies and lower longer-term interest rates, QE carries risks such as inflation, asset bubbles, and income inequality. Its impact on financial markets includes boosting stock performance by lowering interest rates and making risk-on assets more appealing, and affecting exchange rates by devaluing the currency, which makes exports cheaper but imports more expensive.

title: Bank of America Beefs Up Tech Offerings as Digital Logins Rise to a Record
summary: Bank of America is increasing its investment in digital channels due to a record number of customers moving their transactions online. Client logins to the bank's electronic platforms reached 1 billion in July and 2.8 billion in the second quarter, marking an 11% increase. The new investments will focus on enhancing budgeting tools, financial planning, app personalization, and security features.

title: Bank loses 2.31% on the NYSE
summary: The RG/BSX Index rose by 3.70% this week, with four advancers and two decliners. While most Bermudan stocks saw gains, the Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son Limited experienced a 2.31% drop on the New York Stock Exchange. The index was down marginally for the day due to Bermuda Aviation Services Ltd. declining.

title: Huntington Bancshares Inc. stock outperforms market despite losses on the day
summary: Huntington Bancshares Inc. (HBAN) saw its stock fall by 2.64% on Friday, despite a broader market downturn where the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average experienced larger declines. The stock's performance outpaced several competitors, including Bank of America Corp., Fifth Third Bancorp, and F.N.B. Corp., even as it snapped a three-day winning streak. Trading volume for HBAN was below its 50-day average, with the stock closing $4.15 below its 52-week high.

title: Workspace Property Trust Buys Suburban Office Portfolio from Griffin Realty Trust for $1.1B
summary: Workspace Property Trust, leading a consortium of investors, has acquired a controlling interest in a national portfolio of suburban office buildings from Griffin Realty Trust for approximately $1.1 billion. The portfolio includes 41 properties across eight states, totaling 8 million square feet, with many being single-tenant, net-leased assets. This acquisition highlights a growing trend favoring suburban office properties, driven by demographic shifts and the perceived benefits of suburban locations over urban centers.

title: Atlantic Union Bank Names Sherry Williams Chief Risk Officer
summary: Atlantic Union Bank has appointed Sherry Williams as its new Chief Risk Officer, effective by October 2022. Williams will oversee the company's enterprise and regulatory risk management functions. She brings 26 years of experience from previous roles at Amalgamated Bank, PwC, SunTrust Bank, State of Georgia, and Ernst & Young LLP, holding a doctorate in business administration and several professional certifications.

title: Associated Bank to consolidate 7 branches in Wisconsin, 3 in Northeast Wisconsin
summary: Associated Bank announced plans to consolidate seven branches in Wisconsin, including three in Northeast Wisconsin, starting November 18. This move is attributed to an industry-wide trend favoring online banking. The bank will offer new roles to impacted employees where available and also plans to close six branches in Illinois.

title: Newmark Facilitates $260 Million Financing of Iconic Plaza District Office Building in Midtown Manhattan
summary: Newmark has arranged a $260 million refinancing loan for RXR's 75 Rockefeller Plaza, a prominent mixed-use office and retail tower in Midtown Manhattan. The financing, contributed by Bank of America and Carlyle, highlights the building's strong fundamentals, including A+ sponsorship, investment-grade tenancy, and significant capital improvements. The property boasts a prime location near Rockefeller Plaza, comprehensive amenities, and flexible office spaces.

title: Card companies urged to code gun sellers
summary: Public officials and pension funds are increasing pressure on Visa, Mastercard, and American Express to create a unique merchant category code (MCC) for gun sellers. Proponents argue this code would help financial institutions track suspicious gun purchases, citing past incidents where firearms used in mass shootings were bought with credit cards. The International Standards Organization (ISO), which sets MCC standards, is considering the matter, while card companies remain largely uncommitted to publicly supporting the initiative.

title: The Walt Disney Company Hosting Q&A at the 2022 Bank of America Securities Media, Communications & Entertainment Conference
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced that Christine McCarthy, Senior Executive Vice President and CFO, and Josh D’Amaro, Chairman of Disney Parks, Experiences and Products, will participate in a Q&A session. This event will take place at the 2022 Bank of America Securities Media, Communications & Entertainment Conference on September 7th, 2022, at 1:30 p.m. ET/10:30 a.m. PT. A live stream and archive of the session will be available online.

title: Bank of America draws mixed reviews for zero-down-payment mortgages aimed at boosting Black and Hispanic home ownership
summary: Bank of America's new zero-down-payment mortgage program, the Community Affordable Loan Solution, is receiving mixed reactions, particularly on social media. The initiative aims to increase homeownership among Black and Hispanic families but has drawn comparisons to subprime loans that contributed to the 2008 financial crisis. This move comes as bank regulators encourage greater lending equality.

title: Citigroup's Russia exit removes one obstacle for CEO, but challenges remain
summary: Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser's decision to exit Russia and divest consumer businesses in 13 other countries is a step towards paring down risky assets and focusing on core operations. While analysts and investors view her strategy favorably, Fraser still faces significant challenges, including overhauling risk management systems mandated by U.S. regulators and a potentially deteriorating economic environment. The bank's stock remains undervalued compared to its peers, indicating a long road ahead for the turnaround effort.

title: Citigroup's Russia exit removes one obstacle for CEO, but challenges remain
summary: Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser is working to simplify the bank's structure and focus on core businesses by exiting Russia and paring down consumer operations in other countries. While investors and analysts acknowledge the positive direction, Fraser faces significant challenges, including overhauling risk management systems mandated by U.S. regulators and a potentially deteriorating economic environment. Despite these hurdles, some investors are showing patience with her long-term strategy for a "simpler, sounder bank."

title: Bank of America is targeting women and minority businesses with down payments on loans in select markets
summary: Bank of America is now offering grants of up to $25,000 to assist small businesses with down payments on commercial real-estate loans. This initiative targets women and minority businesses in specific markets, including Atlanta, Chicago, Charlotte, Dallas, and Los Angeles, which are defined as opportunity zones lacking access to capital. This program is part of a broader effort by financial firms and regulators to address unequal lending practices.

title: Catching peak bond yields
summary: This article discusses the current state of bond markets, particularly highlighting the risks of spread widening due to growth risk, central bank policies, and high debt levels. It suggests that locking in yields now is preferable to waiting for peak spreads, especially given the likelihood of continued volatility and potential for further deterioration in credit quality for high-yield issuers. The author recommends selective positioning in more defensive sectors and focusing on higher-rated investment-grade bonds.

title: ICICI Bank to raise 10,000 crore to maintain CRR and SLR
summary: ICICI Bank plans to raise up to Rs 10,000 crore through infrastructure bonds to fund project financing and affordable housing. These long-term bonds offer the advantage of exemption from statutory liquidity requirements (SLR) and cash reserve ratios (CRR), helping to mitigate asset-liability management issues. This move aligns with increased government capital spending and a significant rise in bank lending to the infrastructure sector in India.

title: Citigroup to Offer New Government-Sponsored Programs for Borrowers With Credit Challenges
summary: Citigroup announced the launch of two government-sponsored pilot programs under Project REACh to expand credit access for underserved communities. These programs, starting next year, will offer credit cards to individuals without traditional credit scores and make it easier for minority, women, and veteran-owned small businesses to obtain credit. This initiative aims to lower barriers to financial services, following similar efforts by other banks like JPMorgan Chase and Wells Fargo, and comes alongside Bank of America's zero down payment mortgage program for select communities.

title: BOK Financial (BOKF) to Remove Overdraft & NSF fees by '22
summary: BOK Financial (BOKF) announced plans to eliminate all non-sufficient fund (NSF) fees and reduce overdraft fees by the end of 2022, following a trend among U.S. banks. This move aims to enhance customer financial well-being by reducing fees and increasing overdraft cushions, aligning with regulatory pressure to safeguard consumers. Other major banks like Bank of America and Citigroup have also made similar changes to their overdraft policies.

title: Huntington Bancshares Inc. stock underperforms Tuesday when compared to competitors
summary: Shares of Huntington Bancshares Inc. (HBAN) fell 1.13% on Tuesday, underperforming the broader market and its competitors. The stock closed at $13.17, marking its third consecutive day of losses and putting it $4.62 below its 52-week high. Trading volume was higher than its 50-day average.

title: Philippine text scams: Customer names 'harvested', SMS with receivers' names trigger probes
summary: Philippine authorities are investigating a surge in text scams that use recipients' personal information, potentially sourced from various establishments or electronic wallets. This rise highlights the issues of an unregistered SIM card system, contributing to significant financial losses from online fraud. Efforts are underway to pass a SIM Card Registration Act and a financial consumer protection act to combat these crimes and boost consumer confidence in digital financial services.

title: Deutsche Bank’s Chadha Sees 25% US Stock Slump if Recession Hits
summary: Deutsche Bank strategists, led by Binky Chadha, predict a potential 25% decline in US stocks if the economy enters a recession. They cite declining company profits, high stock valuations, and looming recession risks as major challenges for the equity market. Despite these risks, investor positioning in equities is currently low.

title: Former Matrix partners mend rift, but secrets and tension between FPL, Southern Co. linger | Nate Monroe
summary: A legal battle between former partners of Matrix LLC, a political consulting firm, has ended in a settlement, but revelations about the firm's work for major power companies like Florida Power & Light (FPL) and Southern Co. have exposed ongoing tensions. The article reveals how Matrix operatives engaged in surveillance and manipulation of elections and public policy on behalf of FPL, while also attempting to undermine Southern Co.'s interests. The settlement, while quieting some immediate legal noise, highlights a bitter rivalry between FPL and Southern Co. over regional energy projects and market influence.

title: Tages Helios II cashes in a 1.1 bn euro jumbo green loan. Meanwhile the new Helios Net Zero Fund is on the market and Tages’ private debt fund is ready for investing – BeBeez International
summary: Tages Helios II has secured a €1.1 billion green loan, the first for Tages, provided by a consortium of eight banks for financing renewable energy projects. Concurrently, Tages Capital SGR is launching a new fund, Tages Helios Net Zero, with a €750 million fundraising target to develop greenfield renewable energy projects. Additionally, Tages' private debt fund, established a year ago, is set to become operational, expanding the firm's investment vehicles.

title: Bank of America enlists thousands of employees for wealth lending group
summary: Bank of America has formed a new 3,500-person wealth management banking and lending group within its global wealth and investment management division to enhance lending services for its affluent clients. Led by April Schneider, the group will underwrite various loans for wealthy clients, working in conjunction with financial advisers and private bankers who focus on investments and estate planning. This initiative aims to provide a more integrated "concierge service" for high-net-worth individuals.

title: Women in Banking 2022
summary: Arkansas Money & Politics (AMP) has recognized influential women in the state's banking and finance industry for 2022, highlighting their perseverance, hard work, and expertise in a male-dominated field. The list features executives nominated by readers, showcasing their significant contributions and leadership roles across various financial institutions in Arkansas. Profiles include their career paths, achievements, and community involvement.

title: TD Bank and DailyPay team for real-time earned wage access
summary: TD Bank has partnered with DailyPay, an on-demand pay solution provider, to offer its clients' employees real-time access to earned wages before their scheduled payday. This partnership aims to ease financial burdens caused by inflation and unforeseen expenses, allowing workers to access their earnings when needed. DailyPay's solution integrates with existing payroll systems, converting time worked into net earnings accessible through a bank account or card.

title: Comerica Bank Is Building a New Business and Innovation Hub at The Star in Frisco
summary: Comerica Bank is constructing a new Business & Innovation Hub at The Star in Frisco, slated to open in late 2023 or early 2024, which will house approximately 300 employees and feature an innovation center and "tech genius bar." This expansion aims to enhance cross-functional collaboration and meet evolving needs, complementing its downtown Dallas headquarters. The facility will be located in a new Class A+ tower at 17 Cowboys Way and is designed by HKS Architects.

title: Still holding up a decade later? An insight into the effectiveness of the Etridge Protocol
summary: This article assesses the effectiveness of the Etridge Protocol, established in the case of Royal Bank of Scotland plc v Etridge (No 2) [2001] UKHL 44, which revitalized the law of undue influence and clarified the duties of banks and solicitors. The author, Oliwia Maliszewska, discusses the pros and cons of the protocol, particularly its low threshold for notice which aids in swiftly identifying undue influence and protects vulnerable parties. However, she also highlights disadvantages such as the lowering of standards in post-Etridge case law by judicial creativity and the challenges posed during the Covid-19 pandemic for in-person consultations, underscoring the need for reform.

title: Brandon Brouillard, of Worcester, sentenced for trying to buy $83,000 sports car using stolen identities
summary: Brandon Brouillard of Worcester was sentenced to nearly four years in prison for bank fraud and aggravated identity theft. He used stolen identities to open bank accounts, attempt a car loan, and successfully purchase an $83,000 Chevrolet Camaro with a fraudulent check. His scheme involved compromising an Arizona resident's bank accounts, totaling approximately $500,000 in fraudulent purchases, and he was also linked to another man's attempt to buy a $56,000 Jeep using a counterfeit check.

title: Worcester man sentenced to nearly 4 years in $83,000 car scam
summary: A Worcester man, Brandon Brouillard, 29, has been sentenced to nearly four years in federal prison for bank fraud and aggravated identity theft. He used victims' identities to open bank accounts and attempted to buy an $83,000 car. Brouillard's criminal activities involved wiring large sums of money and making significant purchases using compromised accounts.

title: TD Bank Dethrones Wells Fargo as Philly Region's Largest Retail Bank
summary: TD Bank has surpassed Wells Fargo as the largest deposit-taker in the Philadelphia region, according to annual FDIC data. TD Bank now holds a 16.7% market share with $35.4 billion in local deposits, up from the previous year. Wells Fargo had long held the top position due to historical acquisitions.

title: Intellicheck Appoints Dondi Black and Greg Braca to Board of Directors
summary: Intellicheck, Inc. (Nasdaq: IDN) has appointed Dondi Black and Greg Braca to its board of directors, effective September 14, 2022. Both appointees bring over 30 years of extensive experience in the fintech and banking industries, which Intellicheck believes will be valuable for the company's strategic growth and adoption of its technology solutions. Black is currently Senior Vice President, Chief Product Officer at TSYS, and Braca is the former CEO and president of TD Bank.

title: BNY Mellon, Warburg Group, Deutsche Bank to pay $60 mln in 'cum-ex' case
summary: BNY Mellon, Warburg Group, and Deutsche Bank will pay 60 million euros ($59.85 million) to German tax authorities related to the "cum-ex" tax scandal. This payment covers tax liabilities for the BC German Equity Special Fund from 2009. The scandal, which involves multiple banks and has cost taxpayers billions, remains under investigation.

title: The Global Real-Time Rail Ecosystem (Part I)
summary: This article, Part I of a series, explores the global landscape of real-time payment rail modernization. It highlights Canada's modernization journey and reviews faster payment systems in the UK, Australia, Hong Kong, and the United States, detailing the innovative services built upon these infrastructures. The article emphasizes that while the introduction of Real-Time Rails (RTR) is a significant step, it is merely the beginning of a broader modernization process with extensive economic implications.

title: Major U.S. banks threaten to leave Mark Carney's climate alliance - FT
summary: Major U.S. Wall Street banks, including Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, and Bank of America, are reportedly threatening to leave Mark Carney's Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ). The banks fear legal risks associated with the alliance's strict decarbonisation commitments and potential lawsuits, especially concerning upcoming U.S. SEC climate-risk disclosure rules. They also expressed concerns about a lack of government action on climate change and disproportionate membership from top carbon-emitting countries.

title: Bank CEOs push back on capital requirements in Capitol Hill hearings
summary: CEOs from seven of the largest U.S. banks, including JPMorgan Chase, Citigroup, Wells Fargo, and Bank of America, engaged in two days of public hearings on Capitol Hill. They addressed various topics such as inflation, racial equality in home lending, regulatory burdens, and their perspectives on an impending economic slowdown. A key point of discussion was their pushback on capital requirements.

title: Bank executives warn lawmakers of lending risk among nonbanks
summary: Bank executives testified before the House Financial Services Committee, warning lawmakers that less stringent regulations on nonbank lenders are shifting significant lending, particularly in mortgages, outside the traditional banking system. They argued that current capital requirements put banks at a disadvantage and could pose risks during an economic downturn, as nonbanks may not have sufficient capital to cover losses. Despite their concerns, some lawmakers expressed skepticism, noting that banks have remained highly profitable despite post-2008 financial crisis regulations.

title: US bank CEOs say they would stop working with China in event of Taiwan attack
summary: Top US bank CEOs stated they would cease operations in China if the US government instructed them to do so following a Taiwan invasion by mainland forces. This commitment was made during a House of Representatives Financial Services Committee hearing where lawmakers questioned their institutions' business ties to both Russia and China. The CEOs of JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Bank of America, Citigroup, US Bancorp, PNC Financial, and Truist were present.

title: KBRA Rates Non-QM Offering From Onslow Bay Financial – NMP
summary: KBRA has assigned preliminary ratings to six classes of mortgage pass-through notes from the OBX 2022-NQM8 Trust, a $397.5 million non-prime residential mortgage-backed securities (RMBS) transaction sponsored by Onslow Bay Financial LLC. The transaction involves 765 residential mortgages, with a significant concentration (91.3%) using alternative income documentation and many classified as non-qualified mortgages or exempt from ATR/QM rules. AmWest Funding Corp. was the largest originator, contributing 47.3% of the loans, which KBRA considers non-prime due to borrower credit history and alternative income documentation.

title: Lawmakers Grill the Big Banks on Zelle, Interest Rates, and Overdraft Fees
summary: Lawmakers recently questioned the CEOs of seven major banks during annual oversight hearings. Key topics included the economy's state, diversity efforts, electronic payment scams like those involving Zelle, and issues related to interest rates and overdraft fees.

title: Bank CEOs questioned on consumer protections, social issues
summary: Bank CEOs faced a second day of questioning on Capitol Hill regarding consumer protections and social issues. Senate Democrats pressed for more consumer safeguards amidst high inflation, while Republicans questioned banks' involvement in social issues. Topics included overdraft fees, Zelle fraud, and banks' stances on abortion costs, gun rights, and environmental policies.

title: Credit Suisse Mulls Sale of Latin American Wealth Business, Excluding Brazil
summary: Credit Suisse Group AG is considering selling its Latin American wealth management operations, excluding Brazil, as part of a broader restructuring effort. The bank is reportedly in discussions with potential buyers, including Banco Santander SA and Intesa Sanpaolo SpA, to offload this segment which includes operations in countries like Mexico and Colombia. This move aligns with Credit Suisse's strategy to focus on its top 20 markets and exit non-core businesses to improve profitability.

title: Dallas-based Beneficient going public via SPAC in deal valuing it at $3.5 billion
summary: Dallas-based Beneficient Company Group is going public via a SPAC merger with Avalon Acquisition Inc., in a deal valuing Beneficient at $3.5 billion. The company targets the $12 trillion alternative asset market, focusing on providing liquidity and transparency for mid- to high-net-worth investors and small- to medium-sized institutions. This merger is expected to provide Beneficient with approximately $200 million in gross proceeds to fuel its growth.

title: Banking Scams: American Express, Regions, NFCU, ICCU, and Bank of America
summary: This article details recent banking scams targeting customers of American Express, Regions Bank, Navy Federal Credit Union (NFCU), Idaho Central Credit Union (ICCU), and Bank of America. It highlights various phishing emails and SMS (smishing) messages designed to trick users into revealing their login credentials or personal information. The article also provides advice on how to protect oneself from these scams, including checking URLs and using security tools like Trend Micro ScamCheck.

title: Truist, Bank of America post highest deposits in metro Orlando
summary: Truist and Bank of America have secured the top two positions for deposits in the metro Orlando area. The article notes that multiple banks increased their deposits in the market over the last year.

title: Questioning CEOs of America’s Largest Banks on Efforts to Block Gun Purchases, Legal Commerce
summary: Senator Kevin Cramer questioned the CEOs of major U.S. banks during a Senate Banking Committee hearing regarding their commitment to processing transactions for legal goods and services, particularly in light of pressures to block gun purchases. Senator Cramer specifically challenged the banks on a new Merchant Category Code for gun and ammunition stores and sought assurances that legal transactions would not be discriminated against. All seven bank CEOs present committed to processing transactions for legal goods and services, including guns and ammunition.

title: Wall Street firms hit with $2 billion in fines in WhatsApp probe
summary: U.S. regulators have levied over $2 billion in fines against more than a dozen Wall Street firms, including Citigroup, Bank of America, and Goldman Sachs, for failing to monitor employees' communications on unauthorized messaging apps like WhatsApp. These penalties, which include $1.1 billion from the SEC and $710 million from the CFTC, represent the largest-ever fines against U.S. banks for record-keeping lapses. The probes highlighted the widespread use of unapproved channels for work-related communication, even by senior supervisors, which undermined regulatory scrutiny.

title: PNC buys restaurant point-of-sale firm Linga
summary: PNC Financial Services Group has acquired Linga, a Naples, Florida-based point-of-sale (POS) and payments solutions firm specializing in the restaurant industry. This acquisition will expand PNC's corporate payments capabilities and enhance its treasury management platform by integrating Linga's cloud-based operating system, online ordering, and QR code-based menu features. Linga will continue to operate with its existing management team and founder, Onur Haytac, reflecting a broader trend of banks investing in fintech to meet evolving consumer demands for contactless payments.

title: As interest rates rise, is cash king again?
summary: With rising interest rates, "cash is king" again for short-term savings, but experts advise caution. While savings rates are improving, inflation still outpaces them, leading to a loss in real value. For long-term investors, the stock market is still expected to outperform cash, and the US dollar is currently considered the only safe haven asset offering both value and higher yields.

title: Bank of America Study Finds 84% of Employers Now Say Offering Financial Wellness Tools Helps Increase Employee Retention
summary: A Bank of America study reveals that 84% of employers believe financial wellness tools boost employee retention, with 97% feeling responsible for employee financial well-being. The report highlights that 62% of employees are stressed about finances due to inflation, leading to a drop in financial wellness feelings to a five-year low. Employers are expanding wellness programs, including investment advice and D&I initiatives, to address these concerns and improve employee satisfaction and productivity.

title: Global Retirement Partners LLC Has $206,000 Position in Fidelity Stocks For Inflation ETF (BATS:FCPI)
summary: Global Retirement Partners LLC increased its stake in Fidelity Stocks For Inflation ETF (BATS:FCPI) by 9.9% during the second quarter, bringing its total holdings to $206,000. Several other institutional investors also acquired new positions in FCPI during the same period. The ETF's stock opened at $28.28, with moving averages indicating recent price movements.
